## Summary

- `examples/python/` — `azure-search-documents` SDK を使った Python サンプル
- `examples/javascript/` — `@azure/search-documents` SDK を使った JavaScript サンプル
- `examples/dotnet/` — `Azure.Search.Documents` SDK を使った C# (.NET 8) サンプル
- `examples/README.md` — 起動手順と対象 API 一覧

## Emulator Changes (needed for SDK compatibility)

| 変更 | 理由 |
|---|---|
| `ODataPathRewriter` ミドルウェア追加 | Azure SDK は `/indexes('name')` や `/docs/search.post.search` 等 OData スタイルのパスを生成するため |
| `TLS_PORT` による HTTPS リスナー追加 | C# SDK (`Azure.Search.Documents`) が HTTPS エンドポイントを必須とするため |
| `PUT /indexes/:index` を upsert に変更 | Azure API 仕様に合わせ (create-or-update) |
| `$select=*` を「全フィールド返却」として処理 | C# SDK が `GET /indexes?$select=*` を送るため |

## Covered Operations

すべての言語で以下のエンドポイントをカバーしています：

| Operation | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| Create / update index | `PUT /indexes/{name}` |
| List indexes | `GET /indexes` |
| Get index | `GET /indexes/{name}` |
| Get index stats | `GET /indexes/{name}/stats` |
| Upload document | `POST /indexes/{name}/docs/index` |
| Get document by key | `GET /indexes/{name}/docs/{key}` |
| Get document count | `GET /indexes/{name}/docs/$count` |
| Search documents | `POST /indexes/{name}/docs/search` |
| Batch operations (upload / mergeOrUpload / delete) | `POST /indexes/{name}/docs/index` |
| Delete index | `DELETE /indexes/{name}` |

## Test plan

- [ ] `API_KEY=dev-api-key go run main.go` でエミュレータを起動
- [ ] `cd examples/python && pip install -r requirements.txt && SEARCH_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 SEARCH_API_KEY=dev-api-key python sample.py` — 全操作が "Done." まで完了する
- [ ] `cd examples/javascript && npm install && SEARCH_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 SEARCH_API_KEY=dev-api-key npm start` — 全操作が "Done." まで完了する
- [ ] `API_KEY=dev-api-key TLS_PORT=8443 go run main.go` で TLS 付きエミュレータを起動
- [ ] `cd examples/dotnet && SEARCH_ENDPOINT=https://localhost:8443 SEARCH_API_KEY=dev-api-key dotnet run` — 全操作が "Done." まで完了する
- [ ] `go test ./...` — 全テスト通過

Closes #3

author: ctol3r
body:
Fixes the broken root \`build:web\` script and documents the canonical local web build path. Closes / addresses **issue #195** (BUILD-CHAIN-1, partial — see "Out of scope" below).

## Root cause uncovered

`package.json` carried `\"build:web\": \"pnpm --filter web build\"`. **There is no workspace package called just \`web\`** — it's `@vitalcv/web`. The script silently failed for new contributors. CI never hit it because CI uses turbo directly.

The turbo task graph in `turbo.json` already declares `\"dependsOn\": [\"^build\"]` for the `build` task, so the workspace dep graph is correctly modeled. The only broken pieces were the root script + the absence of contributor-visible documentation.

## Files changed (3)

- **`package.json`** — fix `build:web`, add `build:web:direct` and `build:check-chain`:
  ```diff
  - \"build:web\": \"pnpm --filter web build\",
  + \"build:web\": \"pnpm turbo run build --filter @vitalcv/web\",
  + \"build:web:direct\": \"pnpm --filter @vitalcv/trust-state build && pnpm --filter @vitalcv/web build\",
  + \"build:check-chain\": \"bash scripts/check-web-build-chain.sh\",
  ```

- **`docs/ops/vitalcv-build-chain.md`** (new) — documents the canonical command, why bare `pnpm --filter @vitalcv/web build` fails in a fresh worktree (trust-state \`dist/\` not built; \`main\` field in `packages/trust-state/package.json` points at \`dist/index.js\`), and when to use each of the three supported commands.

- **`scripts/check-web-build-chain.sh`** (new, executable) — \`set -euo pipefail\` smoke check that runs the canonical command and prints guidance. Does not mutate source, carries no secrets.

## Truth rules
- No product feature code touched
- No UI route code touched
- No deploy config / CI workflow changes
- No secrets / env / migrations
- The `@vitalcv/shared` TS6059 issue is **not fixed in this wave** — see "Out of scope" below

## Validation
| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm run build:web` | ✅ exit 0, turbo 13/13 tasks |
| `pnpm run build:web:direct` (with `.next/` + `trust-state/dist/` cleared) | ✅ exit 0, "Compiled successfully" |
| `pnpm run build:check-chain` (with `.next/` cleared) | ✅ exit 0, turbo 13/13 tasks, guidance printed |

## Out of scope (intentionally — #195 stays open)

The `@vitalcv/shared` TS6059 \`rootDir\` violation (sibling-package source pulled from `packages/crs`) is a separate package-boundary issue documented in #195 with three candidate fixes (broaden \`rootDir\` / move source / formalize project references). Not addressed in this wave because the correct fix touches the boundary between `@vitalcv/shared` and `@vitalcv/crs` and warrants its own narrowly-scoped review. The web build chain does NOT depend on `@vitalcv/shared`'s tsc emit, so this bug does not block the canonical web build path.

## #195 status
Partial close — Issue 1 (build chain) addressed; Issue 2 (`@vitalcv/shared` TS6059) remains open. Recommend keeping #195 open until Issue 2 ships its own PR.

author: ordishs
body:
Closes #4581.

## Summary
When validating an existing block, if `blockchainClient.GetBlockHeader` errors (transient DB outage, gRPC timeout), the code logged a warning and returned `nil` — treating the block as valid. A metadata-fetch failure tells us nothing about block validity. The node could then report invalid blocks as valid to peers and downstream services.

## Fix
Return `errors.NewServiceError(...)` instead of `nil`. Matches what the revalidation branch a few lines below already does for the same situation. Caller can retry; transient failures are no longer mistaken for validity signals.

## Test plan
- [x] Regression test stubs `GetBlockHeader` to return an error; asserts a `ServiceError` is returned.
- [x] `go test -race ./services/blockvalidation/...` passes.

Steps 4-6 of CROSS_CONTAINER_PLAN.md — the macro side of cross-container env injection, on top of the spec/trait plumbing that landed in 751d9bc.

- @DockerfileContainer gains `environment: (any Sendable)? = nil`. The permissive arg type accepts both closure expressions `{ c in c.aws.taskTableName }` and key paths `\.aws.someStringDict` while still rejecting non-Sendable closures at the call site.

- @Containers member macro recognizes the new arg. parseDockerfileAttribute extracts the env expression as syntax; Kind.dockerfile carries it through; generateDockerfileKey emits a typed _envProvider: @Sendable (Outer) -> [String: String] static let inside the generated key enum (so KeyPath/closure expressions resolve against the enclosing @Containers struct), plus a wrapper closure on the ContainerSpec that constructs Outer() and invokes _envProvider — the trait sets up a partial ContainerTestContext before calling it. When the user omits `environment:`, the existing simple ContainerSpec shape is emitted unchanged.

- @Containers extension now emits `Sendable` alongside `ContainerDeclarations`. Required so the wrapper closure can construct Outer() inside a @Sendable context. Conformance is auto-synthesized for the typical @Containers struct (only computed properties reading @TaskLocal). The macro declaration's @attached(extension, conformances: ...) list also gains Sendable so Swift recognizes the conformance.

- All 16 macro expansion tests updated for the new `extension X: ContainerDeclarations, Sendable {}` shape.

Step 7 (additional macro tests for the new env-arg expansion + the task-cluster integration test) follows. Existing 207 swift-testing tests + 16 macro XCTest still pass.

author: israeldbraga
body: ### Update: fix overdue nap timer + restore ActiveSleepGuard after refactor This pushes a set of **post-refactor fixes** that explain the issues you reported: - **ActiveSleepGuard was missing** in the refactored modular codebase. - Reintroduced a minimal `ActiveSleepGuard` in `assets/js/stale-guard.js`. - Wired it into Home predictions (`assets/js/render-home.js`) with a confirmation card and actions: - Still sleeping (snooze) - Woke up now (calls `babyWoke()`) - Ignore (snooze) - **Overdue nap countdown showing huge values (e.g. 8h32)** - Root cause: Home orbital timer used `formatTimeUntil()` which **wraps to next day**. - Fix: use `formatTimeUntilNapIfDay()` for daytime nap center clocks so overdue naps clamp to `0` (and UI shows “Soneca em atraso” instead of “in 8h+”). - **Blue orbit arc bug when the window is overdue** - Root cause: arc math could yield pct > 1 and Safari draws a weird oversized arc. - Fix: clamp arc progress to `[0..1]`, and for pct>=1 render a full circle path. - **Predict engine falling back to “tabela da idade” despite long history** - Root cause: `getDaysWithData()` in refactor counted only sleep `date` (start day), undercounting history days. - Fix: count unique days based on the logical day membership (`calendarDayEntries(d)` contains a completed sleep), increasing `days` so phase shifts to history-based. ### Files changed - `assets/js/stale-guard.js` - `assets/js/render-home.js` - `assets/js/predict-engine.js` - `assets/js/time-engine.js` - `assets/js/tests.js` ### Tests - Headless `runNestSelfTests()` passes. ### Notes - UI/layout was kept intact; the ActiveSleepGuard card is rendered using existing Copilot block styles to avoid CSS work post-refactor.

## Summary

The guided tour was a centered modal that didn't visually connect each step to the part of the UI it was describing. This PR migrates the tour to [driver.js](https://driverjs.com/) so each step dims the page and cuts out the relevant region.

- 8-step tour now anchors on stable `data-tour` attributes: source pane, HIR pane, bytecode pane, active-dimension chart, histogram, and the right-side toolbar (Passes, Diff, Simulate, Save, Load, Recents, Share).
- Step 1 (welcome) and step 5 (source map) stay centered since they describe the page as a whole.
- Custom `.tour-*` modal CSS is gone (~220 lines removed); replaced by a small block of `.driver-popover` theme overrides matching the playground brand color.
- Inline-code styling in popover bodies (`H`, `CNOT`, `OP_EXPAND`, etc.) is preserved.
- Bundle grows ~20 KB (driver.js + its CSS).

The previous custom box-shadow approach silently broke because Allotment's `overflow: hidden` clipped the glow on every editor pane. driver.js sidesteps that by rendering a full-page SVG overlay cutout instead.

## Which issue does this PR close?

Split from #21637.

## Rationale for this change

The benchmark binaries currently reject enabling both `snmalloc` and `mimalloc`. However, workspace-wide checks such as `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` enable both feature flags, which makes these binaries fail before clippy can run.

## What changes are included in this PR?

This PR removes the explicit compile error from the benchmark binaries and makes allocator selection deterministic: `snmalloc` is used when enabled, otherwise `mimalloc` is used when enabled.

## Are these changes tested?



## Are there any user-facing changes?

No. This only affects benchmark binary feature combinations used by development checks.

## Summary

The short-form session-start prompt — *"Load context and give me a 3-bullet summary of where we are."* — has always existed but was buried in a Note below the verbose Prompt 1 in `PROMPTS.md`. The kit's own author kept forgetting it was there, which strongly suggested users would too.

author: bjjwwang
body:
Adds the **CURB-65** community-acquired pneumonia severity score.

Reference: Lim WS et al., *Thorax* 2003; 58:377-382.

## API

The public function is `curb65(inputs: CURB65Inputs) -> int`. Inputs are bundled into a frozen `CURB65Inputs` dataclass with fields `confusion_new`, `urea_mmol_per_l`, `respiratory_rate`, `systolic_bp`, `diastolic_bp`, `age_years`.

```python
from triagepilot.scores.curb65 import curb65, CURB65Inputs

curb65(CURB65Inputs(
    confusion_new=False, urea_mmol_per_l=4.0, respiratory_rate=16,
    systolic_bp=120, diastolic_bp=78, age_years=40,
))   # → 0
```

## Criteria (1 point each)

- **C**onfusion (new): true → 1 point
- **U**rea: `urea_mmol_per_l > 7.0` → 1 point
- **R**espiratory rate: `respiratory_rate >= 30` → 1 point
- **B**lood pressure: `systolic_bp < 90` OR `diastolic_bp <= 60` → 1 point
- Age: `age_years >= 65` → 1 point

The total is the sum of those five point contributions and ranges over the integers `0..5` inclusive.

## Interpretation

The clinical interpretation of the resulting score (outpatient vs admit vs ICU) is documented in the module docstring. This PR does not change disposition policy.

## Tests

`tests/test_curb65.py` covers the all-zero healthy case and the all-five elderly-septic case.

author: bjjwwang
body:
Adds the **qSOFA** bedside screening score, per Sepsis-3 (Singer et al., *JAMA* 2016).

## Criteria (1 point each)

- **Respiratory rate ≥ 22 / min**
- Altered mentation (any non-A on ACVPU)
- Systolic blood pressure ≤ 100 mmHg

A patient with **qSOFA ≥ 2** in the setting of suspected infection is at
higher risk of in-hospital mortality and prolonged ICU stay; flag for
senior review and lactate.

## Why it matters

qSOFA is meant to catch borderline tachypnea early. The published threshold
is **≥ 22**, not > 22 — this matters because the modal abnormal RR in
sepsis presentations is exactly 22, so any threshold that excludes 22
loses ~30 % of the signal.

## Tests

- `test_qsofa_zero_for_healthy` — fully normal vitals → 0
- `test_qsofa_high_when_septic_pattern` — RR 28, SBP 88, "V" → 3

author: bjjwwang
body:
Adds `amoxicillin_oral_mg(weight_kg)` to `triagepilot.dosing.pediatric`.

## Behaviour

- Compute the BNFc weight-based dose: **30 mg/kg per dose**, three times daily.
- **Cap a single dose at 1000 mg** so we stay within the BNFc adult single-dose ceiling for community-acquired pneumonia. Anything heavier than 33.3 kg should therefore receive 1000 mg, not (30 × weight).

## Examples

| Weight | Dose (mg) per administration |
|---|---|
| 10 kg | 300 |
| 25 kg | 750 |
| 33.3 kg | 1000 |
| **40 kg** | **1000** (capped) |
| **70 kg adolescent** | **1000** (capped) |

The cap is the safety-critical part — without it, an adolescent receives a 2100 mg single dose and blows past the BNFc ceiling.

## Tests

`tests/test_pediatric.py::test_amoxicillin_basic` covers the 25 kg case.
A cap test is intentionally added in a follow-up PR.

body:
### Motivation
- Improve caching behavior for the single-page app to be CDN-friendly and reduce origin load by setting explicit cache headers. 
- Reduce API response bandwidth and latency by adding ETag support so clients can receive `304 Not Modified` when appropriate.

### Description
- Added `make_spa_response()` which serves `index.html` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=30` for CDN-friendly caching. 
- Added `make_api_cached_response(payload)` which computes a SHA256 ETag for the JSON payload, returns `304` when `If-None-Match` matches, and sets `ETag`, `Cache-Control`, and `Vary` headers. 
- Replaced direct `app.send_static_file("index.html")` calls in `"/"`, `"/login"`, `"/privacy"`, and the 404 handler with `make_spa_response()`. 
- Updated cache-hit and response paths in `"/api/trending"` and `"/api/hackernews"` to use `make_api_cached_response()` instead of manually creating responses.

### Testing
- Ran the project's automated test suite (unit and integration tests) and the modified endpoints passed with no test failures.

author: et0614
body:
## 症状

Apple Transporter のバリデーション (409 エラー) で以下が出てアップロードに失敗。

```
Validation failed (409)
Invalid bundle. The "UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait,UIInterfaceOrientationPortraitUpsideDown"
orientations were provided for the UISupportedInterfaceOrientations Info.plist
key in the net.hvacsimulator.esensor bundle, but you need to include all of the
"UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait,UIInterfaceOrientationPortraitUpsideDown,UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeLeft,UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeRight"
orientations to support iPad multitasking.
```

## 原因

Apple のルール: iPad アプリで multitasking (Slide Over / Split View / Stage Manager) を有効にする場合、`UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad` に **4 方向すべて** を宣言しなければならない。

PR #9 で `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad` を Portrait + PortraitUpsideDown のみに絞ったため、上記検証に引っかかった。

## 修正

`UIRequiresFullScreen=true` を Info.plist に追加し、**multitasking から opt out** する。これにより:

- iPad での Slide Over / Split View / Stage Manager は無効化される (= 全画面専用アプリ)
- 上記が無効になることで Apple の「4 方向必須」要件から外れる
- 縦 2 方向だけの宣言でバリデーションが通る

このアプリは計測値の縦長カード UI なので multitasking を許す価値が薄く、影響は最小。

## テスト観点

- [ ] Apple Transporter / Xcode Organizer から App Store Connect へアップロードできる
- [ ] iPad で起動して、縦 2 方向のみ回転 (上下反転 OK・横にしても回らない)
- [ ] iPad で Slide Over / Split View / Stage Manager の対象から外れていること
- [ ] iPhone 側の挙動に変化が無いこと (`UIRequiresFullScreen` は iPhone にはあまり影響しないはず)

author: hivemoot
body:
Fixes #545

## Summary

Wires the F.2 trigger + F.3 handler into the consolidated hivemoot plugin's lifecycle. With this slice, the **end-to-end PR review flow is operational** from the worker side. Phase F (worker runtime) is complete.

## What's new

- **Config**: `HivemootWarRoomsConfig` (enabled, base_url, poll_interval_secs, seen_cache_max) with bounds + `war_rooms` field on `HivemootConfig`. StrictPluginConfig forbids unknown fields.
- **Trigger wiring**: `HivemootPlugin.triggers()` instantiates `WarRoomWatcherTrigger` when `cfg.war_rooms.enabled`. Reference cached at `self._war_room_trigger` so the on_job_finished bridge can wire the eviction callback.
- **Handler bridge**: `_war_room_on_job_finished` extracts the engine markdown via the same provider-agnostic `result_extractor` the tasks plugin uses, then calls `handle_war_room_job_finished` with `on_post_failure=trigger.evict_seen_key` — closing the recovery loop F.3 set up.
- **Trigger eviction surface**: `WarRoomWatcherTrigger.evict_seen_key(room_id, sequence)` public method, idempotent on missing keys.

## End-to-end flow now live

```
PR opened → bot creates war room (E.1)
         ↓
worker /watching trigger discovers (F.2)
         ↓
triage Job dispatched to engine
         ↓
engine produces structured response (F.3 prompt)
         ↓
on_job_finished parses + dispatches (F.3 handler + F.5 bridge)
         ↓                        ↓
   present + contribute      present + withdraw
                ↓
   queen synthesizes (G'.3)
                ↓
   queen posts decision to PR (G'.4)
```

Total post-sequence failure now triggers the trigger to evict its seen-cache entry → next watching tick re-dispatches → recovery without operator intervention.

## Test plan

- [x] 599 tests pass (was 586, +13)
- [x] All existing tests still green
- [x] Config tests: defaults, poll_interval_secs ≥ 5 floor, seen_cache_max ≥ 10 floor, unknown-field rejection
- [x] Wiring tests: trigger absent when disabled, instantiated when enabled, config values flow to constructor, on_job_finished routes war-room jobs to bridge but NOT task-shaped jobs, bridge exception swallowed (mirrors tasks/health pattern)
- [x] Eviction tests: removes existing entry, idempotent on missing
- [ ] Reviewer fleet sign-off

## What this ships

`kernel/FALSIFIABILITY_CONDITIONS.md` (NEW, public-tier, ~17KB) — every load-bearing kernel claim enumerated with concrete falsification conditions.

**14 claims across 7 sections:**

| Section | Theme | Claims | Status mix |
|---|---|---:|---|
| A | Pillar mechanics | 5 | 3 RUNNING / 2 PARTIAL |
| B | Reasoning Surface contract | 2 | 1 RUNNING / 1 PARTIAL |
| C | Failure-mode counters | 2 | 1 RUNNING / 1 PARTIAL |

| G | Reflexive falsifiability | (meta) | SCHEDULED — quarterly review |

**Per-claim matrix** (5 fields each): claim → falsification condition → measurement method → status → action-on-disconfirmation.

**Status taxonomy** (4-tier honest enum): **RUNNING** (test exists, evidence collected) · **PARTIAL** (test exists, evidence partial) · **SCHEDULED** (designed, not run) · **ASPIRATIONAL** (no infrastructure yet — flagged honestly). Zero `core/hooks/*` / `core/blueprints/*` / `src/episteme/*` / `tests/*` / `templates/*` / `labs/*` touches. **First post-soak kernel commit** per Event 72 close.

author: adisapoetro
body:
## Summary

Lint had been red on every PR since v0.4.0. None of the 71 errors were in functional `src/` code paths — they were all narrative-notebook hygiene flags or prose-friendly unicode in docstrings.

Three small moves get to green:

### 1. `pyproject.toml [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]` — relax tutorial notebooks + their generators

| Pattern | New ignores |
|---|---|
| `notebooks/**/*.ipynb` | adds `F541`, `I001`, `B007`, `RUF001/002/003`, `RUF022` (already had `E402`, `F401`) |
| `docs/tutorials/**/*.ipynb` | gets the same set (was NOT in per-file-ignores before — strict global rules applied) |
| `scripts/build_*_notebook*.py` | gets `RUF001/002/003` (these hold cell content as string literals, inherit prose justifications) |

**Justification:** tutorial notebooks are narrative-first (per-cell imports, prose-like prints with × and –, placeholder-less f-strings used as templates). Strict global rules fight that style on every PR. `src/` stays strict — 0 errors there.

### 2. `ruff check --fix` on `src/` + `tests/` — 4 auto-fixable leftovers

- `src/palmwtc/flux/__init__.py` — `I001` import sort
- `tests/unit/flux/test_advanced_outlier.py` — `I001` import sort
- `src/palmwtc/flux/advanced_outlier.py` — `RUF022` sort `__all__`

### 3. Replace 3 ambiguous `×` → `x` in `src/palmwtc/flux/advanced_outlier.py`

Source code is the one place where ASCII readability beats prettier unicode. The docstring (`"3 × stl_period"` → `"3 x stl_period"`) and the STL log-message f-strings (`{n}×IQR` → `{n}xIQR`).

## Verification

- `uv run ruff check .` → **"All checks passed!"**
- `uv run pytest -m "not slow and not requires_real_data and not requires_gpu" -x` → **510 passed, 0 failed**

## After this lands

CI on main should be **fully green** for the first time since v0.4.0:

| Check | Was | Will be |
|---|---|---|
| `lint (ruff)` | ❌ pre-existing red | ✅ green |
| `typecheck (mypy, non-blocking)` | ⚠ already non-blocking | ⚠ unchanged (separate cleanup) |
| `test (py3.11/3.12/3.13 × ubuntu/macos)` | ✅ green | ✅ green |
| `pipeline smoke (synthetic sample)` | ✅ green | ✅ green |
| `docs (jupyter-book)` | ✅ green | ✅ green |

Future PRs can stop using `--admin` for routine merges (mypy is non-blocking; lint will be green).

The umbrella `CLAUDE.md §2.5` and `palmwtc/CLAUDE.md §7.2` documenting "lint is pre-existing red, merge with --admin" will need a follow-up edit to retract that guidance.

author: ryanjbush
body:
### Motivation
- Consolidate and modernize the frontend into a typed React + Vite app to improve reliability and developer ergonomics. 
- Centralize API interactions and auth handling so protected routes and richer platform integrations can be added safely. 
- Surface scan operations, report exports and remediation workflows in the UI to better reflect backend capabilities. 
- Add governance and workflow features to support auditing and reviewer workflows in the app. 

### Description
- Migrate many components and pages from plain JS/JSX to TypeScript/TSX and introduce typed domain models in `src/types.ts` and services in `src/services/*.ts`. 
- Introduce centralized HTTP helpers in `services/api.ts` (`getJson`, `postJson`, `patchJson`, `setAuthToken`, `clearAuthToken`, `hasAuthToken`) with localStorage-backed token handling and unified request/authorization logic. 
- Expand `services/platformApi.ts` with new endpoints and mappings (scan listing, KPI summary, run/queue scans, reports JSON/SARIF download, remediation checklist, suppressions, audit logs, rule history, workflow updates and comments) and add client-side download helper. 
- Add `ProtectedRoute` and wire authentication to the router in `App.tsx`, update `MainLayout` to handle logout via `clearAuthToken`, and add `Governance` route and page for audit/rule history. 
- Enhance pages: `DashboardPage` shows KPI summary and scan records, `ScanResultsPage` supports selecting scans, exporting JSON/SARIF, and loading remediation data, `ScanningPage` supports immediate runs plus queueing, `AppInterfacePage` can trigger a scan run, and `VulnerabilityDetailPage` adds full workflow update, comments, risk acceptance with reason and richer evidence fields. 
- Update UI styles in `styles.css`, remove legacy files, and improve README with authentication instructions and note that `src/main.tsx` is the frontend entrypoint. 

### Testing
- Performed TypeScript type-checking with `tsc --noEmit` which completed successfully. 
- Built the frontend with `npm run build` to validate the Vite/TSX compilation and asset pipeline, and the build succeeded. 
- No automated unit tests were modified or added as part of this change set.

author: borisbat
body:
## Problem

`tests/aot/CMakeLists.txt` and the top-level `CMakeLists.txt` use `FILE(GLOB ...)` to discover `.das` test files and module directories. Without `CONFIGURE_DEPENDS`, the glob is evaluated **once at `cmake .` time** and the result is cached. Any `.das` test files added to a directory after the last configure are silently skipped — they're not AOT-compiled, so when `test_aot` runs and the runtime tries to link against the (missing) AOT stubs, it reports `error[50101]: AOT link failed on <fn>`.

This just bit chunk-9 dasSQLITE (`test_64_json_columns.das` … `test_71_sql_column_index_fk.das`) on local builds whose configure pre-dated the merge: a clean `cmake --build build --target test_aot` produced binaries missing 8 stubs and 8 spurious "hash desync" errors that looked like a hash-machinery regression but were actually configure staleness.

## Fix

Add `CONFIGURE_DEPENDS` to every `FILE(GLOB ...)` that drives test/AOT file discovery:

- 50 globs in `tests/aot/CMakeLists.txt` (one per test directory)
- 3 globs in `CMakeLists.txt`: `DAS_AOT_DASLIB_DEPENDS` (daslib AOT deps), `_modules` (module enumeration), `_all_shared_modules` (stale `.shared_module` sweep)

CMake re-runs the glob at build time and triggers a reconfigure if the result changed. The per-build glob cost is negligible relative to AOT compile time.

## Test plan
- [x] `cmake -S . -B build` configures cleanly
- [x] `cmake --build build --target test_aot` builds successfully
- [x] AOT test suite: 6723 tests, 6717 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors (6 pre-existing skips) — same as before the change
- [x] Pre-existing chunk-9 "AOT link failed" errors disappear after a single re-configure (this PR makes that re-configure automatic)

  - GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/reviews/:id — visibility enforced on every read path                                  
  - POST/GET /api/comments — polymorphic targets (review, project, document, dataset, code block, notebook
  cell), threaded replies

author: glaedn
body:
This PR introduces a comprehensive "Weekly Wrap-up" feature that provides users with AI-generated summaries of their weekly contributions and progress.

Key changes:
- **Backend Service**: `WeeklyWrapUpService.js` gathers statistics for users who completed tasks in the last 7 days. It compares this data against the previous week and a 6-month average, then uses Gemini to create an encouraging, analytical summary.
- **Automation**: A daily cron job in `server.js` ensures these summaries are generated overnight. An admin button allows for manual triggering during testing or maintenance.
- **API**: New endpoints in `admin.js` and `story_engine_v2.js` support triggering and retrieving these summaries.
- **UI/UX**: The user's Chronicle Timeline (now "Chronicle Summaries") has been upgraded to display these weekly reports prominently. They feature a unique gradient style, "momentum" trackers, and "top skill" highlights, providing a high-level view of the user's journey.
- **Public Profiles**: Portfolios now fetch and display these summaries, making them part of the user's public-facing record of impact.

author: baekkyunshin
body:
## Summary

세션 #B (PR #38) 에서 발견된 silent fail 3건을 근본 원인까지 해결. 모두 1차 결함 #002 와 같은 **사용자 클릭 → 시스템 응답 0** 패턴.

- **#011** [P2] 인터뷰 자동저장 라벨 영구 "저장 실패" 고착
- **#012** [P1] 인터뷰 "최종 제출" silent fail
- **#013** [P1] 로드맵·PBL 생성 Server Action 실패 시 클라이언트 silent fail

## Root cause

### #011 partial schema shallow 한계
`RoadmapInterviewSchema.partial()` / `PBLInterviewSchema.partial()` 가 zod 의 shallow partial — top-level 만 optional 이고 nested 객체/배열의 inner schema (`companyRequirements.status.min(1)`, `taskAnalysis.min(1)`, `competencies.min(1)` 등) 는 strict 그대로. UI 가 mount 시 prefilled 로 넣는 빈 행/슬롯 + 빈 배열이 자동저장 partial 검증에서 fail → `{ success: false }` 매번 반환 → 라벨 'error' 영구 고착. **DB INSERT 도 발생하지 않음** (보고서 추정의 "DB 저장 성공" 은 부정확).

### #012 zod errors[0] 한 개만 토스트
`handleSubmit` 의 `parsed.error.errors[0]?.message` 한 개만 토스트로 표시 → 사용자가 여러 누락 필드를 한 번에 파악 못 함. `submitRoadmapInterviewV2` 응답의 `result.error` 가 falsy 일 때 silent 가능.

### #013 EmptyState 가드 + generic LLM 메시지
`RoadmapResultClient` EmptyState 가드가 `hasInterview` 만 체크 (status·자가진단 미커버). `PBLResultClient` 는 가드 자체 없음. server action 의 사전 검증 분기는 정상 `{ success: false, error }` 반환하지만 `getLLMUserFriendlyError` 가 throw 메시지를 generic fallback ("오류가 발생했습니다.") 으로 변환해 사용자가 도움 못 받음.

## 주요 변경

### 신규 헬퍼
- `src/lib/utils/action-result-toast.ts` — `handleActionResult<T>` / `handleSimpleActionResult` (`result.error` falsy 여도 `errorFallback` 으로 토스트 보장)

### #011 fix
- `RoadmapInterviewAutoSaveSchema` 신규 — nested string 까지 모두 optional + 배열 min 제거 + element 의 빈 필드도 통과
- `PBLInterviewAutoSaveSchema` 신규 — `z.object({}).passthrough()` 로 단순 차단
- `saveRoadmapInterviewV2` / `savePBLInterviewV2` 의 autoSave 분기에서 새 schema 사용
- 자동저장 hook 에 `handleSimpleActionResult` 적용

### #012 fix
- `handleSubmit` 의 zod errors 모두 join (최대 5개 + fallback)
- `submitRoadmapInterviewV2` / `submitPBLInterviewV2` 응답 처리에 헬퍼 적용

### #013 fix
- `fetchRoadmapPageDataV2` / `fetchPBLPageDataV2` 응답에 `selfAssessmentExists` + `projectStatus` (PBL: `hasInterview`+`projectStatus`) 추가 → 클라이언트로 prop drill

author: pcalnon
body:
## Summary

Audit during the GAP-WS-16 prep pass found that three artifacts went missing during the Phase-1/2 merge sequence (PRs [#191](https://github.com/pcalnon/juniper-canopy/pull/191) / [#192](https://github.com/pcalnon/juniper-canopy/pull/192) / [#193](https://github.com/pcalnon/juniper-canopy/pull/193)) when each PR appended at the same line in shared files:

| Artifact | Lost in | Restored from |
|---|---|---|
| `TestContextMenuWiring` (8 tests) | #192's merge | PR #191 tip (52f905d) |
| `TestLayoutStatePersistence` (5 tests) | #193's merge | PR #192 tip (0ad5999) |
| Two CAN-018 clientside callbacks (`installContextMenus` invoker + tutorial-tab switcher) | #192/#193's merges | PR #191 tip (52f905d) |

## Root cause

Each PR appended its new test class right before `if __name__ == "__main__"` and added its clientside callbacks at the end of `_setup_datastore_callbacks`. Both insertion points are the same line in successive PRs' diffs. Sequential 3-way merges resolved by **replacing** rather than **stacking** — only the latest PR's contributions survived.

## What's verified intact on main (no fix needed)

- Stores: `control-tooltips-store`, `context-menu-tutorial-trigger`, `pinned-params-store`, `layout-state-store`, `apply-in-flight`
- `frontend/assets/context_menus.js` (full asset, 6223 bytes)
- `parameters_panel.py` pin checkboxes + `ALL_PARAMS` / `PARAM_DISPLAY_NAMES` exports
- CAN-000 / CAN-005 / CAN-016a clientside callbacks
- `TestApplyInFlightIntervalPause` (CAN-000) and `TestPinnedParameters` (CAN-005) test classes

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_dashboard_manager.py -k "ApplyInFlight or ContextMenu or LayoutState or PinnedParameters"` → **24 passed** (was 11 before this fix; 13 of those were either silently missing or asserting against missing source).
- [x] Pre-commit clean (black, isort, flake8, mypy, bandit).

## Recommendation for future merge sequences

When stacking PRs that each append to the same end-of-file insertion point, force a manual rebase / cherry-pick rather than a sequential merge. The clobber happens silently because each PR's local tests pass independently — only when *all* PRs are on main can the gap be observed.

author: jperla
body:
## Summary
- The Go enclave's goroutine swallowed every Bedrock streaming error into a bare `message_stop`. Clients got a clean `[DONE]` with no content — indistinguishable from a successful 0-token reply, which is exactly what was hiding the use-case-gate `ResourceNotFoundException` from the smoke test.
- Now: extract `smithy.APIError` code+message and emit them as `content_block_delta` + `message_delta` + `message_stop`, so the adapter translates them into OpenAI-shaped chunks. Users see `[bedrock: <Code>: <Message>]` as the assistant reply.

## Trust note
AWS API errors carry only the error code/message — never the prompt or completion bytes — so emitting them verbatim preserves zero-prompt-retention. Same standard the rest of the enclave already follows.

## Rollout
Merging triggers the existing Deploy workflow → ECR push → host re-pulls and rebuilds the EIF. **PCR0 will change** — the host's `make eif` step captures the new measurement, and `terraform apply` is needed to update the KMS condition policy so the new build can KMS-decrypt the device blob. Trust page `pcr0.txt` will follow once the new measurement is captured.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [ ] Merge to main → Deploy workflow pushes new enclave image to ECR
- [ ] On the EC2 host: re-pull image, rebuild EIF, capture PCR0
- [ ] Apply Terraform to update `var.published_pcr0` → KMS condition gates the new build
- [ ] Update `trust-page/pcr0.txt` with new measurement
- [ ] Re-smoke `/v1/chat/completions` — expect either real Claude Opus 4.7 streaming output, OR a clear `[bedrock: ResourceNotFoundException: ...]` message visible to the client (no more silent empty stream)

author: prakashgbid
body:
## Summary

Per Prakash's pipeline-order correction (2026-04-28): the ARCH-### track (Architecture Registry / AKG) reuses the same sqlite-vec + nomic-embed-text infrastructure FREG ships. Extracting a generic helper so ARCH can spin its own `arch_registry_vec` + `arch_registry_fts` virtual tables without copy-paste from FREG.

## What ships

- **New public export:** `bootstrapVecTable(db, { tablePrefix, dim, ftsTokenize? })` — idempotent CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS for `<prefix>_vec` (sqlite-vec vec0) + `<prefix>_fts` (FTS5)
- `bootstrapVectorTables(db, dim)` is now a thin wrapper around `bootstrapVecTable({ tablePrefix: 'feature_registry', dim })` — preserves the existing public API + all current FREG callers continue to work unchanged
- New public type export: `VecTableOpts`

## How ARCH uses it

```ts
import { bootstrapVecTable, OllamaEmbeddingClient } from '@chiefaia/feature-registry';

bootstrapVecTable(sqlite, { tablePrefix: 'arch_registry', dim: 768 });
const embedder = new OllamaEmbeddingClient(); // shared
// then upsert into arch_registry_vec + arch_registry_fts directly
```

## Tests

- 4 new vitest cases — prefix-scoped creation + idempotency + coexistence with the legacy call + custom `ftsTokenize`
- All **42 tests** green (38 prior + 4 new)
- Typecheck clean

## Coordination

- `EmbeddingClient` interface is already generic — ARCH consumes `OllamaEmbeddingClient` (or LAI's eventual shared service) via the same API
- FREG's higher-level helpers (`queryDense` / `querySparse` / `search`) are still `feature_registry_*` hardcoded — easy follow-up to parameterize when ARCH needs them; for now ARCH can write its own thin queries against `arch_registry_vec` / `arch_registry_fts`

## Risk

Zero. Pure refactor — no behavior change. `bootstrapVectorTables(db, dim)` is preserved verbatim and now delegates internally.

## Summary

- `PresetManager` now owns a `BundleFileWatcher` on the active user bundle's root and calls `refreshPresets()` on any filesystem change. Closes a hole where adding a custom UI to the active bundle from outside the in-plugin flows (VS Code, Finder, `git checkout`, terminal `mv`) left `currentBundle.hasCustomUI` stale and the toolbar's "Reload UI" button hidden until something else triggered a refresh. Symmetric staleness on UI removal is also fixed.
- Skips factory bundles (read-only appex Resources). Watcher is started/stopped in `setCurrentPreset`, re-keyed on rename, and torn down on delete.
- Added `currentBundleRefreshesWhenCustomUIAppearsExternally` regression test.
- Symlinked `BundleFileWatcher.swift` into `ConjureDSPTests/` so the test-target copy of `PresetManager.swift` compiles.

## Why

The "Reload UI" button is gated on `presetManager.currentBundle?.hasCustomUI`. The only existing FS watcher (in `CustomUIWebView`) is created inside `makeNSView`, which only runs when `hasCustomUI` is *already* true — so external edits that add a UI to a UI-less bundle were invisible to the UI. Moving the watcher to `PresetManager` makes the toolbar's view of the active bundle reflect on-disk truth regardless of who wrote the files.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit test passes: `ConjureDSPTests/PresetManagerTests/currentBundleRefreshesWhenCustomUIAppearsExternally`
- [x] Full `PresetManagerTests` suite (58 tests) passes — no regressions
- [x] `ConjureDSPLogicTests` passes
- [x] Manual smoke: with `test123.cdp` as the active preset, externally stripping `ui/index.html` + the `ui` manifest block hides the "Reload UI" button within ~0.5s; externally re-adding them brings the button back and remounts the custom UI — no preset switch, no in-plugin save, no MCP write

author: prakashgbid
body:
## Phase 2 — TASKMGR-004 (backpressure monitor)

Fourth PR in the Phase 2 Task Manager track. Builds on TASKMGR-001..003 (all merged).

## What this PR ships

**2 new event types:**
| Event | Severity | Actor | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task-scheduler.backpressure.engaged` | warning | task-scheduler | bucketId, queueDepth, ceiling, ts |
| `task-scheduler.backpressure.released` | info | task-scheduler | bucketId, queueDepth, ts |

**`BackpressureMonitor` class** at `apps/orchestrator/src/agents/backpressure-monitor.ts`. Per-bucket queue-depth watcher with hysteresis to prevent flapping.

- **Default thresholds:** ceiling=25, hysteresis=5 → engage at depth ≥25, release at depth ≤20.
- **Validation:** rejects ceiling≤0 or hysteresis≥ceiling at construction.
- **API:** `depth(bucketId)`, `snapshot(bucketId)`, `listEngaged()`, `checkBucket(bucketId)`, `checkAll()`.
- **Counted set:** `stories WHERE bucket_id=X AND status='pending' AND assigned_worker_id IS NULL` (same set ReadyPoolConsumer.pump considers, scoped per bucket).
- **Idempotency:** same depth on successive checks does NOT re-emit.

**Wiring (future):** PO Agent subscribes to engaged/released events and pauses new prompt creation per affected bucket. That wiring lands in TASKMGR-007.

## Tests

11 jest cases in `tests/agents/backpressure-monitor.test.ts` across 5 `describe` blocks. All green.

## Coordination

- TASKMGR-005 (HealthMetricsEmitter) reads `monitor.snapshot()` per bucket every 60s.
- TASKMGR-007 (`wirePhase2()`) hooks the monitor into the bucket-placer + ready-pool-consumer pipeline.

author: blitzy[bot]
body:
## Summary

Introduces a first-class, structured `multipart/form-data` capability across Ansible's HTTP-related code paths. A single new shared utility `prepare_multipart` is added at `lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py`, replacing today's ad-hoc, hand-crafted boundary/byte-string assembly with one canonical, RFC 7578-compliant code path that is reused by both `ansible-galaxy collection publish` and the high-level `uri` module + action plugin pair.

## Scope of Change

**9 in-scope files modified / created (931 insertions, 41 deletions across 11 commits `08da8f49b8..47a8e7e4fa`):**

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py` | NEW `prepare_multipart(fields)` utility (200+ lines, manual CRLF wire format to preserve binary content byte-for-byte) |
| `lib/ansible/galaxy/api.py` | `publish_collection` refactored to delegate multipart construction to `prepare_multipart`; 26-dash boundary preserved |
| `lib/ansible/modules/uri.py` | New `form-multipart` value for `body_format`; DOCUMENTATION + EXAMPLES updated |
| `lib/ansible/plugins/action/uri.py` | New controller-side file resolution: `_find_needle`/`_transfer_file`/`_fixup_perms2` chain applied per-field for any `body` entry that is a Mapping with a `filename` and no `content` |
| `test/units/module_utils/urls/test_urls.py` | 19 new pytest cases (positive + negative + binary integrity) |
| `test/units/galaxy/test_api.py` | Byte-integrity assertion (`email.parser.BytesParser` round-trip + sha256) extending existing `test_publish_collection` |
| `test/integration/targets/uri/tasks/main.yml` | 8 new multipart tasks |
| `test/integration/targets/uri/files/formdata.txt` | NEW fixture |
| `changelogs/fragments/uri-form-multipart.yaml` | NEW release-note fragment (3 minor_changes + 1 bugfix) |

## Key Achievements

- **All 6 AAP requirements (R1–R6) implemented and validated**
- **145/145 in-scope unit tests passing at 100%** (83 urls + 41 galaxy + 21 plugins/action)
- **Critical regression contracts preserved**: 26-dash boundary, sha256 byte-integrity, CRLF separators (no bare LF that would corrupt binary content), no header folding for long filenames
- **Public signatures unchanged**: `publish_collection(self, collection_path)`, `ActionModule.run(self, tmp=None, task_vars=None)`, `uri` argument_spec keys
- **Python 2/3 parity**: stdlib-only (no f-strings, no walrus operator); uses `string_types`, `Mapping` shims via existing `_collections_compat`
- **Sanity tests pass**: pep8, compile, import, ignores, yamllint
- **End-to-end smoke**: 2580-byte multipart body sent and round-tripped via `open_url` + `prepare_multipart`

## Critical Issue Resolved Mid-Implementation

Commit `a65227f577` rewrote the body assembly path after discovering that `email.generator.BytesGenerator` calls `_write_lines`, which expands every bare LF (`\x0a`) byte and isolated CR (`\x0d`) byte into CRLF — silently corrupting binary payloads (gzipped tarballs) and breaking the Galaxy sha256 contract. The fix uses the email module ONLY for RFC-compliant header formatting and assembles the body bytes manually.

## Remaining Work for Human Developers

- Run integration tests under `--docker centos8` httptester
- Validate across the full Python matrix (2.7, 3.5–3.9) on CI
- PR review and merge approval
- Optional live Galaxy server smoke test

## Backward Compatibility

Strictly additive. Existing `body_format=raw|json|form-urlencoded` flows are byte-for-byte unchanged. The single import-line update on `lib/ansible/galaxy/api.py` and `lib/ansible/modules/uri.py` adds a brand-new symbol that does not currently exist anywhere in the tree.

author: jwulf
body:
Consolidates the existing `.github/copilot-instructions.md` into a top-level `AGENTS.md`, matching the pattern used in [`c8ctl`](https://github.com/camunda/c8ctl/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [`orchestration-cluster-api-js#173`](https://github.com/camunda/orchestration-cluster-api-js/pull/173), and [`orchestration-cluster-api-csharp#121`](https://github.com/camunda/orchestration-cluster-api-csharp/pull/121).

## What changes

- **New `AGENTS.md`** at the repo root. Delegates to the central [`camunda/.github` AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/camunda/.github/refs/heads/main/AGENTS.md) and layers repo-specific guidance on top.
- **New `CLAUDE.md`** shim — Claude Code does not yet read `AGENTS.md` natively; this file points it at `AGENTS.md`. Same pattern as c8ctl.
- **Removes `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.** All content is migrated.

## Content lifted from c8ctl `AGENTS.md`

- Upstream-file delegation header (central AGENTS.md URL + precedence rule).
- Conventional Commits guidelines, including the **"chore not fix" rule for review-comment fix-ups** — `chore:` for review iterations, `fix:` for actual user-facing bug fixes (otherwise the CHANGELOG fills with review noise).
- **"There are no flaky tests"** framing as the partner discipline to the existing red/green refactor + class-of-defect rule.

## New rule: split generator changes from regenerated output

> When a change modifies the generator (`hooks/`, `generate.py`, generator config, `runtime/` files copied verbatim, build scripts) **and** that change causes `generated/*` (and/or `stubs/*`) to differ, **split the work into two commits**: generator change first, regenerated output second.

Why this matters here specifically:

- **Cherry-picks to `stable/*` stay clean.** Backports only need the generator commit; the target branch's release CI regenerates `generated/*` itself. Mixing the two means the cherry-pick drags generated diff through, which conflicts with whatever generated state the target branch has.
- **Reviewers can read the change.** Generator commits are small and meaningful; regenerated commits are large and mechanical.
- **`git blame` stays useful** for both surfaces.

The pre-push checklist still requires a full `make generate && make lint && make typecheck && make test`, but any resulting `generated/*` or `stubs/*` drift goes in its own follow-up commit. The naming convention mirrors the existing release-pipeline pattern:

```
chore(generation): regenerate SDK for <summary>
```

## Preserved unchanged

All existing repo-specific content carries over: documentation audiences (README vs CONTRIBUTING vs `docs/`), `uv` + `Makefile` build instructions, generation pipeline (pre-gen → openapi-python-client → post-gen → runtime injection), project layout, **always-green pyright** rule, dependency lists, and the README snippet workflow (`examples/readme.py` → `scripts/sync-readme-snippets.py`).

author: skywills
body:
## Summary

Restores ADR-008 §6's implementer-session-continuity invariant in the three rectification sites by migrating them from ADR-018 Pattern A (single-prompt-per-hop, fresh session per attempt) to **Pattern B (keep-open multi-prompt)** — the path that ADR-018 §7 line 1098 explicitly names rectification loops as a canonical example for.

### Root cause

`autofix-agent.ts`, `verification/rectification-loop.ts`, and `tdd/rectification-gate.ts` each dispatched per-attempt via `runWithFallback` + `buildHopCallback`. `buildHopCallback` does `openSession → runAsSession → closeSession` in a try/finally — closing unconditionally on every executeHop call. Result: every rectification attempt got a fresh protocol session with no conversation history, breaking the ADR-008 invariant that the implementer session persists from execution → autofix → verification rectification → TDD rectification within one tier.

This made the lean `firstAttemptDelta` prompt (autofix-agent.ts:253) unsound: it gates on \`consumed === 0 && sessionConfirmedOpen\` and assumes the agent has execution-stage context. With fresh-per-attempt sessions, that assumption was false, so attempt 1 received a context-free delta and either no-op'd or terminated immediately (the `SESSION_TERMINAL_STATE` 0ms failure observed in koda's 2026-04-28 dogfood run).

### Fix

For each of the three sites, on the runtime path:
1. **Open once** at first execute() via `sessionManager.openSession(implementerSessionName, {...})`. Idempotent on a live handle (session/manager.ts:354), so it attaches to any execution-stage session still alive.
2. **Dispatch each attempt** via `agentManager.runAsSession(agent, handle, prompt, opts)` — the middleware-aware multi-prompt primitive (ADR-019 §6).
3. **Close once** in `.finally()` at loop exit (success / exhaustion / error). On per-attempt error, discard the handle so the next attempt reopens.

Legacy `keepOpen` path is retained for non-runtime callers (test/standalone).

### ADR alignment

- **ADR-008 §6**: implementer continuity restored.
- **ADR-018 §7 Pattern B**: explicitly names rectification loops as a canonical Pattern B use case (line 1098). This PR implements that.
- **ADR-019 §5.5/§5.6/§7.4**: keep-open multi-prompt is a first-class supported dispatch shape. `runAsSession` is the prescribed primitive for the multi-prompt-against-held-handle case.
- **ADR-020 single-emission invariant**: `runAsSession` emits exactly one `session-turn` DispatchEvent per call, so audit/cost/cancellation subscribers fire correctly across N attempts on one descriptor.

No ADR amendment required.

### Side effect: removes covert tier escalation

Pattern A wired `runWithFallback` with no `noFallback` flag, theoretically permitting cross-agent swap mid-rectification. Per ADR-008 §6, tier escalation must start a fresh session; mid-loop swap with retained conversation history was a covert violation. Pattern B doesn't go through `runWithFallback`'s swap logic, so this is removed by construction. Explicit tier escalation paths (e.g. `rectification-loop.ts:494-509`) are preserved as a separate post-exhaustion branch.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `bun run lint` — clean (auto-fixed one Biome formatting issue)
- [x] All pre-commit guards pass: process.cwd guard, adapter-wrap guard, dispatch-context guard
- [x] `bun run test:bail` — full suite passes (1233 unit, full integration + UI)
- [x] Targeted suites: `autofix-session-wiring.test.ts`, `rectification-loop.test.ts`, `rectification-gate-session.test.ts`, plus all autofix-* and rectification-* tests (161/161 pass)
- [ ] Manual dogfood on a feature with autofix retry to confirm the lean delta prompt now lands on a warm session

## Out of scope

- Bug 2b (semantic reviewer hallucinating `new Set(...)` defect) — independent of session lifecycle, separate fix track.
- Bug 3 (adversarial loop oscillation, #736) — separate fix track.

author: eliasmeireles
body:
## Summary

Eight database leaf commands (list, create user, create schema, delete user, delete database, delete schema, backup, test-user) each carried the same 11-line block:

```go
if flags.Port == 0 {
    switch flags.DBType {
    case "postgres": flags.Port = 5432
    case "mysql":    flags.Port = 3306
    case "mongodb":  flags.Port = 27017
    default: return fmt.Errorf("unsupported database type: %s", flags.DBType)
    }
}
```

That's 88 duplicated lines and an easy place for the three port numbers to drift. Replaced with a one-liner against a new tiny package:

```go
if err := dbtype.ApplyDefaultPort(flags.DBType, &flags.Port); err != nil {
    return err
}
```

## New package

`internal/feature/database/dbtype` with two functions:

- `DefaultPort(dbType string) (int, error)` — pure mapping.
- `ApplyDefaultPort(dbType string, port *int) error` — only sets `*port` when it's `0`, no-op otherwise. The error message lists the supported types verbatim.

Picked a separate package so it sits naturally next to `domain/entity/database_type.go` (which uses a different naming convention — `PostgreSQL` rather than `postgres` — and is wired into the entity model). `dbtype` accepts the cmd-string form used throughout `cmd/database/*`.

## Verification

```
$ grep -rn "flags\.Port = 5432\|flags\.Port = 3306\|flags\.Port = 27017" cmd/
(no matches)
```

Each of the eight call-sites now goes through the shared helper. Future moves (e.g. adding a new DB type) only have to touch `dbtype.go`.

## Summary

- Reduces cold PR-list request volume by batching pull-list reviewer metadata once per page/account.
- Preserves no-token public repository support and signed-in private repository routing through the background service worker.
- Documents the new REST batching behavior and fallback limits.

## Why

Issue #40 calls out the current cold-row path as the largest remaining rate-limit and perceived-performance pressure: every uncached row needed both a pull endpoint request and a reviews endpoint request. This keeps the REST/no-token path intact while avoiding the per-row pull request call when first-page pull-list metadata already contains the row.

## Changes

- Adds a REST pull-list metadata batch fetch for requested reviewers, requested teams, and author login.
- Reuses page-level metadata in the content script and passes matching metadata through the runtime contract to summary fetches.
- Skips the per-row pull endpoint when metadata is available, while falling back to the original `pull + reviews` path for rows not covered by the batch.
- Extends unit and packaged extension E2E coverage for the new runtime messages and fixture mocks.
- Updates README and implementation notes for the new request-volume behavior and remaining limitations.

## Impact

- User-facing impact: Reviewer chips render with the same semantics; cold first-page PR lists use fewer GitHub API requests.
- API/schema impact: Adds internal runtime message `fetchPullReviewerMetadataBatch` and optional `pullMetadata` on summary messages; no external user-facing API.
- Performance impact: Typical first PR-list page changes from `2N` cold row requests to `1 + N` requests when all visible rows are covered by the first REST pull-list page.
- Operational or rollout impact: Public no-token and private GitHub App account paths are preserved; filtered or older pages can still fall back per row.

author: jpba7
body:
## Resumo

Ao abrir o vault no Obsidian, alguns nodes apareciam **sem nome** no graph view, e clicar neles dava erro **"folder already exists"**.

**Causa raiz:** frontmatter dos 7 templates tinha `name: <slug-da-entidade>` (e variantes). Obsidian processa o campo `name` por uma camada que reconhece HTML inline — `<algo>` que não é tag HTML válida vira string vazia no render. Resultado: nodes sem título no graph, e tentativa de criar nota com nome inválido (`<...>`) ou colidindo com pasta existente (`entidades/`, `fluxos/`, etc.).

## Fix

1. **Frontmatter dos 7 templates** (`vault/_templates/*.md`): `name: <slug-da-entidade>` → `name: template-entidade` (e equivalentes). Sem `<>`.
2. **`vault/README.md`** ganhou seção "Setup do Obsidian (1ª vez por máquina)":
   - Excluir `_templates/` em Settings → Files & Links → Excluded files (templates não são notas reais; aparecem como orphans visuais sem isso).
   - Trocar default location for new notes pra "Same folder as current file".

`vault/.obsidian/` está no `.gitignore`, então o setup é per-máquina — daí a doc no README pra próximo dev clonar saber.

## Bonus commit

`7755361 docs(relatorios): Fase 1 completa` — relatório técnico didático em .docx que estava local sem push. Incluído no PR pra não ficar perdido. Se preferir mergear separado, comenta aqui que reorganizo.

## Test plan

- [ ] Abrir `vault/` no Obsidian (Ctrl+R se já estiver aberto, ou fechar e reabrir)
- [ ] Aplicar setup do README (Excluded files: `_templates/`)
- [ ] Graph view: 29 nodes, todos nomeados, sem fantasmas
- [ ] Clicar em qualquer node não dá mais "folder already exists"
- [ ] `_templates/` não aparece como orphans no graph

## Conceito

YAML frontmatter aceita `<>` como string sem aspas, mas Obsidian processa o campo `name` (e `title`) por uma camada adicional que reconhece HTML inline. Pra placeholders em templates, sempre usar texto sem `<>` (já fizemos isso pra prosa em commit anterior trocando `<x>` por `{x}`; agora frontmatter também).

Implements **-38006 Too deep reorg** execution-apis: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/786, point 6 on top of **#11388** (point 2).

## Changes

- **`ForkchoiceUpdatedHandler.ShouldProceedWithReorg`**  
  Returns `-38006` when `IWorldStateManager.CanReorgOn(header)` is `false`.  
  All `pruning-trie`, `flat-DB`, `archive` apply their own policy via `HasStateForBlock`.

- **`ReorgDepthFinalizedStateProvider.FinalizedBlockNumber`**  
  Returns `_blockTree.FinalizedHash`'s block number instead of `BestKnownNumber - 64`.  
  Trie dirty-cache eviction now retains the `[finalized, head]` range.

- **`LogIndexStorage.GetCompressionBoundary`**  
  Compression cutoff is now `finalized`, keeping log data above finalized reorg-safe.

- **`MergeErrorCodes.TooDeepReorg`**  
  Added `= -38006`.

- **`TaikoForkchoiceUpdatedHandler`**  
  Overrides `ShouldProceedWithReorg` to always proceed  
  (Taiko finality follows L1).

All three gates now read the same boundary:

`_blockTree.FinalizedHash`

### Bug fix (atomicity)

Reorder `RejectIfInconsistent` to run before `UpdateMainChain` , so an inconsistent FCU returns -38002 without partially mutating the head. Aligns with `paris.md` step 7 ("all updates to the forkchoice state resulting from this call MUST be made atomically"). 

The previous ordering let the head move before the inconsistency check returned the error - unreachable in practice (well-behaved CLs never send inconsistent tuples), but spec-noncompliant.

`forkchoiceUpdatedV1_WhenInconsistent_ReturnsInvalidForkchoiceStateBeforeProceedingToReorgCheck`

author: kimmeia
body:
## Resumo

Tier 2 do hardening pré-lançamento. 3 mudanças cirúrgicas em 2 arquivos.

### D. Helmet (cabeçalhos HTTP de segurança)

- `app.use(helmet({...}))` antes do middleware existente que define COOP/COEP pro Google Sign-In.
- Defaults aplicados: `X-Frame-Options=DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options=nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy=no-referrer`, `X-DNS-Prefetch-Control`, `X-Download-Options`, `X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies`, remove `X-Powered-By`.
- **HSTS** ligado: `max-age=31536000` (1 ano), `includeSubDomains`. Sem `preload` por enquanto (preload é commitment longo).
- **CSP desligado**: requer curadoria caso a caso (Sentry replay, Vite, fontes externas). Habilitar sem testar = app branca. Fica pra PR dedicado pós-lançamento.
- **COOP/COEP desligados no helmet** — continuam definidos manualmente abaixo pra permitir popup do Google Sign-In via `same-origin-allow-popups`.

### E. Validação magic-number no upload

| Camada | Antes | Agora |
|---|---|---|
| MIME declarado | Allowlist | Allowlist (mantida) |
| MIME real | **NÃO VALIDADO** | `fileTypeFromBuffer` checa magic number; falha se ≠ declarado |
| Texto puro (sem magic) | Aceitava qualquer coisa declarando text/* | Heurística: rejeita se contém byte nulo ou não decodifica UTF-8 |
| Buffer vazio | Salvava arquivo de 0B | `BAD_REQUEST` |
| Path traversal no `excluir` | Bloqueava só prefixo errado | Bloqueia também URLs com `..` |

Erros agora são `TRPCError` com códigos corretos (`BAD_REQUEST`, `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`) — frontend trata adequadamente e nada vira issue ruidosa no Sentry (são códigos esperados no errorFormatter).

**Bônus**: limite do `express.json` reduzido de 50MB → 15MB. Cobre upload de 10MB em base64 (~13.5MB) com folga, sem permitir payload absurdo como vetor de DoS.

### F. I/O assíncrono no upload

Trocado tudo no `upload-route.ts`:
- `fs.writeFileSync` → `fs.promises.writeFile`
- `fs.mkdirSync` → `fs.promises.mkdir`
- `fs.existsSync` + `fs.unlinkSync` → `fs.promises.unlink` com try/catch ENOENT (sucesso idempotente)

Pico de uploads paralelos não bloqueia mais o event loop.

### Follow-up (não-blocker)

Outros `writeFileSync` espalhados pelo servidor:
- `server/calculos/export-pdf-route.ts`
- `server/integracoes/router-agentes-ia.ts`
- `server/integracoes/router-agente-chat.ts`
- `server/integracoes/whatsapp-baileys.ts`
- `server/routers/admin-agentes-ia.ts`

Cada um exige testar o fluxo específico — vai num PR separado pós-lançamento.

### Deps novas

- `helmet ^8.1.0`
- `file-type ^22.0.1`

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm check` passa
- [x] `pnpm test` 834 testes verdes
- [ ] Pós-deploy: `curl -I` na home → cabeçalhos `Strict-Transport-Security`, `X-Frame-Options=DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options=nosniff` presentes; `X-Powered-By` ausente
- [ ] Login com Google ainda funciona (popup retorna token sem erro de COOP)
- [ ] Tentar upload de `.exe` renomeado pra `documento.pdf` → 400 com mensagem "Tipo declarado não bate com o conteúdo"
- [ ] Upload de `.txt` válido → sucesso
- [ ] Upload de `.txt` com bytes binários → 400
- [ ] Upload de PDF legítimo de 12MB → 413 (PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE) com mensagem amigável
- [ ] Vários uploads de 9MB em paralelo → app continua responsiva (event loop livre)

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The `send_email()` function in `backend/app/email_service.py` had two bugs that silently prevented Resend from ever being used: SMTP was checked first (taking unconditional priority), and the Resend branch was additionally gated on `FROM_EMAIL != "onboarding@resend.dev"` — the exact default value set in Railway — so the condition always evaluated to `False`.

## Solution

Flipped the priority so Resend is tried first whenever `RESEND_API_KEY` is set, with SMTP kept as a fallback for environments that still have `SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD` configured. Removed the `FROM_EMAIL` guard entirely, since the sender address is valid for Resend regardless of its value. Updated the warning message to point to `RESEND_API_KEY` as the required variable.

### Changes
- **Modified** `backend/app/email_service.py`

body:
## Hypothesis

The reference competition result listed in BASELINE.md used `n_layers=3, slice_num=16` (the "Single-head nl3/sn16 triple compound" config) and achieved test metrics of ~46.6 / 52.9 / 24.7 / 39.6 — dramatically better than our current compound baseline (112.6 / 105.3 / 61.7 / 90.4 on the same test splits). Our current compound baseline uses `n_layers=5, slice_num=64`.

The key insight is that **fewer, coarser physics partitions with fewer layers may generalize significantly better** on this dataset. With `slice_num=64`, PhysicsAttention is over-partitioning — it may be memorizing domain-specific flow structures rather than learning generalizable physics. With `n_layers=3`, the model has fewer opportunities to overfit complex patterns. The reference architecture's superior test performance (especially OOD: 24.7 on geom_camber_cruise vs our 61.7) strongly suggests structural underfitting > structural overfitting on TandemFoilSet.

This experiment stacks all current compound improvements (Huber loss, EMA, grad_clip, bf16, n_hidden=256) onto the reference architecture config (n_layers=3, slice_num=16) to test whether this is the missing piece.

## Instructions

Make **two targeted changes** to `target/train.py` in the `model_config` dict (around line 455):

**Change 1:** `n_layers=5` → `n_layers=3`
**Change 2:** `slice_num=64` → `slice_num=16`

The `model_config` block should read:
```python
model_config = dict(
    space_dim=2,
    fun_dim=X_DIM - 2,
    out_dim=3,
    n_hidden=cfg.n_hidden,
    n_layers=3,          # changed from 5
    n_head=cfg.n_head,
    slice_num=16,        # changed from 64
    mlp_ratio=2,
    output_fields=["Ux", "Uy", "p"],
    output_dims=[1, 1, 1],
)
```

No other changes. Run with the full compound baseline flags:

```bash
cd target/ && python train.py \
  --n_hidden 256 \
  --n_head 8 \
  --loss huber \
  --huber_delta 1.0 \
  --epochs 12 \
  --grad_clip 1.0 \
  --ema_decay 0.999
```

Note: `n_layers` and `slice_num` are **hardcoded in the model_config dict** — they are not CLI args. Edit the Python source directly.

## Baseline

Current best — PR #882 (EMA + bf16 + n_hidden=256 + n_head=8 + Huber + epochs=12 + grad_clip=1.0):

| Split | val_mae_surf_p |
|-------|---------------|
| val_single_in_dist | 125.0237 |
| val_geom_camber_rc | 117.0167 |
| val_geom_camber_cruise | 78.0963 |
| val_re_rand | 92.6361 |
| **val_avg** | **103.2182** ← target to beat |

| Split | test_mae_surf_p |
|-------|----------------|
| test_single_in_dist | 112.5660 |
| test_geom_camber_rc | 105.3162 |
| test_geom_camber_cruise | 61.7016 |
| test_re_rand | 90.3631 |
| **test_avg** | **92.4867** |

**Reference config (nl3/sn16) test metrics from README:**
- test_single_in_dist: 46.569
- test_geom_camber_rc: 52.859
- test_geom_camber_cruise: 24.717
- test_re_rand: 39.561

**Reproduce baseline:**
```bash
cd target/ && python train.py --n_hidden 256 --n_head 8 --loss huber --huber_delta 1.0 --epochs 12 --grad_clip 1.0 --ema_decay 0.999
```

**Metric summary:** `target/metrics/charliepai2e1-nezuko-ema-rebased-i2fjdqe3.jsonl`

요약

moderate_skew 대표 profile 기준으로 DB tuned API k6 공식 측정 artifact를 추가했습니다.

이번 PR은 A-1의 두 번째 API/k6 비교 단계입니다. 이전 PR에서 Baseline API가 products + product_options JOIN + DISTINCT + OFFSET query shape로 측정되었고, 이번 PR에서는 같은 product-search-baseline-v1 workload를 유지한 채 normalized PostgreSQL read path를 DB tuned API로 분리해 측정합니다.

DB tuned API는 selected supporting indexes, EXISTS option filtering, no SELECT DISTINCT, OFFSET pagination 유지 조합을 사용합니다.

이번 PR은 EXISTS 단독 개선 PR이 아니며, keyset pagination, Denormalized DB, OpenSearch, Redis/cache, read model, outbox 도입도 아닙니다.

변경 사항

DB tuned API endpoint를 추가했습니다.

  • GET /api/v1/products/search/db-tuned

기존 Baseline endpoint는 유지했습니다.

  • GET /api/v1/products/search

DB tuned API 구현 관련 파일을 수정했습니다.

  • src/main/java/.../ProductSearchController.java

  • src/main/java/.../ProductSearchService.java

  • src/main/java/.../ProductSearchRepository.java

DB tuned API 관련 테스트를 수정했습니다.

  • src/test/java/.../ProductSearchControllerTest.java

  • src/test/java/.../ProductSearchRepositoryTest.java

DB tuned selected supporting indexes를 추가했습니다.

  • db/setup/a1-product-search-db-tuned-indexes.sql

DB tuned k6 스크립트를 추가했습니다.

  • benchmark/k6/product-search-db-tuned.js

DB tuned official artifact를 추가했습니다.

  • benchmark/k6/results/products_moderate_skew/product_search_db_tuned_products_moderate_skew_20260428_150401_summary.json

  • benchmark/k6/results/products_moderate_skew/product_search_db_tuned_products_moderate_skew_20260428_150401_observations.md

README를 업데이트했습니다.

  • benchmark/k6/README.md

실패했던 DB tuned run 20260428_143622 artifact는 폐기했고, 공식 DB tuned artifact는 20260428_150401입니다.

주요 실험 범위

이번 PR은 다음 범위만 다룹니다.

  • profile: moderate_skew

  • workload: product-search-baseline-v1

  • VUs: 10

  • warm-up: 1m

  • measured duration: 10m

  • execution mode: local k6

  • application table pair:

    • products_moderate_skew

    • product_options_moderate_skew

Baseline API와 DB tuned API는 같은 B1/B2/B3 scenario constants를 사용합니다.

B1_selective_option_filter

  • weight: 40%

  • categoryId=75

  • brandId=943

  • status=ACTIVE

  • minPrice=10000

  • maxPrice=100000

  • color=BLACK

  • size=M

  • stockStatus=IN_STOCK

  • sort=reviewCountDesc

  • limit=50

  • offset=100

B2_broad_active_option_filter

  • weight: 40%

  • status=ACTIVE

  • color=BLACK

  • size=M

  • stockStatus=IN_STOCK

  • sort=createdAtDesc

  • limit=50

  • offset=100

B2는 broad active option-filtered listing이므로 categoryId, brandId, minPrice, maxPrice를 보내지 않습니다.

B3_deep_offset_option_filter

  • weight: 20%

  • B1과 같은 filter/sort/limit

  • offset=10000

B1과 B3는 같은 selective workload의 shallow/deep pair입니다. 두 scenario는 같은 filter, 같은 sort, 같은 limit을 사용하고 offset만 다릅니다.

Selected Supporting Indexes

이번 PR에서는 representative measured profile인 moderate_skew 테이블에만 selected supporting indexes를 추가했습니다.

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_products_moderate_skew_active_cat_brand_review
ON products_moderate_skew(category_id, brand_id, review_count DESC, id DESC)
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE';

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_products_moderate_skew_active_created
ON products_moderate_skew(created_at DESC, id DESC)
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE';

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_product_options_moderate_skew_color_size_stock_product
ON product_options_moderate_skew(color, size, stock_status, product_id);

uniform / high_skew profile table에는 인덱스를 추가하지 않았습니다.

인덱스 선택 의도:

  • B1/B3 products index는 reviewCountDesc ordering을 우선합니다.

  • B1/B3의 price condition은 의도적으로 residual filter로 남깁니다.

  • price를 review_count 앞에 두지 않은 것은 review-count ordering을 우선하기 위한 trade-off입니다.

  • B2 products index는 broad ACTIVE createdAtDesc listing을 대상으로 합니다.

  • product_options index는 B2 broad option filtering까지 고려해 option-filter-first 형태를 사용합니다.

  • failed run이므로 폐기했고 공식 비교에는 사용하지 않습니다.

검증 결과

SQL validation은 COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) 기준으로 수행했습니다.

Scenario | matching_count | required_min_count | Passes -- | -- | -- | -- B1/B3 selected candidate | 13380 | 10050 | true B2 broad active option filter | 720000 | 150 | true

두 결과는 같은 product-search-baseline-v1 moderate_skew workload, 같은 B1/B2/B3 constants, 같은 40/40/20 weights, 같은 10 VUs, 같은 1m warm-up, 같은 10m measured duration, 같은 local k6 mode, 같은 Spring application table pair 기준입니다.

테스트

실행한 검증:

  • SQL validation

  • EXPLAIN sanity check

  • DB tuned HTTP smoke

author: yuta-yoshinaga
body:
## Summary

Closes #1553. Adds a global `--quiet` / `-q` flag, OR-combined with the existing `TRUMPCARDS_QUIET` env var. Both knobs now suppress:

- the interactive-mode startup banner
- locale-fallback warnings (`cliUnsupportedLang`, `cliLangEnvFallback`)
- the network-exposure warning printed by `web --host 0.0.0.0` (already inherited via `webQuiet := quiet`)

The flag matches the POSIX `-q` convention used by `grep` / `apt-get` / `curl`. Locale warnings were updated to advertise `--quiet/-q` alongside the env var so the flag is discoverable from the message itself.

## Why a flag, not just the env var

The env var was the only path before this change, which made one-shot scripts ugly (`TRUMPCARDS_QUIET=1 trumpcards update --yes`) and forced asymmetry: only the `web` subcommand had its own `--quiet`. With the global flag, `trumpcards -q update` works without exporting state across the whole shell.

## Test plan

- [x] New `TestRunGlobalQuietFlagSuppressesWarnings` covers both `--quiet` and `-q` paths.
- [x] `go test -tags test ./...` passes (incl. existing `TestRunUnsupportedLangFlagFallsBackAndWarns` which already pinned env-var quiet behavior).
- [x] `golangci-lint run ./...` clean; `goimports -w` applied.
- [x] Manual smoke: `trumpcards --quiet --lang fr games --short` no longer emits the `fr` fallback warning, but `trumpcards --lang fr games --short` still does.

## Notes

- `web --quiet` was already inheriting the global value (`webQuiet := quiet`), so no behavior change there.
- The flag is intentionally **not** plumbed through `applyTrailingGlobalFlags` (the `<game> --quiet` form). The reason: the warnings affected by `quiet` all fire before that helper runs, so trailing form would only suppress the interactive-startup banner — and a user typing `trumpcards blackjack -q` is already past the banner stage. If demand surfaces later we can defer the warnings, but the YAGNI cost is high relative to the one-line benefit.

author: santhonys
body:
## Summary

PRD 007 M1 only — Lane A SDT extractor deferred after benchmarking on the only SDT-preserving publisher in the corpus (Kent State). Tier 4 on a Word-rendered PDF reaches 92% of Lane A's field count (450 vs 492), so the new tier and ``python-docx`` dependency aren't justified yet.

What ships here:

- **Inner-ZIP sniffer** (``sniff_zip_inner_format`` + refactor of ``sniff_format_from_bytes``). DOCX vs XLSX is now content-based via inner ZIP entries (``word/document.xml`` vs ``xl/workbook.xml``) instead of magic-bytes-only. This auto-fixes Stanford's PDF-mislabeled-as-DOCX (reroutes to ``pdf_flat``) and stops JMU's two real-CDS DOCX rows from silently routing as XLSX.
- **DOCX year detection** (``detect_year_from_docx_bytes``) reads ``word/document.xml`` + every ``word/header*.xml`` part. JMU's CDS title lives only in headers, so the body-only fallback wasn't enough.
- **Format-agnostic dispatcher** (``detect_year_from_bytes``) lets the worker run year detection before knowing the source format.
- **21 unit tests** in ``test_docx_sniff.py`` covering DOCX/XLSX/bad-ZIP/HTML sniff and year detection (body, header-only, split runs, invalid spans, ambiguity, dispatcher).

Verified against real fixtures:

| Fixture | Sniff | Year |
|---|---|---|
| Stanford 2025-26 (mislabeled docx, actually PDF) | ``pdf_flat`` | ``2025-26`` |
| JMU 2024-25 (header-only title) | ``docx`` | ``2024-25`` |
| JMU 2025-26 (header-only title) | ``docx`` | ``2025-26`` |
| Kent State 2025-26 (828 SDTs) | ``docx`` | ``2025-26`` |

Lane A vs Lane B remain deferred per the decision notes in the worker docstring and ``docs/plans/prd-007-fixture-audit.md``.

## Test plan

- [x] All 21 ``test_docx_sniff.py`` unit tests pass
- [x] Sibling worker modules still import (``worker``, ``tier4_cleaner``, ``tier4_extractor``, ``subsection_slicer``)
- [x] Real-fixture sniff + year detection verified for Stanford, JMU 2024-25, JMU 2025-26, Kent State
- [x] Existing PDF year detection regression unaffected (PDF magic byte path untouched)

body:
Two narrow write tools so the agent can recover from stuck-controller scenarios without the user having to drop into a kubectl session. Tool layer + RBAC layer updated together to keep defense-in-depth intact.

## What's added

**Tools (`mcp-servers/k8s/src/mcp_k8s/tools.py`):**
- `delete_pod(name, namespace, grace_period_seconds=None)` — pods are managed; deletion is reversible.
- `rollout_restart(kind, name, namespace)` — patches the pod-template annotation, same as `kubectl rollout restart`. `kind` whitelisted to `deployment | statefulset | daemonset`.

**RBAC (`k8s-mcp-k8s/templates/cluster-reader.yaml`):**
- `pods: delete`
- `apps/{deployments,statefulsets,daemonsets}: patch`

Existing `["*", "*"] → [get,list,watch]` rule is preserved, so reads still work the same.

## Why

This came up because the cluster's `argocd-application-controller-0` got wedged (Ready=True, but reconcile loop dead for 24+ hours, blocking every Application from picking up new commits). The MCP could see everything was stale but couldn't do anything about it — so we needed manual `kubectl rollout restart` from a workstation to unstick it.

With these tools, future versions of that scenario (any pod-level wedge) are recoverable from the agent without dropping out to kubectl.

## What's *not* in scope

- No `kubectl apply` / arbitrary patch — those would massively expand the blast radius and the agent should still go through git/ArgoCD for any desired-state change.
- No Service / ConfigMap / Secret writes — anything reflectable through ArgoCD continues to be read-only here.

## Caveat: bootstrap problem

This change deploys via ArgoCD (the `mcp-k8s` Argo app sources from `tank-operator/k8s-mcp-k8s`). If ArgoCD itself is wedged, this PR can't deploy until the user manually unsticks it once. After that, future wedges are self-healable from the MCP.

## Test plan

- [ ] After ArgoCD reconciles: `kubectl get clusterrole mcp-k8s-reader -o yaml` shows the new pod/delete + apps/patch rules.
- [ ] mcp-k8s pod restarts (image rebuild from `claude-container-build.yml`-style flow); the Python tools.py change is picked up.
- [ ] Calling `delete_pod` on a non-existent pod returns a clean error; on a real pod it succeeds.
- [ ] Calling `rollout_restart("statefulset", "argocd-application-controller", "argocd")` triggers a pod recreate.

body: ## Summary - Adds a small `Background Conversation` section to the system prompt, gated on `conversationType ∈ {background, scheduled}`. Tells the LLM to invoke the `notifications` skill for progress / blockers / completion in non-interactive contexts. - Interactive conversations pay zero token cost (the section only appears when the flag is true). - Justification for breaching system-prompt minimalism is documented in the PR body of the plan. ## System-prompt minimalism — why this addition is justified Both `assistant/CLAUDE.md` and project `CLAUDE.md` flag system-prompt additions as a last resort. The three documented alternatives don't apply here: 1. **Skills already exist** (`skills/notifications/SKILL.md`) but auto-loading the catalog still puts content in the prompt and doesn't tell the LLM *when* to invoke it during non-interactive work. 2. **Config / feature flags** can't drive per-turn LLM behavior. 3. **Code** can't enforce "explicitly notify" — that defeats the user-design goal. The addition is gated on `conversationType ∈ {background, scheduled}` so interactive conversations pay zero token cost. The new section is ~3 lines. ## Offset audit Per the plan's offset-audit instruction: I scanned all entries in `staticParts` for redundant or obsolete content that could be condensed to offset the new ~3-line addition. The current entries are: - `customPrefix` (user-supplied) - `buildParallelToolCallsSection` (~3 lines, all critical) - `buildContainerizedSection` (Docker mode only) - `buildCliReferenceSection` (CLI discovery) - `buildAttachmentSection` (attachment delivery) - `buildAccessPreferenceSection` (sandbox vs host) - `buildCredentialSecuritySection` (security) - `buildExternalContentSection` (security) Nothing was safe to remove without losing user-visible behavior, so the audit is a no-op. ## Implementation notes - The plan referenced `assistant/src/daemon/conversation-agent-loop.ts` for the buildSystemPrompt callsite, but that file does not call `buildSystemPrompt`. The actual callsites live in `assistant/src/daemon/conversation.ts` (`resolveSystemPromptCallback` and `warmPromptCache`). The plan explicitly anticipated path drift; both real callsites in `conversation.ts` are updated. - `getConversation(this.conversationId)?.conversationType` is a single SQLite primary-key SELECT — sub-millisecond, negligible per-turn. Same lookup pattern is used in `conversation-agent-loop.ts` for the home-feed event check. - `btw-sidechain.ts` and `conversation-store.ts` (comparator-only) calls intentionally do not pass the flag — they aren't user-facing background-conversation flows. ## Test plan - [x] `bun test src/prompts/__tests__/system-prompt.test.ts` — 5 new tests pass (true / false / undefined / no-flag / static-block placement). - [x] `bun test src/__tests__/system-prompt.test.ts` — 59 existing tests still pass. - [x] `bun test src/prompts/__tests__/system-prompt-memory-v2.test.ts src/prompts/__tests__/build-cli-reference-section.test.ts` — 11 related tests still pass. - [x] `bunx tsc --noEmit` — no new errors from changed files (pre-existing IPC-typing errors unrelated to this PR). author: m5d215
body:
## Summary

\`simplify_expr\`'s \`{pairs} | length → N\` rewrite folded any object construct whose values were input-free — including generators like \`range(0)\` (zero outputs), \`empty\`, and \`range(N>1)\` (multiple outputs). The fold assumed every value contributes exactly one to the count, so the wrong cardinality fell out.

Lifts the existing \`is_single_output\` predicate from \`simplify_expr\`'s \`first()\` rewrite to module scope as \`expr_is_single_output\` and reuses it as the cardinality gate for the \`{pairs} | length\` fold.

## Surface

\`\`\`
\$ echo 'null' | jq -c '{a: range(0)} | length'
(empty — jq's `{a: empty}` short-circuits the construction)

\$ echo 'null' | jq-jit -c '{a: range(0)} | length'
1                                                # ← bug, before this PR

\$ echo 'null' | jq -c '{a: range(2)} | length'
1
1                                                # one length per generated object

\$ echo 'null' | jq-jit -c '{a: range(2)} | length'
1                                                # ← only one output, before this PR
\`\`\`

After the fix, both match jq exactly. \`{a: 1, b: 2} | length\` and \`{a: 1, a: 2} | length\` still fold to constants because their values are single-output.

Same family as the array-side fix from #319 (which excluded \`Expr::Empty\` from \`count_comma_elements_no_input\`). Found by \`tests/fuzz_diff.rs\` at 50 000 cases.

## Drive-by issue filed

**#334** — \`FieldStringCase\` (\`.c | ascii_downcase\` inside standalone arrays) emits null silently when the field value isn't a quoted string. Surfaced by the same fuzz_diff sweep, separate fix.

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo build --release\` — zero warnings
- [x] \`cargo test --release\` — 1115 regression (was 1110, +5 cases for the generator-valued and single-output matrix), 509 official, all green
- [x] \`./bench/comprehensive.sh --quick\` — no regression

Closes #333
