body:
## Summary

- `TASK_TOPIC_HANDOFF_SCHEMA` only listed `title` and `summary` in `required`, so OpenAI/Azure strict structured outputs rejected every `generateHandoff` call with `400 Invalid schema for response_format 'task_topic_handoff': 'required' is required to be supplied and to be an array including every key in properties. Missing 'keyFindings'`.
- Added `keyFindings` and `nextAction` to `required` so the schema satisfies strict mode. Downstream code in `src/server/services/taskLifecycle/index.ts` already treats both as optional (`keyFindings?`, `nextAction?`) and the title is only written when truthy, so behavior is unchanged when the model returns empty values.

author: ebarlas
body:
The implicit-privileges SPI lets extensions inject index privileges derived from a role's application privileges at role-build time, but the get-role API still returns only the explicitly stored privileges, leaving Kibana and other admin tools no way to show users what they will actually be authorized to do.

Add an opt-in `include_implicit` query parameter that decorates each returned `RoleDescriptor` with the `IndicesPrivileges` its registered `ImplicitPrivilegesProviders` would contribute. The default is `false` so existing clients see no behavior change.

Each implicit entry is wrapped in a new `ImplicitlyGranted` marker subclass that emits `implicitly_granted: true` at xcontent time only. The PUT parser rejects `implicitly_granted` as an unknown field so a GET-then-PUT round-trip cannot accidentally promote an implicit grant into a stored one.

When `xpack.security.dls_fls.enabled` is false, implicit entries that carry DLS or FLS are dropped from the response to mirror the runtime suppression in `addImplicitPrivileges`, keeping the response in lock-step with what authorization enforces.

A new `x-pack/qa/security-implicit-privileges-extension` module wires `HelicarrierImplicitPrivilegesProvider` through the `SecurityExtension` SPI so the `include_implicit` parameter and the `implicitly_granted` response field can be asserted end-to-end against a real cluster.

author: krisbraun
body:
## Summary
- `onChannelEnabled`, `getContacts`, `startSync` in `connectors/google-contacts/src/google-contacts.ts` all threw `"No Google authentication token available"` when `integrations.get(channelId)` returned null. The same connector already handles this case correctly in `syncBatch` (lines 108-117) — *"abort instead of throwing to prevent infinite queue retries."* This brings the three remaining entry points in line: log + return (or return `[]` for `getContacts`), don't throw.
- The throws were surfacing as `"Recovery dispatch failed for connection"` warns at the api worker level, blocking the parent connector's recovery dispatch from completing.

## Why
We hit this on prod tonight while diagnosing why kris@plot.day's Personal Google Calendar wasn't recovering after a stuck-sync repair. PostHog log at `2026-04-28T22:32:28Z` revealed the unwrapped `__TWIST_ERROR__`: `"No Google authentication token available"` thrown at `_GoogleContacts.onChannelEnabled` — bubbling up from a recovery dispatch on a parent GCal twist.

The deeper cause behind the missing token is a real model mismatch worth following up on:

GoogleContacts is built as a sub-connector via `Integrations.MergeScopes`. `getChannels()` returns a static `{id: "contacts"}`, so `integrations.get("contacts")` looks up a token keyed by `"contacts"` — but the parent's OAuth flow stored tokens keyed by *calendar/drive/gmail* channel ids. The lookup misses by design even when OAuth is healthy. The right long-term fix is to route sub-connector token lookups through the parent's token store on miss; that's a runtime change in `@plotday/twister`/api worker and should land separately.

For now, fail-soft restores reliability: contacts won't sync until the next OAuth touchpoint or daily refresh, which is acceptable for the contacts-as-side-effect use case and unblocks the parent connector's recovery for the two affected users (kris@plot.day Personal GCal, cameronandrewpak@gmail.com).

## Test plan
- [ ] After deploy, re-arm `recovery_pending=true` on the affected `twist_instance_connection` rows
- [ ] Confirm next 30-min `recoverPendingConnections` cron reaches the parent GCal connector's `onChannelEnabled` without surfacing a "Recovery dispatch failed" warn
- [ ] Confirm `link` count starts climbing on `019dac4d-96cc-7c24-9d6c-2a45854cbf42`
- [ ] Spot-check PostHog logs for the new `"Auth token missing for ... during onChannelEnabled, skipping"` warn — confirms fail-soft path was taken

author: osamu620
body:
## Summary

Originally a bug report — `open_htj2k_enc -i big.tif -o big.j2c Qfactor=90` failed with *Failed to open input file for streaming* because the encoder's default streaming (line-based) path only had PNM and PGX stream readers; the help text claimed TIFF was supported but only the buffered (`-batch`) path actually handled it.

This PR adds streaming TIFF input, then turns the per-app reader code into a small shared utility:

- **New static lib `openhtj2k_imgio`** (`source/apps/imgio/`) — holds the PNM, PGX, and TIFF stream readers plus an `imgio::open_stream_reader()` factory that dispatches by extension. Linked `PRIVATE` by the encoder and imgcmp; not part of `libopenhtj2k`'s public ABI, and `OPENHTJ2K_TIFF_SUPPORT` is `PRIVATE` on the new target only.
- **Encoder**: streaming path now accepts `.tif` / `.tiff` (8/16-bit, RGB or grayscale, both planar configs, uncompressed or strip-compressed). Tiled TIFFs still need `-batch` with a clear "use `-batch`" hint.
- **imgcmp**: migrated to imgio. PAE / MSE / PSNR rewritten as line-based reductions over per-component planar rows (mathematically identical to the prior interleaved-buffer loop; printf format byte-exact). Adds `num_components` and `bit_depth` equality checks, gains TIFF input, drops `image_class.hpp` (~370 lines). Working set drops from `O(W·H·nc·4)` to `O(nc·W·4)` bytes per side, enabling gigapixel comparisons.
- **PGX parser bug fix**: latent trailing-whitespace overrun. The post-header *"skip single trailing whitespace"* was a `while`-loop that greedily consumed data bytes equal to `0x09 / 0x0a / 0x0d / 0x20`, shifting every row by one byte and overrunning EOF on the last fread. Per spec, exactly one whitespace separates the PGX header from data — consume one, no more. Same bug class as the documented PnmStreamReader fix; surfaced because imgcmp's old reader didn't share the code path.
- **Core lib `image::read_pnmpgx`**: replace `fgets(buf, 256, fp)` with `do { fgetc } while (… != \n …)` so PNM comments longer than 255 chars are no longer truncated. Prior truncation made the next byte get parsed mid-comment as header data, producing garbage `width` / `height` / `maxval`.
- **Docs**: README format-support row and `docs/cli_encoder.md` opening paragraph updated to drop the *"TIFF batch only"* claim.

## Test plan

- [x] Encoder TIFF round-trips: 8-bit RGB contig, 16-bit RGB contig, 8-bit grayscale, 8-bit RGB separate-planar — all encode and lossless round-trip is byte-identical to source. Contig and separate-planar produce the same J2C bytes.
- [x] Gigapixel TIFF (heic2501a, 42208×9870 RGB LZW): encodes in 5.5 s → 278 MB J2C; output byte-identical to the pre-refactor build; `-reduce 4` decode succeeds.
- [x] PNM lossless round-trip byte-identical to source.
- [x] PGX encode passes for 12-bit single-component conformance file.
- [x] imgcmp output format byte-exact vs old binary; same PAE/MSE/PSNR numbers on shared inputs.
- [x] `ctest --build-config Release -j 8` → **627 / 627 pass**.
- [x] `ctest -R ^wasm_` → **137 / 137 pass** (WASM decoder + native imgcmp validation).
- [x] WASM rebuild clean (subprojects/build); `node open_htj2k_dec.mjs` smoke test decodes a real `.j2k` and the new imgcmp confirms WASM == native (PAE = 0).
- [x] Perf: encoder gigapixel timing within noise of pre-refactor; imgcmp +0.5 ms/invocation overhead on small images (lost in process startup), big memory win on large images.

body:
Adds index privileges for ES|QL datasets (`create_dataset`, `delete_dataset`, `read_dataset_metadata`, `manage_dataset`) behind the external datasources feature flag.

No coarse cluster privileges (`read_datasource`, `manage_datasource`) for datasource read/manage; access is only through `global.datasource`.

`global.datasource` has to match which datasource name the request touches, not only the cluster action name. Datasource put/get/delete (and the pre–dataset-PUT authorize) requests implement `DataSourceRequestInfo` so they expose those names in a fixed way; `ManageDatasourcePrivileges` in x-pack-core can evaluate that without depending on concrete ES|QL request classes.


~~Dataset PUT over REST runs `cluster:admin/esql/dataset/authorize_datasource` before `PutDatasetAction` so attaching a datasource requires the same global grant, not just `create_dataset` on indices.~~.  UPDATED: Now an interceptor is used for this behavior

## Summary

author: tad-smith
body:
## Summary

Fixes the chicken-and-egg in `firestore.rules` that was blocking the Phase 7 bootstrap wizard's first write. The bootstrap admin's auto-self-add to `kindooManagers` (and every subsequent wizard write) needed an authorisation path that didn't depend on a manager claim that hadn't been minted yet.

## Option chosen — A1 (rule-level gate, operator-seeded stake doc)

Added a new `isBootstrapAdmin(stakeId)` helper to `firestore.rules`:

```
function isBootstrapAdmin(stakeId) {
  let stakePath = /databases/$(database)/documents/stakes/$(stakeId);
  return isAuthed()
    && exists(stakePath)
    && get(stakePath).data.setup_complete == false
    && get(stakePath).data.bootstrap_admin_email == request.auth.token.email;
}
```

OR'd into the read + write rules on the four wizard-managed paths:

- `stakes/{sid}` — read + update (Step 1 fields + final `setup_complete=true` flip)
- `stakes/{sid}/kindooManagers/{canonical}` — read + write (auto-self-add + Step 4 additional managers)
- `stakes/{sid}/wards/{wardCode}` — read + write (Step 3)
- `stakes/{sid}/buildings/{buildingId}` — read + write (Step 2)

Web-engineer's wizard wires direct-Firestore writes (`apps/web/src/features/bootstrap/hooks.ts`); this rules gate authorises them as-is. Option B (callable wrapper) was rejected because Option A is structurally cleaner here — rules can express the predicate without ambiguity, the web side already wires direct writes, and a callable would add a network round-trip per step plus a parallel enforcement surface.

## Mechanism

The gate is strictly time-bounded by `stake.setup_complete`. The wizard's final write flips it to `true`; the rule evaluates pre-write state, so the flip itself succeeds, but every subsequent wizard-shaped write fails because `isBootstrapAdmin` now returns false. By that point `syncManagersClaims` has minted a real manager claim from the auto-added kindooManagers doc, and `isManager(stakeId)` takes over.

`lastActorMatchesAuth` still applies — the gate widens *who can write*, not *what they can claim to be*. The bootstrap admin's writes still carry `lastActor.{email, canonical}` matching their auth token, so audit trail integrity is preserved during bootstrap.

## Required operator step

Per the brief's recommended A1, the operator pre-seeds the stake doc with `setup_complete=false` and `bootstrap_admin_email=<typed-form email>` BEFORE the bootstrap admin signs in for the first time. New §4.4 in `infra/runbooks/provision-firebase-projects.md` walks through a Firebase-console seed (recommended) plus a brief gcloud / Admin SDK alternative.

The gate's `get()` short-circuits cleanly if the stake doc is missing (`exists()` check returns false → `isBootstrapAdmin` returns false), so a missing-seed scenario fails closed rather than open.

## Files changed

- `firestore/firestore.rules` — `isBootstrapAdmin` helper + four read/write rule predicates
- `firestore/tests/bootstrap.test.ts` — **new**, 23 tests
- `firestore/tests/lib/rules.ts` — `bootstrapAdminContext` helper + `bootstrapAdmin` persona
- `docs/firebase-schema.md` — §6 mirror updates + new §6.1 "Bootstrap-admin gate" subsection
- `infra/runbooks/provision-firebase-projects.md` — new §4.4 "Pre-bootstrap stake-doc seed"

## Test counts

- `pnpm --filter @kindoo/firestore-tests test`: **183 / 183 passing** (160 prior + 23 new) — no regression.
- `pnpm --filter @kindoo/functions test:integration:local`: 21 / 21 passing — no regression.
- `pnpm lint` (all workspaces): clean.
- `pnpm --filter @kindoo/firestore-tests typecheck`: clean.

## Architectural notes

- Phase 7 wizard's `useEnsureBootstrapAdmin` does `setDoc(..., { merge: true })`. The rule treats it as a `write` (set covers create + update), so the gate authorises both first-write and subsequent re-runs of the wizard mid-setup.
- The `isBootstrapAdmin` predicate is the ONLY new authorisation path — the stake-doc `create` rule remains superadmin-only, so the operator-seeded doc is the single source of truth for `bootstrap_admin_email`. The bootstrap admin can't self-elevate by creating a new stake doc.
- Other collections (access, seats, requests, calling templates, auditLog) are intentionally NOT covered by the gate — the wizard never writes to them, and the gate's scope is deliberately minimal.

## Ambiguity surfaced

None blocking. One coordination note: web-engineer's Phase 7 wizard branch (`phase-6-config-bootstrap`) and this rules-fix branch can land in any order. Wizard fails gracefully (toast errors) until the rules fix lands; rules fix is no-op against any stake that doesn't have a `bootstrap_admin_email` field set.

## Test plan

- [x] All 183 firestore rules tests pass under emulator
- [x] All 21 functions integration tests still pass
- [x] Repo-wide prettier check clean
- [x] Typecheck clean across affected workspaces
- [ ] CI green (this PR)

Refs T-22 in `docs/TASKS.md`.

author: derekmwright
body:
## Summary

- Q02 SF10 2026-04-28 failed at 10m57s with `nats: key not found` on a broadcast-join build cache, then `object not found` from the S3 fallback. Root cause: producer wrote payloads ≤4 MB to NATS KV **only** (no S3); KV bucket has a 5-minute TTL, query took longer than that, KV entry expired mid-flight, S3 had nothing to fall back to.
- This change reorders both stage-output paths (`writeUnpartitionedWSHF`, `writePartitionedShuffle`) so S3 is always the durable store; KV becomes a best-effort fast-read cache. Aligns with the existing `writeBatchResult` pattern (which already had this comment about the 5-min TTL).
- Failed KV-cache writes now log at Debug, not Warn — they're a perf nit, not a correctness signal, because S3 is durable.

## Why this is the right architectural fix

Trino, Spark, and Flink all separate "durable shuffle storage" from "fast read cache." Wadjet's KV bucket has both a 5-min TTL and a 1 GB cap — those are correct constraints for a **cache**, but wrong for the **store of record**. This PR keeps the cache constraints and makes S3 the store of record.

Cost: small payloads now incur an S3 PUT (~50–100 ms) in addition to the KV write. For a TPC-H query with many stage boundaries this adds ~1–2 s of stage-boundary latency. Q02 was failing at 10m57s, so the trade is overwhelmingly in favor of correctness. Periodic `ResultCleaner.CleanStale` sweeps S3 (1 hr default TTL).

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/worker/ ./internal/coordinator/` — pass (1.2 s + 212 s)
- [x] `go test -v -run TestTPCHQueries ./benchmarks/tpch/` — 22/22 pass at SF0.01
- [x] Existing `TestKVFastPath_SmallOutputSkipsS3` updated → `TestKVCache_SmallOutputDurableInS3AndCachedInKV` (asserts BOTH stores hold data)
- [x] New regression test `TestKVCache_FallsBackToS3WhenKVMisses` simulates KV expiry by purging the entry; reading via S3 must succeed
- [ ] `cmd/tpch-harness --mode=local` — currently broken on `main` itself ("NATS disconnected error=EOF" on this WSL2 box, environmental); verified via `git stash` that the harness fails identically without this change. Not a regression introduced here.
- [ ] SF10 EC2 deploy — needs explicit user approval per `feedback_no_auto_deploy`; recommend re-running Q02 to validate the failure mode is gone.

2. `AttemptSteeringRollAsync` (generates question)
3. Append the question to the already-degraded delivered message

Result: a Catastrophe-level failure produced unhinged delivered text, but the steering question stitched on at the end was perfectly lucid. The whole-message degradation rule was being violated.

### Fix
1. Steering now runs FIRST.
2. On steering success, the question is appended to `chosenOption.IntendedText` via a fresh `DialogueOption` wrapper (so the caller's option object isn't mutated and combo / callback / history paths still see the original).
3. The combined intended+steering text is what `DeliveryContext.ChosenOption.IntendedText` exposes to the LLM.
4. `DeliverMessageAsync` rewrites the combined text per failure tier — degradation now covers the steering question too.

### textDiffs ordering
- Steering layer: `original_intended` → `intended + steering_question` (FIRST)
- Tier-modifier layer: `intended + steering_question` → `delivered` (SECOND)

### #364 acceptance criteria
- [x] When steering succeeds, the question is appended to intended text BEFORE the delivery LLM call.
- [x] When player rolls a Catastrophe AND steering succeeded, the LLM receives the combined text and degrades the whole thing.
- [x] textDiffs order: Steering first, tier modifier second.
- [x] Existing `SteeringRollTests` adjusted-by-design (the `Contains(steeringQuestion, deliveredMessage)` assertion now covers the new flow).
- [x] Regression tests in `Issue364_SteeringBeforeDeliveryTests`:
  - `Steering_success_appends_question_to_intended_text_before_delivery` — asserts the LLM saw combined text
  - `Catastrophe_with_steering_success_degrades_combined_text` — asserts LLM degraded the whole combined text on failure
  - `TextDiffs_ordering_steering_first_then_tier_modifier` — asserts diff ordering
  - `Steering_failure_no_steering_diff_no_question_appended` — negative case

## #365 — Shadow corruption gated on success

### Problem
The shadow check overlay was guarded by `if (corruptionInstruction != null && rollResult.IsSuccess)`, so a failed roll never triggered shadow corruption. The YAML rules (`data/delivery-instructions.yaml`) explicitly provide corruption instructions for `fumble`, `misfire`, `trope_trap`, `catastrophe`, and `nat1`, and the rules state Catastrophe + Nat 1 trigger BOTH trap + shadow growth.

### Fix
- Drop the `&& rollResult.IsSuccess` condition. Shadow corruption fires whenever the shadow check misses AND `corruptionInstruction != null`, regardless of main roll outcome.
- The existing interest-delta-override block (which converts a success into a failure delta when shadow corrupts a success) is preserved but now guarded separately by `if (rollResult.IsSuccess)`. On a failed roll the failure interest delta has already been applied earlier in the turn — re-applying it here would double-penalize.

### #365 acceptance criteria
- [x] `ApplyShadowCorruptionAsync` fires whenever shadow check misses AND `corruptionInstruction != null`, regardless of roll success/failure.
- [x] Interest-delta-override only fires on roll success.
- [x] textDiffs includes `Shadow (X)` layer on failed rolls when shadow check misses.
- [x] Regression tests in `Issue365_ShadowOnFailedRollTests`:
  - `FailedRoll_ShadowMiss_AppliesShadowCorruption` — Nat 1 + shadow miss → corruption fired + Shadow textDiff present
  - `FailedRoll_ShadowMiss_DoesNotDoubleApplyInterestDelta` — interest delta on failed-roll path stays bounded by the failure tier
  - `SuccessRoll_ShadowMiss_StillOverridesInterestDeltaToFailure` — preserves the existing success→failure-delta override

## DoD Evidence

**Build (`dotnet build pinder-core/Pinder.Core.sln`)**:
```
160 Warning(s)
0 Error(s)

Time Elapsed 00:00:13.24
```

**Tests (`dotnet test tests/Pinder.Core.Tests/Pinder.Core.Tests.csproj`)**:
```
Failed!  - Failed:     6, Passed:  2464, Skipped:    18, Total:  2488, Duration: 4 s
```

The 6 failures are pre-existing on `main` (verified by `git stash` + retest before this branch's changes) — `CharacterLoaderSpecTests.Load_StarterCharacter_HasValidProfile(...)` and `Load_Gerald_MatchesSpecExactValues` use `Assert.Fail("SKIPPED: ...")` when the `design/examples` prompt directory isn't on disk. Unrelated to this change.

**Tests (`dotnet test src/Pinder.GameApi.Tests/Pinder.GameApi.Tests.csproj`)** — runs against the new submodule via the pinder-web parent worktree:
```
Passed!  - Failed:     0, Passed:   405, Skipped:     0, Total:   405, Duration: 21 s
```

**New regression tests added**:
- `tests/Pinder.Core.Tests/Issue364_SteeringBeforeDeliveryTests.cs` — 4 tests
- `tests/Pinder.Core.Tests/Issue365_ShadowOnFailedRollTests.cs` — 3 tests

All 7 new tests pass on the first run. The pre-existing `SteeringRollTests` (12 tests) all still pass with the new flow.

**Commit**: `3249f27 fix(engine): steering before delivery + shadow corruption on failed rolls`

**Push**: `* [new branch]      fix/W1b-engine-pipeline-fixes -> fix/W1b-engine-pipeline-fixes`

**Deviations from contract**: none. `SteeringContext.DeliveredMessage` keeps its name (it's the LLM-adapter contract field) but semantically now carries the player's intended pre-delivery text — documented inline in `GameSession.cs`.

## Research Log

| Topic | Source | Key finding |
|-------|--------|-------------|
| `DialogueOption` immutability | `pinder-core/src/Pinder.Core/Conversation/DialogueOption.cs` | All fields readonly via constructor; safe to wrap by allocating a new option for the delivery LLM call without mutating caller state. |
| `TextDiff` field names | `pinder-core/src/Pinder.Core/Text/WordDiff.cs` | Public properties are `LayerName`, `Spans`, `Before`, `After` (not `Layer`/`Original`/`Final`). |
| `ShadowCheckResult` API | `pinder-core/src/Pinder.Core/Conversation/ShadowCheckResult.cs` | Public properties are `CheckPerformed`, `IsMiss`, `OverlayApplied`. |
| `StatDeliveryInstructions` typing | `pinder-core/src/Pinder.Core/Conversation/GameSessionConfig.cs` + `HorninessEngine.cs` | Stored as `object?` and accessed via reflection in `HorninessEngine.GetShadowCorruptionInstruction`; the regression test loads the real YAML via `Pinder.LlmAdapters.StatDeliveryInstructions.LoadFrom`. |
| LESSONS_LEARNED §13 (submodule commit ordering) | `pinder-web/LESSONS_LEARNED.md` | Followed: commit + push pinder-core first, then `git add pinder-core` in parent and commit. Did NOT run `git submodule update` between those steps. |
| LESSONS_LEARNED §5 / §9 (worktree isolation) | `pinder-web/LESSONS_LEARNED.md` | Used a `git worktree add /tmp/work-W1b origin/main` worktree; never touched `/root/projects/pinder-web`. |

## Summary
Phase 1 of the impact-adjacency consensus gate per `docs/specs/2026-04-28-impact-adjacency-gate.md`. PRs that touch any file marked `// @gossip:impact-adjacent:<category>` must reference a consensus-id whose report file exists under `.gossip/consensus-reports/<id>.json`. CI fails closed.

- **scripts/impact-adjacency-gate.mjs** (165 LOC) — reads PR diff, scans annotated files, verifies consensus-id ↔ report-file binding, supports one-time bootstrap exemption.
- **.github/workflows/impact-adjacency-gate.yml** — runs on `pull_request`, dry-run mode keeps `.gossip/` clean.
- **packages/orchestrator/src/round-counter.ts** — first annotated file: `shared-state-with-lifecycle` (the `inMemoryFallback` Map at line 45).
- **tests/scripts/impact-adjacency-gate.test.ts** (219 LOC, 9/9 pass) — covers no-annotation pass, consensus-id+report happy path, missing-report fail, waiver-only skip, bootstrap one-time exemption, fail-closed on unresolvable base ref, JSON.parse-tolerant bootstrap dedupe.

## Consensus context
This PR was reviewed via consensus round `7311feac-48734d78` (gemini-reviewer + sonnet-reviewer + haiku-researcher with cross-review). Round produced **13 confirmed / 3 disputed / 2 unique / 1 new** findings. All critical/high findings were addressed before this PR was opened:
- Path (b) `.gossip/consensus-reports.jsonl` flat-file lookup was dead code (storage is `.gossip/consensus-reports/<id>.json`); replaced with directory-based existence check.
- Bootstrap-exemption substring match → `JSON.parse` dedupe.
- `expiresAt` field added per spec §6 (audit-only in Phase 1).
- `changedFiles()` now fails closed (exit 1 with "could not resolve base ref") instead of silently returning [].
- Consensus-id regex broadened to allow whitespace.
- `execSync` → `execFileSync` (no shell-string interpolation).
- `path.join` traversal hardened with `realpathSync` + ROOT-prefix check.
- `IMPACT_ADJACENCY_DRY_RUN=1` set in CI workflow so runs never dirty tracked `.gossip/`.

Spec §1 enum updated to include `shared-state-with-lifecycle` (kept local — `docs/specs/` is gitignored).

| `components/dashboard/seller-edit-form.tsx` | Formulaire client, warning si IBAN manquant |
| `app/dashboard/admin/sellers/page.tsx` | Indicateur "⚠ pas d'IBAN" + lien Éditer |

**Validé en runtime local** (Stripe sandbox, branche `feat/stripe-checkout`) :
- [x] `npm run build` passe
- [x] `npm run lint` 0 erreurs
- [x] `POST /api/orders` crée Order + Stripe Checkout Session (`cs_test_...` retourné)

author: jbeast291
body:
## Changes made in this PR

 -  Added `CellManagerPatches`
    - LWEs now resolve to the correct batch when in negative voxel space, fixing entities in negative batches
    - LWEs local cell positions within batches are now always positive, relative to the batch's origin (mirroring the same logic from positive batches that the game uses)
 - Removed `Array3Patches`
    - The patch to `CellManager` means that entities are no longer stored in negative cell indexes within an `EntityCell`, making `Array3Patches` redundant. `CellManagerPatches` fixes the root cause and not some workaround `Array3Patches` was doing (that didn't even work in most cases).

I've documented the logic behind the patch within the code in an xml tag (hopefully they are useful and not too verbose).

author: apaksh-gupta
body:
## Summary

Adds 11 marketing-tier presentational primitives to `@amplify/ui` (v2.1.0) so product landing surfaces stop reinventing the same building blocks. Every visual primitive lives in the design system per the MANDATORY DESIGN RULE.

## Components (11)

| Component | Variants | Notes |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| `Hero` | centered / split / asymmetric | Density-aware, eyebrow + media slot |
| `Section` | default / muted / inverted / accent | Heading / description / body / footer slots |
| `FeatureGrid` | plain / card / bordered | Auto 1→4 col responsive |
| `CTABand` | default / accent / inverted | between/center/start align |
| `LogoCloud` | greyscale / colour / colour-on-hover | 3–6 column |
| `Testimonial` | card / inline / featured | Avatar + company logo slots |
| `PricingTable` | N tiers, highlighted plan | Plan card composition slots |
| `AnnouncementBar` | default / accent / inverted | Dismissible, controlled or uncontrolled |
| `ComparisonTable` | N plans × N features | Optional category groups |
| `StatLarge` | up / down / flat trend | Hero stat display |
| `Quote` | small / medium / large | Decorative quote mark + attribution |

## Stories (77 total)

5–8 stories per component covering default, all variants, density variants, and edge cases (long content, no description, no avatar, etc).

## Patterns

- Followed `Card` (composition + variants), `Button` (density × size table), `MetricCard` (slot pattern)
- Server-renderable everywhere except `AnnouncementBar` (internal dismiss state → `'use client';`)
- Semantic CSS variables only (`--amp-semantic-*`) — no hardcoded colours
- Phase A motion/shadow/surface tokens not yet merged → sensible CSS values with `// TODO(phase-a):` comments
- Strict TypeScript, all types exported from package barrel

## Verification

- `npm run build -w packages/ui` → 57 contracts generated, ESM 135.58 KB, DTS 30.64 KB
- `npm run validate` → 0 errors / 0 warnings
- `npm test -w packages/ui` → 20 tests passing (3 files)
- `npm run build -w packages/storybook` → built successfully (77 new stories indexed)
- `component-status.json` updated — all 11 registered as `beta` since `2.1.0`

## Test plan

- [ ] Storybook deploys cleanly to GitHub Pages
- [ ] Chromatic visual regression baselines accepted
- [ ] Verify a11y addon shows no violations on default stories
- [ ] Spot-check responsive breakpoints (sm/md/lg/xl) on Hero split + FeatureGrid 4-col
- [ ] Verify `AnnouncementBar` keyboard dismiss works with `Tab` + `Enter`
- [ ] Pixel governance review (per CLAUDE.md — Pixel may raise PRs back here)

author: stuagano
body:
## Summary

The `/_apx/probe` route was redirecting to `/_apx/setup`, so the existing connectivity tester in `_ui_probe.py` never actually rendered. This PR turns the probe page into a real first-stop diagnostic for "why isn't my agent working" — first item on the [dev UI roadmap](../blob/main/ROADMAP-dev-ui.md). Builds on #16 / #17 / #18 / #19.

- **`_dev.py`** — route renders the probe page, plus `GET /_apx/probe/checks` for the JSON health-check payload.
- **`_ui_probe.py`** — four parallel checks with a 4 s per-check timeout:
  - `workspace_auth` — `WorkspaceClient()` init succeeds
  - `model` — one-shot LLM call to `ctx.config.model`
  - `env_vars` — keys declared in `.env` vs the running process
  - `sub_agents` — for each configured URL, `GET /.well-known/agent.json`

  Each check returns `{name, status, message, hint}`; the aggregate exposes `overall` ok / warn / fail. Page renders a "Health checks" section above the existing URL tester with traffic-light rows; JS fetches the JSON endpoint on load.

  Drive-by fixes: missing `_deploy_overlay_html` import (NameError that would have fired on first render), stray `{url_prefill}` template var with no formatter behind it.

## Test plan

- [x] **11 new tests** in `test_probe_checks.py`: all-green path; workspace auth fail propagates to overall fail; model fail; model skip when no model configured; env-var warn surfaces overall warn (uses `tmp_path` + `monkeypatch`, no /tmp pollution); sub-agent unreachable / non-200 paths through the aggregator; **three direct unit tests for `_check_sub_agent`** that exercise the actual `httpx` code path with a context-manager-shaped mock (200 / non-200 / exception).
- [x] `pyright` clean on all changed files.
- [x] Full Python suite: **268 passing** (was 257).

author: synapticode-ai
body:
Closes #1.

## Summary

Adds finite-and-range checks at the two FP32→FP16 cast sites in `_load_weight_for_coreml`, extracted as two named helpers (`_validate_ternary2_alpha`, `_cast_fp16_retain_with_guards`) with `FP16_MAX = 65504.0` as a named constant.

## Approach

Three-way handling distinguishes input-bug (raise) from representation-bug (clamp):

- **Non-finite alpha or |alpha| > FP16_MAX** → raise. Clamping would mask a quantiser bug upstream.
- **Non-finite source FP32 weight** (NaN/Inf) → raise. Source-model corruption shouldn't propagate silently.
- **Finite but |value| > FP16_MAX in fp16_retain** → clamp to ±FP16_MAX with operator-visible WARNING. Preserves the run on legitimate outliers while surfacing them.

## Validation

DSR1-7B export+palettise pipeline:
- Clean pre-fix (baseline confirmed during diagnosis)
- Clean post-fix (export 49.8s, palettise saved, zero guard activations on legitimate inputs)

Full pytest suite post-fix: **310 passed, 19 skipped (no regressions)**.

Mistral-7B re-export pending WD Passport archive mount; will validate end-to-end then.

## Tests

`tests/test_coreml_export.py`: 7 cases covering clean pass-through, all pathology raises, and the clamp-with-warning path.

body:
# Organize CP MiniZinc parts with their respective meanings

The scope of this PR is "put the right content in the right attribute". In the next PR we will modify every model to use the transport class MiniZincModelParts introduced in #445. By attributes we mean `_model_prefix`, `_variables_list`, `_model_constraints`, `mzn_output_directives`. For example, before we were mixing content that must be in _variable_list with `_model_prefix`.  

We needed to update `test_assemble_model_preserves_legacy_order` and `test_assemble_model_accepts_explicit_parts` because the first one is not anymore a legacy and the second one because we needed to decouple it from a specific cipher (since the "MiniZinc model parts" should not be attached to a cipher )

We needed to update more tests in order to fulfill "organize CP MiniZinc parts with their respective meanings" refactor. Here the explanation why we need to update each tests.

## Why the tests had to change

Before this refactor, several CP MiniZinc model builders mixed parts:

- `_model_prefix` collected variable declarations on top of the include directives and helper predicates it was supposed to hold.
- `_variables_list` received items returned as constraints by `input_*` methods.
- Models then baked the prefix into `_model_constraints` with `self._model_constraints = self._model_prefix + self._model_constraints`.

That layout made `model_constraints` carry items that were not constraints (the includes and helpers, plus the input declarations), and `model_variables` carry items that were not declarations (the `cp_constraints` returned from `input_*` methods).

The refactor moves each fragment to its semantically correct attribute:

| Attribute            | What it should hold                                         |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `_model_prefix`      | only `include` directives and helper predicates             |
| `_variables_list`    | only variable declarations                                  |
| `_model_constraints` | only constraints and the solve directive                    |
| `mzn_output_directives` | only `output [...]` directives                            |

`MznModel.current_model_parts()` now exposes `prefix=list(self._model_prefix)` so `assemble_model()` produces the same final MiniZinc source without each builder having to pre-merge the prefix into `_model_constraints`.

This invalidates two kinds of test assertions that lived in the test suite:

1. **Index-based reads of `model_constraints[i]` that returned a declaration.** Those declarations now live in `model_variables`, not `model_constraints`.
2. **Total-count assertions of `len(model_constraints) + len(model_variables)`.** The two prefix items (`include "globals.mzn";` and the `MINIZINC_USEFUL_FUNCTIONS` block) no longer appear in `model_constraints` after
   deduplication, so the combined count drops by exactly 2.

The sections below document each updated test and why.

---

## tests/unit/cipher_modules/models/cp/mzn_model_test.py

### `test_assemble_model_orders_variables_constraints_outputs` (line 31, was `test_assemble_model_preserves_legacy_order`)

**Changes:**
1. Renamed from `test_assemble_model_preserves_legacy_order` — the new name describes what the test actually verifies now that the prefix is a separate,
   explicitly-cleared part.
2. Added `model._model_prefix = []` immediately after constructing the model.

**Reason:** `MznModel.__init__` calls `initialise_model()`, which seeds `_model_prefix` with `['include "globals.mzn";', MINIZINC_USEFUL_FUNCTIONS]`. The
test sets `_variables_list`, `_model_constraints`, and `mzn_output_directives`
manually and then asserts the assembled output is exactly:

```
var int: x;
constraint x = 1;
solve satisfy;
output ["x=", show(x)];
```

Now that `current_model_parts()` includes `prefix=list(self._model_prefix)`, the assembled output also contains the seeded include + helper block. The test narrowly exercises the variables → constraints → outputs ordering, so we
explicitly clear `_model_prefix` to keep the expected string as-is. The assertion itself is unchanged. The "legacy" framing in the old name no longer fit (the test no longer mirrors the pre-refactor `_model_constraints`prefix-bake), so the test is renamed to describe what it now checks.

### `test_build_generic_cp_model_from_dictionary_xor_linear` (line ~340)

**Change:** replaced the legacy "extend prefix with declarations and bake the prefix into constraints" pattern with the new direct placement:

Before:
```python
variables, constraints = model.input_xor_linear_constraints()
model._model_prefix.extend(variables)
model._variables_list.extend(constraints)
model._model_constraints.extend(model.final_xor_linear_constraints(weight))
model._model_constraints = model._model_prefix + model._model_constraints
```

After:
```python
variables, constraints = model.input_xor_linear_constraints()
model._variables_list.extend(variables)
model._model_constraints.extend(constraints)
model._model_constraints.extend(model.final_xor_linear_constraints(weight))
```

**Reason:** the test was reproducing the bug at the call site — declarations were sent to `_model_prefix`, constraints were sent to `_variables_list`, and then the prefix was baked into `_model_constraints`. With `current_model_parts()` now returning the prefix, repeating that pattern would emit the prefix twice. The new code mirrors what the production builders now do and exercises the same end-to-end `model.solve(...)` path.

### `test_minizinc_model_parts_lines_concatenates_in_order` (was `test_assemble_model_accepts_explicit_parts`)

**Change:** rewrote the test to call `MiniZincModelParts.lines()` directly, asserting on the returned list. Removed the `SpeckBlockCipher` /
`MznModel(speck)` setup.

Before:
```python
def test_assemble_model_accepts_explicit_parts():
    speck = SpeckBlockCipher(number_of_rounds=1)
    model = MznModel(speck)
    parts = MiniZincModelParts(...)
    assert model.assemble_model(parts) == "<concatenated string>"
```

After:
```python
def test_minizinc_model_parts_lines_concatenates_in_order():
    parts = MiniZincModelParts(...)
    assert parts.lines() == [
        'include "globals.mzn";',
        "var int: x;",
        "constraint x = 1;",
        "solve satisfy;",
        'output ["x=", show(x)];',
    ]
```

**Reason:** the assertion only verified that
`prefix + variables + constraints + outputs + carries_outputs` are returned in that order — pure-function behaviour of the dataclass. The cipher and the `MznModel` instance were not used by the assembly path when `parts` is provided (`assemble_model_lines(parts)` returns `parts.lines()` without touching `self`). They were a coupling artefact left over from `MznModel.__init__` requiring a cipher. Testing the dataclass directly removes the unnecessary fixture, makes the test faster, and pins the contract on the layer that actually owns it. The `MznModel.assemble_model` delegation is still exercised by `test_assemble_model_orders_variables_constraints_outputs` above.

---

## tests/unit/cipher_modules/models/cp/mzn_models/mzn_impossible_xor_differential_model_test.py

### `test_build_impossible_xor_differential_trail_with_extensions_model` (line 11)

**Change 1 — total count:** `1764 → 1762`.

**Change 2 — index-based assertions replaced with membership checks:**

Before:
```python
assert mzn.model_constraints[99] == "array[0..31] of var 0..2: inverse_plaintext;"
assert mzn.model_constraints[3]  == "array[0..63] of var 0..2: key;"
assert mzn.model_constraints[39] == "array[0..31] of var 0..2: cipher_output_5_12;"
```

After:
```python
assert "array[0..31] of var 0..2: inverse_plaintext;" in mzn.model_variables
assert "array[0..63] of var 0..2: key;" in mzn.model_variables
assert "array[0..31]

body:
## Summary

Closes #227 and #229. Filing a separate comment on #228 noting the symptom doesn't reproduce — see "On #228" below.

## #227 — manifest_name fallback at finalize time

Pre-fix: \`manifest_name\` in \`summary.json\` was set directly from \`resolved.name\`. A manifest without \`[run].name\` produced \`null\` in the finalized summary, which then forked across UI surfaces:

- Runs list synthesized \`<unnamed>\`
- Insights aggregator re-derived from filename basename
- Run-detail card (\`GET /api/runs/{id}\`) returned \`null\`

Three surfaces showed three different names for the same run.

**Fix:** new \`dispatch::summary::resolve_manifest_display_name\` helper:

1. Prefers \`[run].name\` (trimmed) when non-empty
2. Falls back to \`manifest_path.file_stem()\`
3. Returns \`None\` only when neither yields a non-empty value

Both \`runner.rs::finalize_run\` and \`hierarchical.rs\`'s finalize phase now route through it, so the three surfaces agree on a single string per run.

## #229 — dim aborted rows in runs list

Pre-fix: a run with \`status: \"aborted\"\` and \`tasks_total: 0\` rendered with the same visual weight as a completed multi-task run. The status pill was the only differentiator.

**Fix:** \`opacity-60 italic\` applied to \`<TableRow>\` when \`r.status === 'aborted'\`, in both the flat list and the manifest-grouped expanded rows. Default visible — no filter, no localStorage state, no new UI controls. The operator can still scan and click through; the rows just don't compete visually with completed runs.

## On #228

Issue #228 says \"The frontend run-detail surface renders this on every run\" but \`grep -rin 'interrupt' crates/pitboss-web/spa/src/\` returns no matches. The \`was_interrupted\` field exists in the data model and is set at finalize time, but no SPA surface displays it today. The symptom in the issue doesn't reproduce — closing as not-applicable in a follow-up comment rather than touching unrelated code.

## Tests

6 new unit tests in \`dispatch::summary::tests\` covering the declared / empty / filename / no-stem / no-extension / whitespace cases. Full workspace + SPA \`npm run check\` + \`npm run build\` all green.

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test --workspace --features pitboss-core/test-support\` — 571+ tests pass
- [x] \`cargo lint\` clean
- [x] \`cargo tidy\` clean

- [x] SPA \`npm run build\` succeeds
- [ ] After merge: dispatch a manifest without \`[run].name\`, confirm runs list / insights / run-detail all show the filename stem
- [ ] After merge: dispatch a manifest, kill before any task spawns, confirm the row in the runs list shows dimmed/italic

## Summary

Closes **FARM-LOW-006** with a registry-only architectural correction. Earlier in this session a thorough-mode Explore agent audited Phase 3.0 and reported "13/16 modals exist; 3 missing." Empirical re-check confirms all 3 supposedly-missing mutations are already wired with correct architectural shapes the rote modal-per-mutation heuristic missed.

## Empirical evidence

| "Missing" mutation | Actual UI surface | Why this shape is correct |
|---|---|---|
| `updateBatchFeedAssignment` | Re-uses `AssignFeedsToBatchModal.tsx` per `BatchFeedingTab.tsx:5` docblock | Backend upsert semantics (the `(tenantId, batchId)` UNIQUE index from PR #216) make a separate edit modal redundant — same fields populate from existing row, save as upsert |
| `deleteBatchFeedAssignment` | `ConfirmModal` (generic) per `BatchFeedingTab.tsx:7` | Domain-specific delete-modal would only carry a confirm message; `ConfirmModal` does that with typed props. Less code = correct choice |
| `createBatchWaterQualityMeasurements` | `BulkRecordTab.tsx` (TAB, not modal) | Bulk-entry UX correctly modelled as a tab — a modal would force context switch per entry |

The earlier audit's heuristic was *"every mutation has a domain-specific `*Modal.tsx` file"*. The right rule is *"every mutation has a UI surface that calls it from the appropriate role gate"*. By the right rule, Phase 3.0 is 16/16 and has been since before this session started.

## Architectural decision: closure-by-correction

Same pattern as PR #217 (FARM-MEDIUM-007 closed by rate-analysis showing the proposed handler was over-engineered): close by reasoning, not by code. Building three additional modals "to match the heuristic" would have produced exactly the duplication the existing architecture correctly avoided.

## Side effect

PR #207's session-summary doc listed 3 missing modals in its OPEN-items table. A future doc-update should retract that line. Tracked as a separate concern from this finding's closure.

## Test plan

- [x] No code change — registry-only commit
- [x] commit-msg validator: `Closes:` trailer present
- [x] finding-registry chain valid (tip `90dbaf9b…`)

Closes: FARM-LOW-006

author: eanzhao
body:
## Summary

Three independent issues on the Lark `/daily` flow, each surfacing as a confusing UX problem for bot owners:

### 1. Duplicate "GitHub authorization required" block
`BuildDailyReportCredentialsCard` set both `content.Cards[0].Text` (card body) and `content.Text` (intended as non-card fallback) to the same auth content. Lark's form-mode composer (`LarkMessageComposer.BuildLeadingMarkdown`) concatenates `content.Text` with the first card body into a single rendered markdown element, so users saw the block twice. Card body is now the single source of truth; `content.Text` stays empty.

### 2. Submitted github_username dropped on auth re-prompt
`BuildDailyReportCredentialsCard` rebuilt the form with `preferredGithubUsername: null`, so the username the user typed (`/daily eanzhao`) was discarded and the field reverted to the `octocat` placeholder. `CreateDailyReportAgentAsync` now passes the resolved username into `BuildGitHubAuthorizationResponseAsync`, the auth-required JSON echoes it back as `github_username`, and the card threads it into the form's `default_value`.

### 3. SkillRunner / WorkflowAgent ignored bot owner's LLM route
Reported as `Upstream LLM route 'nyxid' rejected the request with HTTP 400 for model 'gpt-5.4'. Provider 'openai' not connected.` even though the bot owner had a working `chrono-llm` service in NyxID and a UserConfig with `defaultModel = gpt-5.5` / `preferredLlmRoute = /api/v1/proxy/s/chrono-llm`.

Root cause: `ChannelLlmReplyInboxRuntime` (nyxid-chat) reads UserConfig and pins `ModelOverride` / `NyxIdRoutePreference` / `MaxToolRoundsOverride` on outbound LLM metadata, but `SkillRunnerGAgent` and `WorkflowAgentGAgent` built their own metadata from `State.OutboundConfig` only. Without those keys, `NyxIdLLMProvider` fell through to compile-time defaults (`gpt-5.4` against `/api/v1/llm/gateway/v1/`), and the gateway routed `gpt-*` to OpenAI — which the bot owner hadn't connected.

Both agents now resolve `IUserConfigQueryPort` via `Services.GetService<>` and apply the same three metadata keys nyxid-chat applies. Empty fields and projection failures fall through to provider defaults silently, preserving existing test fixtures and no-projection hosts.

## NyxID-side verification

Used `nyxid` CLI on the affected account:

- `nyxid service list` → `api-github` shows `pending_auth`; `chrono-llm` shows `active`.
- `GET /api/v1/providers/my-tokens` → `{"tokens":[]}` (so the GitHub OAuth check correctly returns "not connected").
- `GET /api/v1/llm/status` → all providers `not_connected` (so any `gpt-*` model routed to the gateway 400s).
- `GET /api/user-config` → `defaultModel=gpt-5.5, preferredLlmRoute=/api/v1/proxy/s/chrono-llm`.

So the LLM was correctly configured at NyxID; the skill runner just wasn't reading it.

## Test plan
- [x] `dotnet test test/Aevatar.GAgents.ChannelRuntime.Tests/Aevatar.GAgents.ChannelRuntime.Tests.csproj` — 713 passing
- [x] New `BuildExecutionMetadata_ShouldApplyOwnerUserConfigOverrides_*` covers ScopeId-based lookup, missing port fallback, empty-fields fallback, and throwing-port fallback
- [x] New `FormatDailyReportToolReply_*` tests cover oauth_required + credentials_required + username pre-fill
- [x] Updated existing tool tests to assert `github_username` is echoed
- [x] Updated `NyxRelayAgentBuilderFlowTests.FormatToolResult_ShouldReturnCardForm_WhenCredentialsRequired` to require empty `Text` (the old assertion codified the duplicate-render bug)
- [ ] Manual sanity check on Lark with a real bot post-deploy

## Summary

- When `isPaused` transitions to true (via PauseButton / usePauseSystem), the AudioContext is suspended, freezing the hum loop, swing crossfade, and any in-flight one-shot sounds mid-playback
- When `isPaused` transitions to false, the AudioContext resumes exactly where it left off
- This is orthogonal to mute: mute zeroes the master gain (persistent user preference via `audioMuteStore`); pause freezes the entire audio graph via `AudioContext.suspend()/resume()` (transient simulation freeze via `uiStore.isPaused`)
- The pause effect lives in `useAudioEngine.ts` (not `usePauseSystem.ts`) because the audio engine owns the `AudioContext`

body:
## Summary

Lands all seven phases of `docs/prompt-type-inference-worklist-refactor.md`. Replaces the manually-ordered 13-step build pipeline (with its hand-coded `fold → chain → fold` shape) with a single witness-bag worklist driver, `Builder::fold_to_fixed_point`.

- **Phase 0** — Lifted ~1300 lines of inline `mod tests` into sibling `_tests.rs` files (tokio/serde-style layout) so `builder.rs` and `file_analysis.rs` are navigable before the refactor lands.
- **Phase 1** — Captured dump-golden fixtures for four representative packages (Mojolicious::Routes::Route, MojoApp, Moo::Service, Schema::Result::User) so every commit on this branch can prove no observable behavior change. Test-count baseline + at-risk internal-field reader audit in `tests/fixtures/dump-golden/BASELINE.md`.
- **Phase 2** — Pinned the architectural invariants the worklist relies on (chain convergence, plugin-override survival, fixed-point idempotency, provenance round-trip) as `type_inference_invariants_tests`. Tightened in Phase 6.
- **Phase 3** — Plugin overrides became priority witnesses. `apply_type_overrides` no longer writes `Symbol.return_type` directly; it pushes a Plugin-source `InferredType` witness, and `WitnessSource::priority()` (Plugin=100, Builder=10) makes the `PluginOverrideReducer` short-circuit dominate the per-arm fold. The `is_overridden` skip branch in writeback is gone.
- **Phase 4** — `resolve_return_types`'s 274-line monolith decomposed into named reducers + helpers (`ArityReturnReducer`, plugin-override seeding, `DelegationReducer`, `SelfMethodTailReducer`, `CallBindingPropagator`, hash-key-owner fixup). Driver shrunk to ~10 lines.
- **Phase 5** — The three former post-walk CST walks (assignment typing, return-arm refresh, invocant filling) collapsed into one `ChainTypingReducer` with three modes, fed by a single `ChainTypingIndex` built once per build.
- **Phase 6** — `Builder::fold_to_fixed_point` replaces the explicit pre/post-fold sequence. Snapshot-based convergence (Sub/Method `return_type` + `type_constraints.len()`); `MAX_FOLD_ITERATIONS = 64` debug safety net; the two re-emittable inner passes became clear-and-emit via `WitnessBag::remove_by_source_tag`. Convergence test lifted from 1 → 4 hops; idempotency test now asserts byte-identical witness count + TC length across re-folds.
- **Phase 7** — CLAUDE.md's 13-step pipeline collapsed to 9 with a new "Worklist invariants" subsection naming the contract for adding new fact-folds (reducers stateless, witnesses monotone, re-emittable passes clear-and-emit, source priority breaks ties, bag-and-TC sync). Type-inference spec status snapshot rewritten around `fold_to_fixed_point`. Plugin-system spec corrected for the Phase 3 priority-witness override flow.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test`: 506 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `./run_e2e.sh`: 93 passed across 5 nvim suites (27 + 25 + 7 + 14 + 20), matches baseline
- [x] Dump-golden parity: byte-identical against `tests/fixtures/dump-golden/*.json` for all four representative packages
- [x] Phase 2 invariants pass on the worklist driver: `convergence_chain_resolves_through_four_reassignment_hops`, `plugin_override_survives_all_folds`, `post_walk_fold_is_observably_idempotent` (now asserting witness count + TC length equality), `provenance_accessor_and_round_trip`
- [x] Acceptance grep `grep -rn "fold pass 1\|fold pass 2\|13[ -]step\|13 phases" CLAUDE.md docs/` returns only matches inside the (now `Status: landed`-annotated) worklist-refactor spec itself

### 📌 Overview
This PR adds automated integration tests for authentication routes using Jest and Supertest. It ensures that the API endpoints for user registration and login are functioning correctly and reliably.

---

### ✅ Changes Made

- Installed **Jest** and **Supertest** as development dependencies
- Configured Jest to run in a Node.js environment with ES module support
- Refactored server structure:
  - Created `app.js` to export Express app
  - Updated `server.js` to handle server startup and socket.io
- Implemented test database configuration using `MONGODB_URI_TEST`
- Updated database connection logic to switch based on `NODE_ENV`
- Created integration tests in `tests/auth.test.js`
- Added lifecycle hooks for setup and cleanup:
  - `beforeAll` → connect to test database
  - `afterEach` → clear user collection
  - `afterAll` → close database connection

---

### 🧪 Tests Implemented

#### POST /api/auth/register
- ✅ Should register a new user successfully (201)
- ✅ Should fail if email already exists (400)
- ✅ Should fail if required fields are missing (400)

#### POST /api/auth/login
- ✅ Should login with correct credentials (200)
- ✅ Should fail with incorrect password (401)

---

### 🔄 Test Lifecycle Management

- Database connection established before tests
- Database cleaned after each test to ensure isolation
- Connection closed after all tests complete

---

### ▶️ Test Execution

Run tests using:

```bash
npm test

PASS tests/auth.test.js

    ✓ should register a new user successfully
    ✓ should fail to register with an existing email
    ✓ should fail to register with missing required fields
    ✓ should log in with correct credentials

## Summary

Implements the stack-aware prompt addendum spec'd in `docs/brainstorms/2026-04-27-stack-aware-prompt-addendum-design.md` (committed in this PR). Fixes the root cause behind ENG-45's UI-stage halt: `AGENT_PROMPTS.md` was hard-coded to "Twinning, a desktop app built with Tauri v2 + SvelteKit + Rust", so every harness-self issue (ENG-24, ENG-45, ENG-46) trips on prompts that reference `cargo`, `bun`, `#[tauri::command]`, `docs/architecture/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md`, etc.

After this PR, every dispatched stage prompt has a per-slug `learned-rules/<slug>/project-profile.md` appended automatically. The base prompts in `AGENT_PROMPTS.md` are stack-neutral; the profile carries all stack-specific framing (Stack, Build & test gates, File layout, Language idioms, Don'ts).

## What this PR contains (16 commits, 16 plan tasks)

| Commits | Tasks | What |
|---|---|---|
| `fc7bbb9`, `5f470c1` | docs | Brainstorm + plan committed first so the PR is self-describing. |
| `62c0022`, `4103441` | T1, T2 | `_validate_project_profile_schema` + `_resolve_profile_markers` in `bin/setup-helpers.sh`; `bin/setup-helpers-test.sh` covers both. |
| `58449f3`, `9cf5438` | T3, T4 | `bin/setup-prompts/discovery.md` + `_render_discovery_prompt` token-interpolator. |
| `0ea17ec`, `0317786` | T5, T6 | `phase_project_profile` + `is_project_profile_done` in `bin/setup.sh`; new `bin/phase-project-profile-test.sh`. Discovery invocation carries the same ENG-48 isolation flags as `dispatch.sh` (`--setting-sources project,local`, `--disable-slash-commands`, `--disallowed-tools "<list>"`, `gtimeout` watchdog at 10 min). |
| `48e555f` | T7 | `install-launchd.sh` + `phase_launchd` refuse to run without a complete profile. `install-launchd-test.sh` updated to seed test-slug profiles. |
| `6c2d26d` | T8, T9 | Flag-gated `append_project_profile` in `bin/render-prompt.sh`; `bin/render-prompt-test.sh` covers flag-on / flag-off / retrospective-skip / missing-profile / marker-bearing-profile paths. |
| `92ef7d5` | T10, T11 | Hand-authored `learned-rules/harness/project-profile.md` + `learned-rules/twinning/project-profile.md` (saves a discovery-dispatch round-trip; either can be regenerated by `bash bin/setup.sh project-profile`). |
| `02e2184` | T12 | `PIPELINE_PROFILE_ADDENDUM` flag removed; addendum is unconditional. |
| `96a7b95` | T13 | `bin/dry-run.sh` adds a "project-profile present and complete" check. |
| `5cf3318` | T14 | `AGENT_PROMPTS.md` §§ 1–8 reframed: framing lines, gate examples, scope statements all reference the addendum. Tauri/SvelteKit/cargo/bun specifics demoted to illustrative `e.g.` examples. Fence-count invariant preserved (each stage still has exactly 2 fences). |
| `642be51` | T15 | `phase_migrate` calls `phase_project_profile` so existing single-project installs get profiled at upgrade time. |
| `bc70dbc` | T16 | `render-prompt-slug-test.sh` updated to seed the test slug's profile (the addendum-injector dies on missing profile, by design). |

## Test plan

- [x] `bash bin/setup-helpers-test.sh` — 12/12
- [x] `bash bin/phase-project-profile-test.sh` — 4/4
- [x] `bash bin/render-prompt-test.sh` — 5/5

- [x] Full sibling sweep: 21/21 `bin/*-test.sh` files green
- [x] `TARGET_REPO=… bash bin/dry-run.sh` — 21/22 (the one fail is `config: paused=false`, which is expected because the orchestrator was deliberately paused for this work)
- [x] `AGENT_PROMPTS.md` fence-count: each of the 9 stages has exactly 2 fences (load-bearing for `render-prompt.sh`)
- [ ] Live verification post-merge: dispatch ENG-45 UI stage and confirm the agent reads the harness profile (Stack: bash, gates: bash bin/*-test.sh) instead of improvising.

## Operator notes

- **Orchestrator is paused** in `state.local.json` for this work. Don't unpause until this PR is merged AND you've eyeballed both profiles.
- **Profiles can be regenerated** at any time: `TARGET_REPO=/path/to/target bash bin/setup.sh project-profile`. Discovery is idempotent; if the profile is already complete, it's a no-op.
- **`phase_launchd` now blocks** if the slug has no profile — operators on existing single-project installs must either run `bash bin/setup.sh migrate` (which auto-runs project-profile) or `bash bin/setup.sh project-profile` directly before re-installing launchd.
- **No Linear ticket per operator preference** — this PR carries the brainstorm + plan as in-tree docs.

## Out of scope

- Auto-skip UI stage on backend-only projects (deferred per spec §11 — operator controls UI routing via Linear `stage:*` labels for now).
- Schema versioning beyond v1 (the validator will warn on `schema_version != 1`; v2 is when migration semantics become real).
- A `compound-engineering:document-review`-style multi-persona pass on the generated profiles (would be valuable for high-stakes targets; punt for now).

## 概要

`DiseaseSearchService.applySort` 純関数の骨格を t-wada 流 TDD 三角測量 (2 サイクル) で導入する。
既定ソート (`REVISED_AT_DESC`) と、同 `revisedAt` 衝突時の tie-break 決定論性 (id 降順) を
ユニットテストでドライブし、Drug 側 (#118) と対称な API 契約を確立する。

## 実装サイクル

### Cycle 1: 既定値 (revisedAt 降順、distinct 入力)
- Red: `applySort returns items sorted by revisedAt descending when REVISED_AT_DESC is specified`
  → 素通しスタブで AssertionError を観測
- Green: `items.sortedByDescending { it.revisedAt }`
- コミット: `f870cc5e`

### Cycle 2: tie-break 決定論性 (id 降順、同 revisedAt 衝突)
- Red: `applySort breaks revisedAt ties by id descending`
  → Kotlin stable sort では入力順保持となり AssertionError を観測
- Green: `compareByDescending { it.revisedAt }.thenByDescending { it.id }`
- コミット: `cd62f005`

`tie-break = id 降順` は Issue 本文の Cycle 2 サンプル (#131 / #118 両 Issue 共通) に
明記された推奨仕様と一致させた。

## 完了確認

`./gradlew spotlessCheck detektMain test` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL (16s)。
既存テスト 100% パス + 新規 2 テスト パス、unsorted な振る舞いを保ったまま新規 sort 契約を追加。

## 備考

- `NAME_KANA_ASC` / `ICD10_CHAPTER_ASC` は本 Issue のスコープ外。silent fallback `else -> items` ではなく
  enum exhaustive を保ったまま素通しブランチを残し、後続 sub-issue で triangulation する設計。
- `diseaseWith(id, revisedAt)` テストヘルパは `sampleDisease().copy()` 流用で新設。

Closes #131

# 网页相亲模拟器开发需求

## 项目概述
创建一个有趣的网页相亲模拟器，完全适配手机端浏览器，使用千问API实现智能对话交互。

## 核心功能需求

### 1. 登录与性别选择
- 用户首次进入选择自己的性别（男/女）
- 简洁的UI设计，适配手机屏幕
- 性别选择后进入配对页面

### 2. 随机异性信息卡片生成
根据用户性别，随机生成异性的详细信息卡片，包含：
- **基本信息**：姓名、年龄（25-35岁）、身高、职业
- **性格标签**：如"开朗活泼"、"温柔体贴"、"幽默风趣"、"知性优雅"、"运动健将"、"文艺青年"等
- **兴趣爱好**：3-5个具体的兴趣爱好
- **个性签名**：一句话简介
- **头像**：使用占位图标或emoji表示
- **人设特点**：聊天风格的核心特征（如："喜欢用emoji，说话简短有趣"、"比较内敛，回复较为含蓄"等）

**卡片样式要求**：
- 卡片设计美观，类似交友App的个人资料展示
- 可以左右滑动查看多个随机生成的异性（至少3个选项）
- 点击"开始聊天"按钮进入对话界面

### 3. AI聊天交互系统
**集成千问API**：
- 使用阿里云千问大模型API（Qwen）
- API配置说明需要放在README中，包括如何获取API密钥
- 支持配置文件或环境变量设置API密钥

**聊天特性**：
- 每条AI回复控制在15-50字以内，符合真实聊天节奏
- AI回复风格严格按照所选卡片的人设特点：
  - 性格标签影响语气（活泼/温柔/幽默等）
  - 兴趣爱好会在对话中自然提及
  - 根据人设使用合适频率的emoji
- 对话内容聚焦相亲场景：
  - 初次见面的礼貌寒暄
  - 兴趣爱好交流
  - 工作生活话题
  - 适度的调侃和幽默
  - 避免过于私密或不适当的话题

**对话管理**：
- 记录完整对话历史（本轮会话）
- 对话轮次统计（用于评分）
- 用户可以随时结束相亲，查看评分

### 4. 相亲评分系统
当用户点击"结束相亲"按钮后，展示评分报告：

**评分维度**（总分100分）：
- **话题契合度**（30分）：根据对话内容分析双方兴趣是否匹配
- **互动积极性**（25分）：对话轮次、回复速度、主动性
- **情感温度**（25分）：对话氛围是否愉快、有无尴尬冷场
- **深度交流**（20分）：是否有深入了解彼此

**输出内容**：
- 总体匹配度评分（显著展示）
- 各维度详细得分
- **适合的异性方向推荐**：基于本次对话分析，推荐3-5个适合用户的异性特质标签，例如：
  - "你更适合找一个活泼开朗、能带动气氛的伴侣"
  - "建议寻找有共同兴趣爱好的文艺型对象"
  - "你的沟通风格适合温柔体贴、善于倾听的类型"
- 本次相亲的亮点和改进建议
- 提供"再来一次"按钮重新开始

## 技术实现要求

### 前端技术栈
- **纯HTML + CSS + JavaScript**（单页面应用）
- **移动端优先设计**：
  - 响应式布局，完美适配手机屏幕（320px-428px宽度）
  - 触摸友好的交互设计
  - 避免横向滚动
  - 字体大小适中，易于阅读

### 样式与UI
- 使用现代、清新的配色方案（粉色、紫色等恋爱主题色）
- 卡片式设计风格
- 平滑的动画过渡效果
- 聊天界面模仿主流聊天App（左右气泡样式）

### API集成
- 千问API调用封装
- 错误处理和重试机制
- API密钥安全管理（提供Node.js后端代理）
- 提供简单的Express后端示例用于API中转

### 数据生成逻辑
- 随机姓名生成（中文真实姓名）
- 人设模板库（至少准备10种不同人设组合）
- 确保每次生成的异性卡片有足够的差异性

## 项目文件结构
```
datingweb/
├── index.html              # 主页面
├── css/
│   └── style.css          # 样式文件
├── js/
│   ├── app.js             # 主应用逻辑
│   ├── character.js       # 角色生成逻辑
│   ├── chat.js            # 聊天功能
│   └── scoring.js         # 评分系统
├── server/                # 后端API中转
│   ├── server.js          # Express服务器
│   └── package.json       # 依赖配置
├── config.example.js      # API配置示例
└── README.md              # 项目说明文档
```

## README文档要求
需包含以下内容：
1. 项目简介和功能特性
2. 千问API密钥获取教程（详细步骤）
3. 本地运行步骤（前端+后端）
4. 配置说明（如何填写API密钥）
5. 技术栈说明
6. 目录结构说明
7. 常见问题解答

## 重要功能实现细节

### 角色生成（character.js）
- 创建至少10个不同人设模板
- 随机生成中文姓名（真实常见姓名）
- 职业列表：产品经理、设计师、程序员、医生、教师、摄影师等
- 性格标签池：开朗活泼、温柔体贴、幽默风趣、知性优雅、运动健将、文艺青年、成熟稳重、可爱甜美等
- 兴趣爱好池：旅行、摄影、阅读、健身、美食、音乐、电影、绘画、登山、瑜伽、游泳、烘焙等

### 聊天功能（chat.js）
- 调用后端API与千问对话
- 实现打字动画效果（逐字显示）
- 消息气泡样式（用户右侧蓝色，AI左侧白色）
- 自动滚动到最新消息
- Loading状态显示
- 错误处理和重试

### 评分系统（scoring.js）
- 基于对话轮次、消息长度、关键词匹配等维度计算分数
- 生成个性化的推荐文案
- 美观的评分报告展示（使用进度条或圆形进度图）

### 后端服务器（server/server.js）
- Express框架搭建
- CORS配置
- 千问API调用封装
- 环境变量读取API密钥
- 错误处理中间件
- 请求日志

## 额外加分项
- ✅ 打字动画效果（AI回复时逐字显示）
- ✅ 加载状态提示
- ✅ 平滑的页面切换动画
- ✅ 响应式设计（完美适配所有手机尺寸）
- ✅ 详细的代码注释

## 注意事项
- 确保所有文本内容使用中文
- 代码注释清晰完整
- 保持代码结构清晰易维护
- 注意用户隐私，所有对话数据仅本地存储
- API调用需要做好错误提示
- 测试在不同手机尺寸下的显示效果

## Summary

Issue #6 (テスト戦略の完全欠如) と #10 (CI 不在) を一括解決。

## 追加

- **vitest** (frontend): `src/lsp.test.ts` で `uriToPath` を 5 ケース。`vitest.config.ts` を node 環境に固定。
- **cargo test** (backend): `stack_trace.rs` に `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` を 15 ケース追加 (GCC/GDB/V8/Python/Rust panic、Windows ドライブレター、index 連番、`in_project` 判定、混合書式)。
- **GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): `ubuntu-latest` / `windows-latest` / `macos-latest` の matrix で:
  - rust job: Linux deps インストール → `cargo check --all-targets` → `cargo test --all-targets`
  - frontend job: `npm ci` → `tsc -b` → `npm test` → `vite build`

## tsconfig 簡素化

旧 `tsconfig.json` + `tsconfig.node.json` (composite references) で `tsc -b` が 何故か `src-tauri/tsconfig.json` を読みに行く挙動が出ていたため、references を畳んで単一 tsconfig に統合。`vite.config.ts` と `vitest.config.ts` も include に追加。

## ローカル検証

- \`npm test\` → 5/5 passed
- \`cargo test --all-targets\` → 15/15 passed
- \`npx tsc -b\` → 0 errors
- \`npx vite build\` → ✓ built

Closes #6, closes #10

- Linear-style sectioned packet list — six fixed groups (In Progress / In Review / Backlog / Done / Cancelled / Archived) — replaces the flat packet list in Mission Control.
- Pure render-time grouping. No `lanes` schema changes, no new packet status. Mapping is derived from existing fields (`archivedAt`, `status`, `releaseState`, `queueState`, `lane?.laneId`).
- Empty groups collapse entirely (no `DONE · 0` headers). Per-group open/closed state persists to localStorage at `cortex-ide:mission:group-open:<status>`.

## Where the grouping lives
- `src/components/desktop/thoughts/mission-panel/groupPackets.ts` — `classifyPacketGroup(packet)` + `groupPacketsByStatus(packets)` + the canonical `PACKET_GROUP_ORDER` (defines label + default open state per group).
- `src/components/desktop/thoughts/mission-panel/StatusGroupedLanes.tsx` — section renderer with collapse state, localStorage persistence, cross-tab sync via `storage` event, and a render-prop API so `ThoughtsMissionPanel` keeps owning `PacketCard` / `ComparisonCard` wiring.
- `src/components/desktop/thoughts/ThoughtsMissionPanel.tsx` — the flat `missionState.packets.map(...)` block was extracted into a `renderPacket` callback and the map replaced with `<StatusGroupedLanes packets={...} renderPacket={renderPacket} />`. Comparison-group dedupe `Set` is still tracked at the parent level so multiple section traversals share it.

## Status mapping
- **Archived** — `archivedAt` set OR `status === 'archived'` (manual user action).
- **Done** — `status === 'released'` OR `releaseState === 'released'` (merged).
- **In Review** — `status === 'awaiting_review'`.
- **Backlog** — `queueState === 'draft'` AND no `lane.laneId` (created but not yet dispatched).
- **In Progress** — everything else live (queued/launching/running/idle/recovering/failed/blocked).
- **Cancelled** — never assigned today (no `cancelled` status exists). Section header stays hidden because empty groups collapse; bucket is in place for the eventual cancel flow.

## Section header treatment
- Uppercase Rams-style label in `var(--t-text-muted)` (`fontSize: 11`, `fontWeight: 600`, `letterSpacing: 0.05em`).
- Mono-flavored count badge (`fontFamily: var(--font-mono)`, `fontVariantNumeric: 'tabular-nums'`) inside a pill against `var(--t-divider-subtle)` — matches the existing `IssueGroupList` pattern for visual harmony.
- Chevron rotates `0deg` open / `-90deg` closed with the same 150ms cubic-bezier curve used elsewhere in the panel.
- Sticky `top: 0` so headers pin above their rows during scroll.

## Empty-section behavior
- Renderer counts visible rows after invoking `renderPacket` (a `null` return — e.g. an already-rendered comparison sibling — does NOT count). Sections with 0 visible rows skip rendering entirely. So `Cancelled` is invisible, and `Done` only appears once a packet ships.

## Defaults (per #772 acceptance criteria)
- In Progress + In Review default OPEN.
- Backlog / Done / Cancelled / Archived default CLOSED.

## Caveats
- Comparison cards (`#517` best-of-n) keep their dedupe contract — the `renderedComparisonGroupIds` Set is allocated once per parent render so all section passes share it. No cross-section duplication.
- Cross-tab sync via the `storage` event keeps multiple Mission panels in agreement when an operator toggles a section.
- File ceiling respected: `ThoughtsMissionPanel.tsx` 749 lines, `StatusGroupedLanes.tsx` 195 lines, `groupPackets.ts` 104 lines.

## Test plan
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes (verified locally).
- [ ] `npx eslint` on the three changed/added files passes (verified locally).
- [ ] Visual: open Mission Control with mixed packets — verify all six labels render in fixed order, empty groups hide.
- [ ] Visual: collapse a section, reload the app — collapse state persists.
- [ ] Visual: dispatch a backlog packet — packet jumps from Backlog to In Progress.
- [ ] Visual: approve_and_merge a packet — packet jumps to Done.
- [ ] Visual: comparison group still renders ONE ComparisonCard inside its section, not duplicated.

## Summary

Audit and repair of the corporate View Style Pack catalogue (`STING_VIEW_STYLE_PACKS.json`) and Drawing Types (`STING_DRAWING_TYPES.json`) against the `ViewStylePack` data model and `ViewStylePackApplier` runtime. Three critical defects fixed that were silently dropping graphic overrides on load.

## Key Changes

- **Defect 1a — Silent JSON key drop on line overrides**: Renamed 350+ occurrences of shorthand keys (`projColor`, `projWeight`, `cutColor`, `cutWeight`) to match the `StyleVgOverride` data model (`projectionLineColor`, `projectionLineWeight`, `cutLineColor`, `cutLineWeight`). `Newtonsoft.Json` was silently dropping unknown keys at deserialization, causing every non-visibility override across all packs to be lost.

- **Defect 1b — Nested `appearance` sub-object**: Eight packs incorrectly nested `lineWeightScale`, `textStyleName`, `dimensionStyleName`, and `hatchPalette` under an `appearance` block. Flattened to root level with correct key names (`textStyle`, `dimensionStyle`). Recovered two managed-template packs with intentional 25–50% global line-weight reductions that were never applying.

- **Defect 1c — Missing `viewStylePackId` backfill**: Added `viewStylePackId` references to 11 drawing types in `STING_DRAWING_TYPES.json` to link them to their intended corporate View Style Packs (e.g., `arch-plan-A1-1to100` → `corp-standard-plan`).

- **Research documentation**: Added `docs/DRAWING_VG_RESEARCH.md` (661 lines) — deep-dive on the Drawing Template Manager editor architecture, data model, runtime, and gaps between JSON and AEC drawing standards (BS EN ISO 19650, BS 1192, ISO 13567, NBS, AIA NCS). Documents every field the editor exposes, every Revit API call the applier makes, and the corporate baseline as it ships.

## Implementation Details

- JSON keys validated against `ViewStylePack.cs` (lines 170–176) and `StyleVgOverride` property names.
- All 27 corporate packs and 54 drawing types re-validated post-repair.
- Changelog entry added documenting Phase 165 completion.

### Motivation
- Allow environments without native utilities (e.g. `public_html`) to obtain normalized text from `norma.pdf` by delegating OCR to a remote pipeline defined by `NORM_OCR_PIPELINE_ENDPOINT` and to prevent publishing a norm to production if no usable text exists.

- Integrated remote OCR into the existing fallback chain after `ocrmypdf` and `pdftotext`, and kept persistence of normalized output through the existing `persistNormalizedText` path so `norma.txt` and `metadata.normalized_text` are written on success.

author: vicbravodev
body:
## Summary

Implements the **Notifications** domain (spec 13) end-to-end as PR #1. The domain orchestrates outbound notifications across multiple channels with templates, recipients, deliveries, and preferences. Pipeline:

```
SendNotification (idempotent on team_id+event_key)
  -> SendNotificationJob   (queue: notifications)
  -> DispatchNotification  (resolve recipients -> select channels -> render -> driver -> record attempt -> usage metering)
```

## Models / Tables

- `notifications` (idempotency: unique `team_id` + `event_key`)
- `notification_recipients`
- `notification_deliveries` (dedup: unique `notification_id` + `recipient_id` + `channel_id`)
- `notification_channels`
- `notification_templates`
- `notification_preferences`

All tenant-scoped via `BelongsToTenant`. New `NotificationMeterSeeder` registers the `outbound_notifications` meter and `RecordUsageEvent` is fired per delivery attempt with idempotent event keys (`notif_delivery_{id}` / `notif_retry_{id}_{attempt}` / `notif_fallback_{id}`).

## Channels — implemented vs deferred

| Channel | Driver | Status |
|---------|--------|--------|
| Email | `MailNotificationDriver` (Laravel Mail + `GenericNotificationMail`) | ✅ Full |
| Web (Soketi) | `WebNotificationDriver` + `NotificationPushedBroadcast` on `private-users.{userId}` | ✅ Full |
| SMS / Push / Whatsapp / Slack / Webhook | `NullNotificationDriver` | ⏸ `SPEC-13-CHANNEL-DEFERRED` (PR #2) |

`ChannelDriverRegistry` resolves the driver by `ChannelType` and falls back to the Null driver for deferred channels — pipeline stays exercised end-to-end.

## Cross-domain wiring (string-based listeners)

`NotificationsServiceProvider` registers listeners against FQCN strings so this domain compiles before the parallel specs land:

| Event (FQCN) | Listener | Marker |
|--------------|----------|--------|
| `App\Domains\Incidents\Events\IncidentCreated` | `NotifyOnIncidentCreated` | `SPEC-11-DEFERRED` |
| `App\Domains\Incidents\Events\IncidentStatusChanged` | `NotifyOnIncidentStatusChanged` | `SPEC-11-DEFERRED` |
| `App\Domains\Incidents\Events\IncidentClosed` | `NotifyOnIncidentStatusChanged` | `SPEC-11-DEFERRED` |
| `App\Domains\Automation\Events\ActionExecutionCompleted` | `NotifyOnActionExecutionCompleted` (only `send_email`/`send_sms`/`send_push`/`send_whatsapp` action types) | `SPEC-12-DEFERRED` |

Tests dispatch fakes from `tests/Fakes/` (`FakeIncidentCreatedEvent`, `FakeActionExecutionCompletedEvent`) and re-bind the listeners against those classes to exercise the same handlers without requiring the spec 11/12 code.

`TenantNotificationPoliciesResolver` is bound to a Null implementation with sensible defaults (`SPEC-16-DEFERRED`) until TenantConfig ships `notification_policies` (allowed channels, critical-priority channels, fallback channels, quiet hours).

## Events emitted (FQCN)

- `App\Domains\Notifications\Events\NotificationCreated`
- `App\Domains\Notifications\Events\NotificationDelivered`
- `App\Domains\Notifications\Events\NotificationFailed`
- `App\Domains\Notifications\Events\NotificationPushedBroadcast` (broadcast on `private-users.{userId}` after every successful Web-channel delivery)

## Jobs

All on the `notifications` queue (already in `supervisor-medium` in `config/horizon.php`):

- `SendNotificationJob` — orchestrates the full dispatch.
- `RetryNotificationDeliveryJob` — 5 tries with exponential backoff `[30, 60, 120, 300, 600]`.
- `FallbackNotificationChannelJob` — re-dispatches on the tenant's fallback channel after primary exhaustion.

## Policies + API

- `NotificationPolicy`, `NotificationTemplatePolicy`, `NotificationChannelPolicy`, `NotificationPreferencePolicy` registered via `Gate::policy(...)`.
- New permissions `notifications.view`, `notifications.send`, `notifications.manage` added to `AccessSeeder` for `tenant_admin`/`supervisor`/`monitorista`/`viewer` roles.
- API endpoints (all under `/{current_team}/notifications/...`, with `EnsureTeamMembership` + `throttle:api` + `$this->authorize(...)` per action):
  - `GET /notifications`, `POST /notifications/send`, `GET /notifications/{notification}`
  - `GET|POST /notifications/templates`, `PUT /notifications/templates/{template}`
  - `GET /notifications/channels`, `PUT /notifications/channels/{channel}`
  - `GET|PUT /notifications/preferences`

## Tests (23 new feature tests)

- `NotificationsTenantIsolationTest` — tenant scope on notifications, recipients, deliveries.
- `RenderNotificationContentTest` — template rendering with `{{ $var }}` interpolation; fallback to `subject`/`body_preview` when no template.
- `SendNotificationTest` — record creation, job dispatch, idempotency on `team_id` + `event_key`.
- `DispatchNotificationTest` — full email pipeline with `Mail::fake()`; delivery dedup; critical multi-channel fan-out; web channel `NotificationPushedBroadcast`; muted preference suppression.
- `CrossDomainListenersTest` — string-based listeners react to fake spec-11/spec-12 events; non-notification action types ignored; idempotent on duplicate dispatches.
- `NotificationControllerTest` — index/show, send endpoint dispatching `SendNotificationJob`, cross-tenant blocking.
- `RetryAndFallbackTest` — retry job marks delivered, exponential backoff config, fallback creates delivery on alternate channel.
- `SendNotificationJobTest` — queue routing, no-op on missing notification, delegates to `DispatchNotification`.

Full suite: **416 tests / 1004 assertions / 9.0s** with coverage thresholds (Tier 1 95% per-file, Tier 2 80% aggregate, Global 75%) all green.

## Order of merge

This PR depends on nothing in the parallel set. Recommended merge after specs **10**, **11**, **12**, and **16** so the deferred markers (`SPEC-10/11/12/16-DEFERRED`) can be replaced with real bindings without intermediate churn. Each marker is grep-able for the cleanup pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent`
- [x] `php artisan test --compact tests/Feature/Domains/Notifications` (23 passed)
- [x] Full suite `php artisan test --coverage-clover=coverage.xml --compact` (416 passed) + coverage thresholds pass
- [ ] CI green

## Summary

The `fmtlog` plugin lived at the top of the repo, alongside `plugins/`, while every other LogLayer plugin (`redact`, `sampling`, `datadogtrace`, `oteltrace`) lived under `plugins/`. The docs grouped fmtlog under "Available Plugins" and linked to `/plugins/fmtlog`, but the actual import path was bare `go.loglayer.dev/fmtlog` — so users saw the page in the Plugins sidebar, copied the install line, and ended up with an inconsistent import relative to its neighbours.

This PR aligns code layout and import path with the rest of the plugin family. The package stays bundled in the main module (no separate `go.mod`), matching `plugins/redact` and `plugins/sampling`.

## Changes

- `fmtlog/{fmtlog.go,fmtlog_test.go}` → `plugins/fmtlog/...` (`git mv`)

## Behaviour

Unchanged — same package name (`fmtlog`), same `fmtlog.New()` constructor, same `MessageHook` semantics. **Only the import path changes.**

## Breaking change

The fmtlog plugin's import path changes from `go.loglayer.dev/fmtlog` to `go.loglayer.dev/plugins/fmtlog`. Update imports accordingly. Acceptable now because v1.0.x just released and there are no known users yet.

body:
## Summary

Fixes the Claude 4 routing bug discovered in the AI model audit: when users picked "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Latest)" from the admin UI, the Cloud Function silently fell back to \`claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022\` (October 2024) — users got 3.5-era quality while paying for and expecting 4.6.

## Root cause

The model-mapping logic in \`functions/index.js\` only had branches for \`haiku\` and \`opus\`. The UI sent \`"claude-4-sonnet"\` / \`"claude-4-sonnet-latest"\`, which doesn't include either keyword, so it dropped through to the default \`claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022\`.

## Fix

Added a Claude 4 family branch checked **before** the legacy haiku/opus checks. Any model string containing \`claude-4\`, \`sonnet-4\`, \`haiku-4\`, or \`opus-4\` is now routed to the current GA Claude 4 model IDs:

| Selector contains | Routes to |
|---|---|
| \`haiku\` | \`claude-haiku-4-5\` |
| \`opus\` | \`claude-opus-4-7\` |
| else | \`claude-sonnet-4-6\` (default for Claude 4 family) |

Model IDs verified against the Anthropic SDK skill catalog — used as-is, **no date suffixes** (per skill guidance: "Do not append date suffixes").

## Verification
