body:
## Summary
- **Worktree-aware**: hook resolves `biome`/`tsc` against the main repo's `node_modules` so a fresh worktree without `npm install` works without slow `npx` download fallback paths.
- **Change-aware**: parses git's stdin ref tuples, diffs the push range, and skips firmware checks on TS-only pushes (and TS checks on firmware-only pushes).
- **Parallel**: independent checks run concurrently via `&` + `wait`; output captured to a temp dir and reported together at the end.
- **Faster firmware**: `firmware/check-build-warnings.sh` auto-uses Ninja (separate `build-ninja/` dir, doesn't fight `make build`) and ccache when installed (`CCACHE_BASEDIR=<worktree-root>` so cache hits cross worktrees with identical source). `cppcheck -j N` parallelizes the lint.

## Why
Old hook unconditionally ran ~100s of checks (CMake reconfigure alone = 92.7s for ARM toolchain detection) on every push — including TS-only PRs. New worktrees were the worst case: every first push paid the full configure + build cost. With the new hook, a non-firmware push finishes in ~2s; a firmware-touching push finishes in seconds when `build-ninja/` is warm.

## Verification
All CI checks (lint, typecheck, test:ts, test:firmware, codegen:check) pass locally:
- `biome check .` → 110 files, no fixes (1.2s)
- `tsc --noEmit` → clean
- `npm run test:ts` → 289 passed
- `make -C firmware test` → 139 passed
- `make -C firmware format-check` → clean
- `make -C firmware lint` → clean (parallel cppcheck, ~2s wall)
- `firmware/check-build-warnings.sh` → 0 warnings, 0 CMake warnings

End-to-end push (this PR) ran the new hook in 2s with TS checks correctly skipped for the firmware-touching commit.

## Test plan
- [x] Hook script syntax-checks (`bash -n`)
- [x] TS-only diff → only `biome` + `tsc` run
- [x] Firmware-only diff → only firmware checks run (verified on this PR's push)
- [x] No-op diff (docs/markdown only) → all checks skipped, `nothing to verify` message
- [x] Empty stdin (manual run) → `Scope: unknown` and runs everything
- [x] Bash 3.2 compatible (no `declare -A`, empty arrays guarded with `${arr[@]+...}`)
- [ ] CI green on this PR

## Notes
- Repo policy still forbids `--no-verify`; this PR doesn't change that.
- For ~10x firmware speedup on fresh worktrees: `brew install ccache` (the script auto-detects).

author: walle250ai
body:
## Problem

`ToInt8E(128)` silently returned `-128` with no error, and `ToInt16E(32768)` silently returned `-32768`. These are silent integer overflow wraps caused by unchecked narrowing casts from wider signed integer types.

The `toNumber` function converted signed integers with bare `T(s)` casts, which wraps in Go rather than signalling overflow. The `parseInt` function already used the correct `bitSize` per type (added in the previous fix for unsigned types), so string-based parsing was correct — only numeric-to-numeric conversion was affected.

## Changes

- **`int64Overflow[T Number](v int64) bool`** — new helper that returns true when `v` falls outside the representable range of `T` (int8, int16, int32, int64, int).
- **`toNumber`** — added `int64Overflow` gate before every signed-integer cast (`int`, `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`), returning `(0, false)` on overflow so callers fall through to proper error reporting.
- **`number_test.go`** — extended `generateNumberTestCases` to run underflow/overflow string cases for signed integer types (`isSint || isUint`), matching the existing coverage for unsigned types.

## Tests

```
ok  github.com/spf13/cast  2.229s
```

All existing tests pass; new overflow edge-cases for `int8`/`int16`/`int32`/`int64`/`int` are now exercised.

author: sebasnallar
body:
Two layered fixes for the case where a pod's container has died but the log workflow returns nothing:

1. kube-logger-go now fetches the previous container instance's logs (PodLogOptions.Previous) on the first page for any pod whose application container has restarted or has a terminated last state. The kubelet retains exactly one prior instance per container, so this surfaces the crash output that `kubectl logs` alone hides while the replacement container is starting. Previous-container fetching is gated on the absence of a per-pod pagination cursor, so paginated requests stay unchanged: no extra round-trips, no duplicated lines (the existing timestamp-based dedup in processor handles overlap), and no token format change.

2. Deployment template flips terminationMessagePolicy from File to FallbackToLogsOnError on the application and traffic containers. When the file at /dev/termination-log is empty and the container exits non-zero, the kubelet auto-populates status.containerStatuses[].lastState.terminated.message with the tail (~80 kB) of stdout/stderr, which survives container restarts inside the Pod object itself. Apps that already write to the termination file are unaffected.

Together these cover CrashLoopBackOff and recently-terminated containers without any new in-cluster tooling. Pods that have been fully garbage-collected still require an external log aggregator.

author: steggl
body:
Closes #11. Adds the full Zod-validated configuration loader. ADR-0024
records the four bundled design decisions.

## What

A turbocharger deployment can now configure all six config objects
through:

1. Environment variables (`TURBOCHARGER_*`, double-underscore for
   nesting, comma for arrays)
2. A YAML or JSON config file (path from `TURBOCHARGER_CONFIG`)
3. Hard-coded defaults (just `port=11435`)

Precedence: env > file > defaults. Validation is aggregated — every
issue is reported in one error message so operators fix all of them
in one edit.

## Key decisions (ADR-0024)

- **Source of truth.** TypeScript interfaces in `src/types.ts`
  remain authoritative. Zod schemas validate against them.
- **YAML and JSON.** Both supported; extension decides parser.
- **Env-overrides-file.** 12-factor precedence; works with
  immutable container images.
- **Hard rename.** `TURBO_*` env-var prefix is gone; `TURBOCHARGER_*`
  is the only one recognised. No alias, no deprecation period —
  pre-v0.1, exactly the right time to break.

## New runtime dependencies

`zod@^4.3.6`, `yaml@^2.8.3`. Total runtime deps: 4 (still <5).

## Test count

223 → 291 passed (+22 env, +28 schema, +18 load).

## Bugs found mid-implementation

Two type-system collisions and one snake_case quirk surfaced when
the patches first hit your repo. All are documented in commit
messages:

- `fix(config): align schemas with exactOptionalPropertyTypes` —
  Zod's `T | undefined` encoding clashes with the project's strict
  optional-property mode. Resolved by dropping the explicit
  `z.ZodType<X>` annotations and adding mapper helpers in load.ts.
- `fix(config): preserve snake_case keys inside orchestrator.weights` —
  the YAML normalizer was too aggressive. `tool_error` and
  `syntax_error` are `SignalCategory` data values, not structural
  keys, and the schema expects them verbatim.

The mid-flow fixes are kept as separate commits in the PR history
rather than squashed: future maintainers reading the log can see
the actual sequence of constraints.

## Out of scope

- Per-request header overrides (Issue #12)
- Schema export for IDE autocomplete (post-MVP)
- SIGHUP config reload (post-MVP)
- LLM critic's runtime callable — the loader populates the static
  `LlmCriticConfig` side; operators inject the `LlmCritic` callable
  in code (mirrors the existing src/types.ts split)
``

author: falfab
body:
## Summary

`RosActionNode::cancelGoal()` calls `async_get_result()` and `async_cancel_goal()` on the `rclcpp_action` client without exception handling. When the action server completes the cancel handshake before the BT thread reaches those calls, the client's result callback has already erased the goal from its internal registry (`goal_handles_.erase(...)` inside the `make_result_aware` lambda in `rclcpp_action/client.hpp`). Both calls then throw `rclcpp_action::exceptions::UnknownGoalHandleError` (`"Goal handle is not known to this client."`), which escapes `halt()`, lands in `TreeExecutionServer`'s top-level `catch(const std::exception&)`, and causes the outer `/bt_execution` goal to be **aborted** instead of **canceled**. Downstream code that distinguishes `SUCCESS / CANCELED / ABORTED` ends up with the wrong signal on a clean operator cancel.

Closes #18. Also addresses the duplicate report in #110.

## Change

Wrap the three calls in `cancelGoal()` with a narrow `try { ... } catch (const rclcpp_action::exceptions::UnknownGoalHandleError& e) { RCLCPP_DEBUG(...) }`.

The catch is intentionally narrow:

- **Only `UnknownGoalHandleError` is caught.** Any other exception coming out of `rclcpp_action` (network-layer RCL errors, invalid handle, etc.) is still propagated. Those are real bugs and should continue to fail loudly.
- **The pre-accept path is untouched.** @robin-mueller raised a legitimate concern in #57 / #53 that users may *want* to observe `cancelGoal()` failing when the goal response has not arrived yet. That case goes through the existing `if (!goal_handle_)` branch (`RCLCPP_WARN("cancelGoal called on an empty goal_handle")`), which this PR does not change. The new catch only fires on the `goal_handle_`-populated path, i.e. after the server has already terminated the goal.

## Test

Adds a gtest regression under `behaviortree_ros2/test/` that reproduces the race:

- Fake action server with a detached thread that waits up to ~50 ms for a cancel request, then synchronously calls `goal_handle->canceled(result)`.
- BT leaf subclass of `RosActionNode<Sleep>`.
- Test ticks the tree until the server has accepted the goal, then calls `tree.haltTree()` and asserts no exception leaks.

Verified by stashing the source fix and re-running the test: without the patch it terminates with `"Goal handle is not known to this client."`, the exact throw this PR fixes. With the patch it passes in ~220 ms.

This is also the first gtest added to the repo. Happy to adjust naming / layout conventions if you have a preference.

## Prior art

- Same fix shape has been used downstream for a while, e.g. @ErickKramer's fork (`ErickKramer/BehaviorTree.ROS2@2fdf4a5`), confirmed working through 2025 by @tropappar (in #18).
- #53 fixed the *pre-accept* null-handle case; this PR fixes the *post-result-erase* race, which is a different code path.

author: nedseb
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #164 — fixes the actual symptom Aline reported.

PlatformIO's native env only compiles in `compile_commands.json` what the smoke-test sketch (`src/main.cpp`) pulls in via LDF. Drivers not referenced by `main.cpp` don't end up in the database, so clang-tidy falls back to default flags when it processes their `.cpp` files. That means a header that legitimately includes another driver's public API (e.g. `daplink_flash.h` → `daplink_bridge.h`) fails with `file not found` even when both libs ship a proper `library.properties` and the consumer declares `depends=`.

The fix: pass `--extra-arg-before=-I<lib>/src` for every driver to the clang-tidy invocation so the include path is uniform across the lint regardless of compile_commands.json coverage.

## Why a follow-up rather than part of #164

The diagnostic only surfaced when reproducing on Aline's `feat/daplink-flash-driver` branch after #164 had already landed. On `main` today only HTS221 and WSEN-PADS exist, neither has cross-driver deps, and `main.cpp` includes HTS221 — so `make tidy` is green. The bug is latent until the first real cross-driver pair lands (DAPLink), which is exactly Aline's case.

## Verified locally

Reproduced Aline's failure on her branch, applied this fix, ran `make tidy` end-to-end:

```
[1/4] Processing file lib/daplink_flash/src/daplink_flash.cpp.
[2/4] Processing file lib/wsen-pads/src/WSEN_PADS.cpp.
[3/4] Processing file lib/daplink_bridge/src/daplink_bridge.cpp.
[4/4] Processing file lib/hts221/src/HTS221.cpp.
exit=0
```

Each `.cpp` is processed without the `daplink_bridge.h: file not found` error. Same `make tidy` on current `main` (no cross-driver deps yet) stays green.

## Note for downstream

There's a stale branch `tooling/library-properties` on origin that I accidentally re-pushed when this commit was on it (the original branch was deleted by GitHub on merge of #164, my push recreated it). Safe to delete from the GitHub UI — its content is exactly this PR's diff.

body:
Part of #1443.

Extracts the duplicated `Casing` type into a new public `src/utils/types.ts` so it can be imported once and reused across modules — and so consumers can pre-construct typed arguments before passing them to faker methods.

## Changes

- New `src/utils/types.ts` exporting `Casing = 'upper' | 'lower' | 'mixed'` with JSDoc.
- `src/modules/string/index.ts` and `src/modules/color/index.ts` no longer declare their own `Casing`; both now `import type { Casing } from '../../utils/types'`.
- `src/modules/finance/bitcoin.ts` re-points its `Casing` import from `../string` to `../../utils/types`.
- `src/index.ts` re-exports `Casing` from `./types` instead of from `./modules/color`.
- Apidocs snapshot updated to reflect the unified union order (`'upper' | 'lower' | 'mixed'`), which matches the existing `switch (casing)` order in both modules.

- No runtime behavior change — type-only refactor.
- Public API surface is unchanged: `Casing` is still exported from the package root.

author: germanocaumo
body:
### What does this PR do?
Remove video sources from the EDL during long PTS gaps so ffmpeg does not process/fill those ranges while rendering. This avoids excessive memory usage for recordings with large timestamp gaps in video streams.

It uses the same code as audio (added in https://github.com/bigbluebutton/bigbluebutton/pull/24776).

The min gap for removal used for video is set as 30 seconds instead because with 60 we still saw ffmpeg memory going over 2GB+ of usage in some recordings.

author: volta2030
body:
This pull request streamlines the workflow for handling UTXO files in the `create_transaction.py` script. The main improvement is automating the removal of input UTXO files using `git rm` after a transaction, reducing manual steps and potential for user error.

**Automation of UTXO file handling:**

* The script now automatically runs `git rm` on input UTXO files after writing output UTXOs, instead of just prompting the user to do so manually. If any removal fails, a warning is displayed.
* Updated the user prompt to clarify that both writing output files and removing input UTXOs will be performed automatically.
* Added the `subprocess` import to support running `git rm` commands from within the script.

**User experience improvements:**

* The instructions shown to the user after file operations have been updated to reflect the new automation and clarify the next steps.

body:
### Motivation
- Owners were not receiving real-time `notification` events because the frontend emitted `join` with `user.id` while backend emits target the Mongo `ownerId` (stored as `user._id`), causing sockets to join the wrong/empty room.

### Description
- Updated `SocketContext.jsx` to compute `userRoomId = user?._id || user?.id`, only emit `join` when a valid id exists, and added `_id`/`id` to the `useEffect` dependencies so the socket re-joins when the effective id changes.

author: tedd-an
body:
The Bluetooth host decides whether to download firmware by reading the
controller firmware download completion flag and firmware version
information.

If a USB error occurs during the firmware download process (for example
due to a USB disconnect), the download is aborted immediately. An
incomplete firmware transfer does not cause the controller to set the
download completion flag, but the firmware version information may be
updated at an early stage of the download process.

In this case, after USB reconnection, the host attempts to re-download
the firmware because the download completion flag is not set. However,
since the controller reports the same firmware version as the target
firmware, the download is skipped. This ultimately results in the
firmware not being properly updated on the controller.

This change removes the restriction that skips firmware download when
the versions are equal. It covers scenarios where the USB connection
can be disconnected at any time and ensures that firmware download can
be retriggered after USB reconnection, allowing the Bluetooth firmware
to be correctly and completely updated.

author: chrisye96
body:
## Summary

CI's `npm ci` was failing with:

```
Missing: @emnapi/core@1.10.0 from lock file
Missing: @emnapi/runtime@1.10.0 from lock file
```

These are platform-specific optional native deps pulled transitively (likely via lightningcss / vite native bits). When the lock file was generated on Windows, npm 11 omitted Linux-only resolution entries; npm ci on Ubuntu then refused to install.

## Fix

- Wipe `node_modules` + `package-lock.json`, regenerate with `npm install --include=optional --force` so every platform variant of every optional dep lands in the lock file.
- Bump CI Node from 20 to 22 (current LTS, aligns with local dev runtime).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm ci` succeeds locally on Windows
- [x] `npm run test:run` -> 148/148
- [ ] CI run on this PR completes green
- [ ] After merge, master CI passes for next push

author: alint77
body: ## Summary This PR adds a DDP Track_3_optimization training script (#263) and updates the optimizer setup for the optimization benchmark. The main change is a hybrid optimizer: - I'm using Muon and Normuon from the Microsoft Dion repo since it's much more optimized in terms of throughput and also I'm a contributor. - Attention Q/K/V/O matrices use Muon. - MLP up/down matrices use NorMuon. - Both Muon and NorMuon use cautious weight decay. - MLP NorMuon uses a more aggressive learning rate than the original Muon baseline. - The script uses Flash Attention 3 on H100 when the kernel is available, with PyTorch SDPA as a fallback. - The script logs per-step timing and MFU estimates for H100 NVL. - The script captures a short PyTorch profiler trace. ## Result This run reaches the target before the final validation point: - Step 3375: validation loss `3.27842` - Step 3500: validation loss `3.27400` The previous Track 3 Muon baseline reached: - Step 3375: validation loss `3.28126` - Step 3500: validation loss `3.27673` So this run beats the baseline at step 3375 and finishes with a lower final validation loss, I might be able to push it down to 3325 or so, might try later when have access to more compute. ## Optimizer Details AdamW is still used for embeddings, the final projection, and scalar parameters. Attention matrices use Muon with: - `lr=0.025` - `weight_decay=0.0125` - `mu=0.95` - `nesterov=True` - `adjust_lr="spectral_norm"` MLP matrices use NorMuon with: - MLP up: `lr=0.030`, `weight_decay=0.025` - MLP down: `lr=0.060`, `weight_decay=0.0125` - `mu=0.95` - `muon_beta2=0.9` - `nesterov=True` - `cautious_wd=True` - `adjust_lr="spectral_norm"` The motivation is to keep attention close to the strong Muon baseline, while applying NorMuon where it is most likely to help: the large rectangular MLP matrices.

author: tedd-an
body:
hci_le_big_sync_established_evt() currently does:

    conn->num_bis = 0;
    memset(conn->bis, 0, sizeof(conn->num_bis));

sizeof(conn->num_bis) is wrong - it would make sense to either use
conn->num_bis (before setting that to 0) or sizeof(conn->bis).
Fix it by using sizeof(conn->bis), the least intrusive change.

Luckily, nothing actually depends on this memset() working properly:
Nothing seems to ever read from conn->bis beyond conn->num_bis, and when
conn->num_bis is increased, the corresponding elements of conn->bis are
initialized. So I think this line could also just be removed.

This is a purely theoretical fix and should have no impact on actual
behavior.

Fixes: 42ecf1947135 ("Bluetooth: ISO: Do not emit LE BIG Create Sync if previous is pending")
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>

author: zerego
body:
## Summary

Layer 1 of [PROD-7169](https://linear.app/lightdash/issue/PROD-7169) — prevent Slack scheduled deliveries from failing with `invalid_blocks` by validating Block Kit constraints before posting. When a constraint can't be met, the dropped element is replaced with an inline warning so the user knows what happened and how to recover (open in Lightdash) instead of silently losing content.

Linear: [PROD-7209](https://linear.app/lightdash/issue/PROD-7209)

### What `invalid_blocks` is

Slack rejects any `chat.postMessage` whose payload violates Block Kit limits — too many blocks (max 50), section text > 3000 chars, button/image URLs > 3000 chars, malformed mrkdwn, etc. Today the user sees the literal `invalid_blocks` string in scheduler logs and the entire delivery is lost. This PR closes the most common failure modes.

### What changed

`packages/backend/src/clients/Slack/SlackMessageBlocks.ts`:

- New `safeUrl(url, maxLen)` — returns `undefined` when a URL is > 3000 chars, malformed, or non-http(s). Applied to every `accessory.button.url`, `actions.elements.button.url`, and `image_url` site across all 6 builders.
- New `sanitizeHeaderText(text)` — returns `undefined` for empty/whitespace titles so the header block is dropped instead of emitting a single space.
- New `unavailableSection(message)` — renders `:warning: …` in place of a dropped block so the user sees what happened (with a CTA: open in Lightdash).
- Dashboard CSV deliveries with > 35 charts now collapse into a **single grouped section** with each filename rendered as a clickable mrkdwn `<url|filename>` link, plus a `+ N more — open in Lightdash …` summary line. Char budget keeps the section under the 3000-char limit and never truncates mid-link.
- Per-chart rows whose download URL is invalid render as `:warning: <filename> — download unavailable. Open in Lightdash to access this result.` (no button) so a single bad URL no longer brings down the whole message.

`packages/backend/src/clients/Slack/SlackMessageBlocks.test.ts` (new) — 18 unit tests covering: block-count cap, mrkdwn link embedding, invalid-URL handling, warning messages, header sanitisation, and regression coverage of the typical inputs.

No DB / API / frontend changes.

## Before / After

### 1. Dashboard CSV with too many charts (the production trigger)

**Before** — 60-chart dashboard:
> Slack rejects the whole post with `invalid_blocks` (60+ section blocks > 50 cap). User gets nothing; scheduler log shows literal `invalid_blocks`.

**After** — same 60-chart dashboard:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Sales overview — daily delivery                        │  ← header
│                                                          │
│  name              description                          │  ← fields
│  Sales overview    Daily snapshot of pipeline           │
│                                                  [Open] │
│                                                          │
│  ▪ revenue-by-region.csv   ← clickable mrkdwn link      │  ← collapsed
│  ▪ deals-by-stage.csv      ← clickable                  │     section
│  ▪ pipeline-velocity.csv   ← clickable                  │     (one block)
│  …                                                       │
│  + 35 more — open in Lightdash to access all downloads. │
│                                                  [Open] │
│                                                          │
│  This is a scheduled delivery every day at 9 AM ...     │  ← context
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
~5 blocks total, well under Slack's 50-block cap. Delivery succeeds, every visible filename is a clickable download link to its S3 URL, and the "+ N more" CTA points to the dashboard's Lightdash URL.

### 2. Chart CSV where the presigned download URL is too long

**Before**: Slack rejects with `invalid_blocks` → delivery fails entirely.

**After**:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Weekly revenue                                          │
│                                                          │
│  name              description                          │
│  Weekly revenue    YoY revenue by week           [Open] │
│                                                          │
│  ⚠️ Download link unavailable for this delivery (the    │  ← warning
│  URL was too long or invalid). Open in Lightdash to     │     replaces
│  download.                                               │     dropped
│                                                          │     button
│  This is a scheduled delivery every Monday ...          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 3. Chart image where the image URL is malformed/too long

**Before**: Slack rejects with `invalid_blocks` → no message at all.

**After**:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Conversion funnel                                       │
│                                                          │
│  name              description                          │
│  Conversion funnel Step-by-step drop-off          [Open] │
│                                                          │
│  ⚠️ Chart preview unavailable (the image URL was too    │  ← warning
│  long or invalid). Open in Lightdash to view.           │     replaces
│                                                          │     image
│  This is a scheduled delivery every Monday ...          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 4. Dashboard CSV with one bad row (mixed)

Only the bad row gets the warning suffix; the others keep their download buttons.

**After**:
```
  ▪ revenue-by-region.csv                       [Download]
  ⚠️ deals-by-stage.csv — download unavailable.
     Open in Lightdash to access this result.
  ▪ pipeline-velocity.csv                       [Download]
```

## Layered fix

This PR is one of four sub-tickets under PROD-7169. Together they make `invalid_blocks` rare and recoverable:

- **PROD-7209 (this PR) — Prevention** in `SlackMessageBlocks.ts`.
- **PROD-7210 — Fallback** in `SlackClient.postMessage`: retry once with text-only payload on `invalid_blocks`.
- **PROD-7211 — Friendly error** in `SchedulerTask.ts`: translate the raw error in the scheduler log.
- **PROD-7212 — Diagnostics**: structured breadcrumbs in the existing warn log so we can confirm causes from production.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm -F backend test src/clients/Slack/SlackMessageBlocks.test.ts` — 18 passing
- [x] `pnpm -F backend test src/clients/Slack/ src/scheduler/ src/services/UnfurlService/` — 33 passing (no regressions)
- [x] `pnpm -F backend typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm -F backend linter src/clients/Slack/SlackMessageBlocks*.ts` — clean
- [ ] Manual: trigger a dashboard CSV delivery with >35 charts in local dev, confirm the collapsed section renders with clickable links

author: jvs1328
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a major schema refactor from a flat season structure to a hierarchical v2 model where events contain seasons, with a centralized unit registry at the event level. It includes a new Elo rating engine with Bayesian-shrunk historical adjustments and comprehensive migration support for legacy data.

## Key Changes

- **New `eventStore.js`**: Defines v2 schema structure with:
  - Event-level unit registry replacing flat unit lists
  - Centralized Elo system and config defaults
  - Factory functions for creating default events, seasons, and app state
  - Migration logic (`migrateLegacyFlatToV2`) to wrap legacy flat-shape data into v2 hierarchy
  - Unit name slugification and registry building with collision handling
  - Balancer settings migration with field renames (gapWeight → regimentCountWeight, minDiffWeight → rangeSimilarityWeight)

- **New `eloEngine.js`**: Complete Elo rating system featuring:
  - Chronological replay engine that processes rounds in (season, week, round) order
  - Per-unit Elo ratings with provisional K-factor support
  - Map-side and unit-on-map-side history tracking (wins, losses, casualties)
  - Bayesian-shrunk Elo-equivalent adjustments based on historical win rates
  - Expected win probability computation with configurable map/unit weight and prior regularization
  - Support for flipped rosters, per-round swaps, and playoff/single-round lead modes
  - USA attacker map definitions for side derivation

- **Updated `shareSeason.js`**: Added v2 payload creation functions:
  - `createV2SeasonPayload()` for sharing individual seasons as plain JSON
  - `createV2EventPayload()` for sharing complete event trees (registry + all seasons)
  - Maintains v1 tuple-compacted format for backward compatibility

- **Refactored `SeasonTracker.jsx`**: Significant restructuring to work with v2 hierarchy (detailed changes in binary diff)

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Elo shrinkage**: Historical rates are converted to Elo equivalents and shrunk toward 0 using `total / (total + priorRounds)` to prevent noise in thin samples
- **Unit registry**: Built from all unit names across seasons/weeks with automatic slug-based ID generation and collision suffixes (-2, -3, etc.)
- **Legacy compatibility**: Migration strips removed bias fields (mapBiases, eloBiasPercentages) and preserves all season data in the new structure
- **Player count resolution**: Falls back through week override → season default → 25 for weighting Elo averages
- **In-game sides**: Derived from roster team + flip flag, enabling proper casualty and lead attribution to USA/CSA sides

author: jamesadevine
body:
## Summary

Adds `awf_path_prepends()` to the `CompilerExtension` trait so extensions can declare directories that should be on PATH inside the AWF chroot. The Lean runtime uses this to make `lean`, `lake`, and `elan` discoverable without absolute paths.

## Problem

After PR #354 added the `$HOME/.elan` AWF mount, the agent could access Lean binaries at `~/.elan/bin/lean` — but `lean` wasn't on PATH. The agent had to do an extra step (`which lean` fails → `~/.elan/bin/lean -h` works) before it could use Lean.

**Root cause:** `sudo` resets PATH via `secure_path`. AWF reconstructs PATH internally from `process.env.PATH` (post-sudo, missing elan). On GitHub Actions, AWF reads the `$GITHUB_PATH` file to recover lost paths, but no equivalent existed for ADO.

## Solution

- New `CompilerExtension::awf_path_prepends()` trait method — extensions declare bin directories to inject into the chroot PATH
- `LeanExtension` returns `["$HOME/.elan/bin"]`
- New `generate_awf_path_step()` generates a dedicated pipeline step ("Generate GITHUB_PATH file") that writes path entries to a file and sets `GITHUB_PATH` via `##vso[task.setvariable]`
- AWF natively reads `$GITHUB_PATH` at startup and merges entries into the chroot PATH

Generated step (when Lean is enabled):

```yaml
- bash: |
    AWF_PATH_FILE="/tmp/awf-tools/ado-path-entries"
    echo "$HOME/.elan/bin" >> "$AWF_PATH_FILE"
    echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=GITHUB_PATH]$AWF_PATH_FILE"
  displayName: "Generate GITHUB_PATH file"
```

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/compile/extensions/mod.rs` | `awf_path_prepends()` trait method + macro dispatch |
| `src/runtimes/lean/extension.rs` | Returns `["$HOME/.elan/bin"]` |
| `src/compile/common.rs` | `generate_awf_path_step()` + tests |
| `src/compile/standalone.rs` | Wire up replacement |
| `src/compile/onees.rs` | Wire up replacement |
| `src/data/base.yml` | `{{ awf_path_step }}` marker |
| `src/data/1es-base.yml` | `{{ awf_path_step }}` marker |
| `src/compile/extensions/tests.rs` | Trait + Lean tests |
| `docs/extending.md` | Add method to trait listing |
| `docs/template-markers.md` | Document `{{ awf_path_step }}` |

## Testing

- All 1012 tests pass
- Clippy clean (no new warnings)
- New tests for `awf_path_prepends()` default + Lean impl, and `generate_awf_path_step()` with/without Lean

### Motivation
- Replace the local JPA `PlayerRepository` persistence with a PocketBase-backed API so player records are stored and managed in a PocketBase collection.
- Centralize remote PocketBase interactions and XML-to-entity mapping in the `NbaApiService` to support both XML export and CRUD operations.
- Surface PocketBase record IDs in API responses while hiding the internal DB primary key from external JSON.

### Description

author: fderuiter
body:
🚨 **Severity:** MEDIUM
💡 **Vulnerability:** Unrestricted client-side image file uploads in `LogoControls.tsx` and `BorderControls.tsx`. Because `FileReader.readAsDataURL()` loads the entire file into a base64 string in memory, uploading massive files (e.g., multi-gigabyte ISOs) could freeze or crash the user's browser tab. Furthermore, unsupported file types could lead to unexpected rendering behavior.
🎯 **Impact:** Client-side Denial of Service (DoS) via resource exhaustion, resulting in a degraded user experience.
🔧 **Fix:** Implemented a new `validateImageUpload` utility in `src/utils/security.ts` to strictly enforce a 2MB file size limit and an allowlist of MIME types (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, `image/svg+xml`). Integrated this check into `LogoControls` and `BorderControls` before `FileReader` is invoked, and added UI state to surface validation errors clearly to the user.
✅ **Verification:** Ran `pnpm test` and verified that the newly added `validateImageUpload` tests pass, and existing style control tests succeed. UI logic cleanly bails out and sets the error state when an invalid file is selected.

author: rtissera
body:
## Summary

Adds the C-side primitives Megadrive Studio needs for single-step, execution breakpoints, memory watchpoints, and live Z80 visibility. All hooks are additive; vanilla libretro frontends see no behaviour change because the new fields default to zero (BSS-init).

### clown68000 (via submodule bump)

- `volatile cc_bool halt_request` on `Clown68000_State`, set/cleared via `Clown68000_RequestHalt` / `Clown68000_ClearHaltRequest`.
- `Clown68000_BreakpointCallback bp_cb` checked before every instruction fetch. Non-zero return halts the dispatch loop.
- `Clown68000_WatchpointCallback wp_cb` stored on the state, fired by the bus glue (`M68kReadCallback` / `M68kWriteCallback` in clownmdemu-core's `bus-main-m68k.c`) on every bus access. Non-zero return raises `halt_request` so the dispatch loop bails at the next instruction boundary.

### libretro-interface (new memory IDs)

| ID     | Name                    | Layout                                         |
|--------|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| 0x105  | `LIBRA_MEMORY_Z80_RAM`  | 8 KiB raw Z80 RAM ($A00000-$A01FFF)            |
| 0x108  | `LIBRA_MEMORY_Z80_BUS`  | `unsigned char`: bit 0 = bus_requested, bit 1 = reset_held |
| 0x109  | `LIBRA_MEMORY_DEBUG_API`| `struct libra_md_debug_api` of fn pointers     |

`libra_md_debug_api` exposes `request_halt`, `clear_halt_request`, `set_breakpoint_callback(cb, userdata)`, `set_watchpoint_callback(cb, userdata)`.

### Why memory-ID 0x109 (Option B) instead of a new RETRO_ENVIRONMENT extension (Option A)

The libretro env callback is intended for *frontend -> core* configuration, set up at `retro_set_environment` time. A static fn-pointer table returned from `retro_get_memory_data` fits the existing `LIBRA_MEMORY_*` extension scheme already pioneered for CRAM / VSRAM / VDP_State / M68K / Z80 in this fork, is ABI-stable, and frontends that don't know about 0x109 simply get NULL.

### Submodule bumps

- `common` -> `rtissera/clownmdemu-frontend-common@feature/m4-debug-hooks`
- `common/core` -> `rtissera/clownmdemu-core@feature/m4-debug-hooks`
- `common/core/libraries/clown68000` -> `rtissera/clown68000@feature/m4-debug-hooks`

`.gitmodules` files are repointed at the rtissera forks at every level so a fresh recursive clone resolves the chain.

## Test plan

- [x] `make -j$(nproc)` succeeds in the fork tree (clean build, no new warnings).
- [x] `clownmdemu_libretro.so` builds at 896,376 bytes (+504 B over baseline 895,872 B).
- [ ] mds-mcp Rust integration (parallel agent B) wires `LIBRA_MEMORY_DEBUG_API` and exercises `request_halt` / breakpoint / watchpoint callbacks against a known ROM.
- [ ] Megadrive Studio M4 milestone: single-step / set breakpoint / set watchpoint via MCP tool surface.

## Summary

- Run list (`spa/src/routes/+page.svelte`) now polls every 5 s while the tab is visible, with a `visibilitychange` listener for immediate refresh on focus. New runs and in-flight status changes appear without a manual click.
- Run-detail (`spa/src/routes/runs/[id]/+page.svelte`) tick now also re-fetches the top-level run record via `getRun(runId)`, so `inProgress` flips when the dispatcher writes the finalised summary and the page transitions gracefully from Live → Tasks/Manifest/etc. without a manual reload.
- Adds a comment near the Live tab gate explaining the gating is intentional. The "SSE filter UI disappears at finalize" symptom from #246 was downstream of (2) — it resolves once the page transitions correctly.

Closes #246.

## Notes

- Pure SPA change. No Rust changes; the binary just needs a rebuild to pick up the embedded SPA assets.
- Polling on the run list runs every 5 s only when `document.visibilityState === 'visible'`, so a tab left open in the background stays quiet.
- The run-detail tick adds a second `try { } catch { }` for `getRun` so a transient network blip during polling doesn't surface to the user — it just keeps the last good record until the next tick.
- The Live tab gating comment explicitly tells future readers not to strip the `{#if inProgress}`. If operators want to filter historical events post-finalize, that's a separate feature (mentioned in #246's out-of-scope section).

author: cryphon
body:
Boot sequence in boot.s:
- Wire mtvec to trap_entry before any code runs
- Store kernel stack in mscratch for trap_entry use
- Configure PMP to grant S-mode access to all memory
- Set mstatus MPP=01 and mepc=kernel_main, then mret to drop to S-mode

S-mode confirmed via illegal instruction trap on mstatus read from C —
M-mode CSRs are inaccessible from S-mode as expected. MPP=0 after mret
is correct per spec; mret clears MPP as a security measure.

trap_handler updated to advance mepc+4 on illegal instruction to prevent
re-entrancy loops during S-mode verification.

Follow-up to PR #51: clears the high-severity transitive vulnerabilities and restores `--audit-level=high` on the CI gate.

## Vulnerabilities resolved

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| 23 vulnerable packages (8 moderate, 15 high) | **1 package** (1 moderate Astro 5.x — see below) |

## Changes

1. **`npm audit fix`** (safe minor/patch updates) — cleared 19 packages.
2. **`astro-compress` 2.3.8 → 2.4.1** — clears the astro-compress-side svgo high-severity advisory.
3. **`overrides` in package.json** for transitive deps:
   - `picomatch: ^4.0.4` (high — ReDoS, method injection)
   - `yaml: ^2.8.3` (moderate — Stack Overflow; transitive in `@astrojs/check` / yaml-language-server)
   - `svgo: ^4.0.1` (high — Billion Laughs DoS; transitive in `@iconify/tools` / astro-icon)
   - `fast-xml-parser: ^5.7.2` already added in PR #51 for the critical-severity advisory; kept
4. **CI gate restored to `--audit-level=high`** in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Updated allowlist string in `scripts/check-workflows.mjs` to match.

## Remaining: 1 moderate Astro 5.x advisory (intentionally deferred)

```
astro <6.1.6 (moderate): XSS in define:vars via incomplete </script> tag sanitization
https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-j687-52p2-xcff
```

Clearing this requires bumping to **Astro 6.x** — a major version upgrade with breaking changes to integration APIs and internals. That belongs in its own PR with thorough regression testing and is **not** done here. `--audit-level=high` does not block on moderate, so the gate passes.

body:
## Summary

- Adds a minimal zero-dependency block-style YAML parser (`src/workflow/yaml.ts`) scoped to the `GraphDef` shape
- Adds `parseGraph(text, locator?)` helper (`src/workflow/parse.ts`) that auto-detects JSON vs YAML by file extension or content sniff, with clear parse error messages naming the source
- `FilesystemWorkflowAdapter.loadGraph` / `loadSourceGraph` / `listGraphs` now check `.yaml` / `.yml` extensions (`.json` preferred when multiple exist)
- `spores workflow create` now accepts `.yaml` / `.yml` input files
- Exports `parseGraph` from the package root so source-backed consumers (e.g. loading graphs from R2) can parse either format without depending on a YAML library

Existing JSON support is unchanged.

## Closes

Closes #47

## What the YAML parser supports

Block-style YAML covering the `GraphDef` schema:
- Block mappings (`key: value`) and block sequences (`- item`)
- Nested objects and arrays
- Double/single-quoted strings, bare scalars, integers, floats
- `null` / `~` / `true` / `false` literals
- Flow-style empty collections (`[]`, `{}`)
- Inline comments

Not supported (out of scope): anchors/aliases, tags, flow collections beyond `[]`/`{}`, block scalars (`|` / `>`).

## Summary

Two related fixes, bundled with a 0.5.4 → 0.5.5 bump.

### Auto-install bug (fixes upstream regression)
\`auto_install_provider_packs\` checked for existing packs by canonical
filename only (\`<provider_id>.gtpack\`). Bundles that ship a tenant-specific
build under a custom filename (e.g. \`messaging-webchat-gui-3aigent.gtpack\`)
had the canonical name re-installed from a sibling bundle on every setup
run. Two files for the same pack_id ended up registered, which caused:
- the setup wizard to list the provider twice (\"21 questions Done\" twice),
- \`gtc start\` to abort with \"static route webchat-gui ... overlap ambiguously\".

Fix uses \`discovery::discover()\` to detect by pack_id regardless of filename.

### Cargo.lock drift
PR #79 bumped the package version 0.5.3 → 0.5.4 in \`Cargo.toml\` but did not
refresh \`Cargo.lock\`. CI's \`cargo fetch --locked\` aborted with "cannot
update the lock file because --locked was passed". Folded into the 0.5.5
bump in this PR.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## 改了什么 / What changed When an account hits the quarantine threshold (default 4 consecutive `internal_error`), the system now **proactively refreshes its Firebase token** before quarantining. If the refresh produces a new API key, the next attempt after quarantine will use it automatically. New function `_tryRefreshOnPersistentError(account)`: - Fire-and-forget (doesn't block the request path) - Rate-limited to once per 60s per account (avoids hammering Firebase) - Skips accounts without `refreshToken` (api_key-only accounts) - Logs whether the refresh produced a new API key ## 为什么 / Why Production logs show account `oimoseob` consistently returning `internal_error` for even tiny requests (30 chars, 1 turn): ``` [WARN] Cascade error step {errorText=an internal error occurred (error ID: 81cceb774c6a4e9d85a4f654c086cc62) trail=[{"type":34,"status":3},{"type":14,"status":3},{"type":17,"status":3}]} ``` The account has adequate credits but the upstream Cascade rejects all requests. Investigation found: 1. **No code regression** — diff between old/new code shows no changes to cascade message building, auth flow, or protobuf encoding. Changes were only in security hardening (dashboard), model aliases, and account selection sorting. 2. **Root cause**: The upstream `internal_error` with trail `[type:34, type:14, type:17]` (type 34 = access verification step) suggests **stale API key or session corruption** on the upstream Windsurf side, not a proxy bug. 3. **Current behavior**: The quarantine cycle (quarantine 5min → retry → fail → quarantine again) never resolves because the API key itself may be stale. Firebase tokens expire after 60min and are refreshed every 50min, but if a refresh was missed or the API key rotated server-side, the account gets stuck. 4. **Fix**: Trigger a token refresh when the quarantine threshold is hit, so the next attempt after quarantine uses a fresh API key. This is the same `refreshFirebaseToken` + `reRegisterWithCodeium` flow used by the periodic 50-minute refresh. **Manual workaround** (if auto-refresh doesn't resolve): Dashboard → POST `/accounts/:id/refresh-token` to force a manual token refresh for the affected account. ## 测试 / Testing - 38/38 unit tests pass (including all health scoring, credit check, entitlement, and proxy ordering tests) - No changes to request handling flow — only adds an async side-effect in `reportInternalError` - Token refresh uses existing `refreshFirebaseToken`/`reRegisterWithCodeium` functions already proven by the periodic refresh loop ## Checklist - [x] 代码风格和现有文件一致 / Code style matches existing files - [x] 没有引入 npm 依赖 / No new npm dependencies (project is zero-dep) - [x] 涉及 LS binary 协议改动时 在 PR 描述里注明字段号来源 / N/A — no protocol changes - [x] 涉及 dashboard UI 用 App.confirm / App.prompt 不用浏览器原生 alert/confirm / N/A — no dashboard changes Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c45d878bf7264f6ab8cc0339ba720643 Requested by: @fanxemphim1-jpg ---

body:
Classification training was graphing wrong data (box/dfl showing 0s, cls showing accuracy metrics instead of loss) due to a regex/mapping mismatch between live output scraping and CSV loading. Three additional UX improvements are bundled.

## Graph data fixes

**Live training (`_EPOCH_INNER_CLS_RE` reader branch)**  
Previously passed `0.0` for `box` and `dfl`, causing a zero-point to be appended every epoch. Now passes `None`; all three commit sites (`_update_epoch_inner_progress`, `_update_train_progress`, `_training_finished`) skip appending when the value is `None`:

```python
# Before – 0.0 polluted box_loss and dfl_loss graphs
_train_pending_losses[0] = (0.0, loss_v, 0.0)

# After – only cls_loss receives data
_train_pending_losses[0] = (None, loss_v, None)
```

**CSV pre-load (`_load_results_csv_into_graphs`)**  
Classification `results.csv` has no `box_loss` column; the old positional fallback (indices 2/3/4) mapped `train/loss → box_loss`, `accuracy_top1 → cls_loss`, `accuracy_top5 → dfl_loss`. Now detects classification CSVs by `box_loss` column absence + `train/loss` presence, maps only `train/loss → cls_loss`, and clears the other two series.

## Dynamic "Training Output" header & column labels

`_train_output_header_lbl` and `_train_col_header_lbl` are stored as widget refs and updated by `_on_task_type_change` via `_TASK_HEADER_PREFIXES` and `_TASK_COL_HEADERS`. Classification shows `Epoch  GPU_mem  loss  Instances  Size`; all other tasks keep the three-loss format.

## Per-task console font colour

`output_textbox` `text_color` is set at build time and on every task switch via `_TASK_CONSOLE_COLORS`:

| Task | Colour |
|---|---|
| Detection | `#cdd6f4` (near-white) |

author: siarheirazuvalau
body:
## Problem

`createInvitationLink` activity events were persisted to the `activity` table with `project_id = NULL` and `organization_id = NULL`. As a result, these events never appeared in:

- **Project Activity Panel** widget (filters strictly by `project_id`)
- **Organization Activity** page (filters strictly by `organization_id`)

A TODO comment in the original code confirmed the developer was aware of the gap:

```java
// TODO: Add org IDs to event publisher. Needs to refactor ActivityEvent.
eventPublisher.publishEvent(
    new CreateInvitationLinkEvent(rpUser.getUserId(), rpUser.getUsername()));
```

## Root Cause

Three issues combined:

1. `CreateInvitationLinkEvent` constructor did not accept `projectId` or `organizationId`
2. `UserInvitationServiceImpl` published a single event with no project/org context
3. `CreateInvitationLinkEventConverter` did not call `.addProjectId()` or `.addOrganizationId()`

## Changes

**`CreateInvitationLinkEvent`** — constructor now accepts `projectId` and `organizationId`

**`UserInvitationServiceImpl`** — replaced single event publish with per-entry publishing:
- If the invitation includes explicit project IDs — one event per project (with `projectId` + `organizationId`)
- If the invitation is org-level only (no projects) — one event per organization (with `organizationId`, `projectId = null`)

**`CreateInvitationLinkEventConverter`** — added `.addProjectId()` and `.addOrganizationId()` calls

author: a-jeaugey
body:
## Summary
Implements spatial audio attenuation for sound effects based on the player's distance from sound sources. This prevents audio clutter by reducing volume for distant events and muting sounds beyond a configurable threshold.

## Key Changes
- Added `audibleGain()` method that calculates volume attenuation based on distance to the local player
  - Full volume (1.0) for sounds within `HEAR_NEAR` radius (22 units)
  - Silent (0.0) for sounds beyond `HEAR_FAR` radius (55 units)
  - Linear fade between the two thresholds
  - Returns 0 if player position is unknown (safety measure against audio clutter)

- Updated all spatial sound effect calls to use distance-based gain:
  - `bladeDestroyed` events
  - `crateDestroyed` events
  - `powerupPickup` events (full volume for local player, attenuated for others)
  - `clash` events (with special handling for local player involvement)
  - `bladeThrown` events (full volume for local player, attenuated for others)
  - `bladeImpact` events

- Modified `SoundManager` methods to accept optional `gain` parameter:
  - `pickup()`, `hit()`, `throwBlade()`, and `kill()` now support gain control
  - Early return if gain ≤ 0 to avoid unnecessary synth triggering
  - Gain passed to Tone.js `triggerAttackRelease()` calls

- Improved clash event handling:
  - Distant clashes now use distance-based attenuation instead of binary visibility
  - Screen shake for distant clashes only triggers if gain > 0.6 and a blade was destroyed
  - Rarity-to-tier mapping moved outside conditional for cleaner code

## Implementation Details
- Uses Euclidean distance (`Math.hypot`) for accurate spatial calculations
- Linear interpolation formula: `1 - (d - HEAR_NEAR) / (HEAR_FAR - HEAR_NEAR)`
- Special case: local player actions (pickup, throw) always play at full volume for immediate feedback
- Prevents audio feedback loops by checking gain before synth triggering

body:
## Summary

Converges fap-web's frontend-owned canonical domain to the apex origin `https://fermatmind.com` for PR-01 of the 2026-05-06 SEO/GEO launch train.

This PR keeps the scope narrow: runtime canonical source and the `www` host redirect only. It does not attempt sitemap hygiene, CMS/API canonical cleanup, llms hygiene, tracking, schema, content, or payment/order changes.

## Why

The live scan found that `https://fermatmind.com` and `https://www.fermatmind.com` both returned `200`, which splits canonical authority and can dilute SEO signals. The frozen launch plan selected `https://fermatmind.com` as the single canonical owner. PR-01 establishes that owner at the frontend runtime layer before later PRs clean sitemap, llms, and CMS/API canonical payloads.

## What changed

- `lib/site.ts`
  - Added `CANONICAL_SITE_URL = "https://fermatmind.com"`.
  - Normalizes FermatMind apex/www environment origins to the apex canonical URL.
  - Preserves non-production/non-canonical deployment origins such as staging as env-owned.
- `next.config.mjs`
  - Adds the first redirect rule for `www.fermatmind.com` to `https://fermatmind.com/:path*`, permanent.
- Contract tests
  - Site URL contract now proves `www` and `http://fermatmind.com` converge to apex.
  - Robots contract now proves `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=https://www.fermatmind.com` emits `https://fermatmind.com/sitemap.xml`.
  - Added a canonical-domain redirect contract that executes `next.config.mjs` and asserts the first redirect rule, rather than relying on source grep.

## Re-review fix included

During re-review, the first contract for the redirect was found to be too weak because it only inspected source strings. It now imports and executes the actual Next config `redirects()` function and asserts the first runtime redirect object exactly.

## Validation

Passed scoped/runtime validation:

```bash
node --check next.config.mjs
pnpm lint lib/site.ts app/robots.ts lib/seo/metadata.ts next.config.mjs tests/contracts/site-url.contract.test.ts tests/contracts/robots.contract.test.ts tests/contracts/canonical-domain-redirect.contract.test.ts
pnpm vitest run tests/contracts/site-url.contract.test.ts tests/contracts/robots.contract.test.ts tests/contracts/canonical-domain-redirect.contract.test.ts
pnpm typecheck
git diff --check
git diff --cached --check
node -e "const {default: config}=await import('./next.config.mjs'); const redirects=await config.redirects(); console.log(JSON.stringify(redirects[0]));"
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=https://fermatmind.com NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://api.fermatmind.com pnpm build
```

The build with production API env completed successfully. A first build attempt without overriding `.env.local` failed during prerender because local API `127.0.0.1:8000` was not running; the compile and TypeScript stages had passed before that environment-dependent prerender failure.

Live production checks were run before deploy:

```bash
curl -sS -I https://fermatmind.com/
curl -sS -I -L https://www.fermatmind.com/
curl -sS -I -L https://www.fermatmind.com/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types
curl -sS -L https://fermatmind.com/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types | rg '<link rel="canonical"'
curl -sS https://fermatmind.com/robots.txt
```

Current live production still returns `200` for `www` because this PR is not deployed yet. After deploy, `www` should single-hop redirect to matching apex paths as declared by the new Next redirect rule.

`pnpm verify:pr` was attempted and remains blocked by existing repository-wide lint baseline errors outside this PR scope:

- `components/result/mbti/clone/MbtiCloneAssetSlot.tsx`
- `ecosystem.config.cjs`
- `tests/contracts/enneagram-asset-backed-renderer.contract.test.tsx`

Because of that baseline, this PR is opened as draft and should not be considered mergeable until required checks are green or the baseline is resolved.

## Intentionally not touched

- fap-api / CMS/API canonical payloads
- sitemap URL corpus, filters, or additionalPaths
- `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` inventory
- tracking, GA4, Baidu, UTM
- schema additions
- content edits
- payment/order flows
- markdown mirror
- Product / SoftwareApplication schema

## Current PR-00 validator status

Ran with `|| true` to confirm this PR does not try to make later hygiene gates pass:

- `pnpm seo:assert-live-sitemap`: `total_urls=637`, `bad_count=637`
- `pnpm seo:assert-live-llms`: `total_urls=220`, `bad_count=99`
- `pnpm seo:assert-live-llms-full`: `total_urls=218`, `bad_count=97`

## Rollback

Rollback only the `lib/site.ts` canonical convergence, the `next.config.mjs` host redirect, and the related contract tests. Do not modify sitemap, llms, CMS/API, tracking, or content as part of rollback.

body:
## Summary

Run #25110421840 (post-PR-#12) showed the new \`stage_details\` diagnostic working: Scout generated 5 ideas with composites **3.10 / 2.85 / 3.20 / 3.05 / 2.85**. Two ideas (3.10 and 3.20) cleared the new 3.0 composite floor — but **all five still failed** because the gate was \`composite >= X AND novelty >= Y AND data_adequacy >= Z\`. Claude rated one of those two dimensions at 2 ("below average") on every idea, even when the weighted composite was acceptable.

The per-dimension AND-gate is a redundant second filter: the composite already weights novelty (0.20) and data_adequacy (0.20). Provably blocking ideas the composite accepted is the wrong tradeoff when the composite is the sound aggregate.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| \`backend/app/config.py\` | New setting \`scout_screen_strict_per_dimension: bool = False\` (overridable via env var) |
| \`backend/app/services/paper_generation/roles/scout.py\` | Default gate is now composite-only. Strict-mode preserved as opt-in. \`thresholds.strict_per_dimension\` surfaced in the screening output. |
| \`backend/app/services/paper_generation/orchestrator.py\` | \`_stage_scout\` now copies per-dimension scores into each screenings entry, so the response payload shows \`{question, composite, scores, passed}\` per idea instead of just the collapsed composite. |

## Tests — \`backend/tests/test_scout_screening_gate.py\` (new, 6 tests)

| Test | What |
|---|---|
| \`test_default_gate_is_composite_only\` | composite=3.20, novelty=2, data=2 → **passes** (mirrors prod case) |
| \`test_default_gate_rejects_below_composite_floor\` | composite=2.0 → rejected |
| \`test_strict_mode_rejects_low_novelty\` | composite=3.20, novelty=2 → rejected when strict=true (legacy preserved) |
| \`test_strict_mode_accepts_when_all_floors_met\` | All 4s → passes in strict |
| \`test_thresholds_surfaced_in_result\` | screening.thresholds includes strict flag |
| \`test_per_dimension_scores_preserved\` | Full \`scores\` dict survives in screening output |

## Test plan
- [x] \`pytest backend/tests/test_scout_screening_gate.py\` — 6/6
- [x] \`pytest backend/tests/\` — 121/121
- [x] ruff check + ruff format clean

## Operational impact
After merge + Render redeploy, the next \`/batch/generate\` call should:
- (a) **Produce a paper end-to-end.** Two of the five ideas in run #25110421840 had composites of 3.10 and 3.20 — the new composite-only gate accepts them. The pipeline can continue past Scout into Designer → Data Steward → Analyst → Drafter → Verifier → Packager.
- (b) Response payload now shows full per-dimension scores, so any downstream failure surfaces exactly where the bottleneck is.

## Out of scope
The asyncpg \`InterfaceError: cannot call Transaction.rollback(): the underlying connection is closed\` seen for paper 2 in run #25110421840 — separate concern (long-running pipeline outliving its DB session). Worth a follow-up PR; not blocking the screening question.

author: dev-nid
body:
## Summary
GPT-OSS 20B tool calling was broken — the model emits a Harmony tool call frame but generation stops silently before `<|call|>` reaches the SDK, resulting in 0 parsed tool calls and no visible frame delimiter.


## Root cause
`<|call|>` (token 200012) is in the model's EOG set. When sampled, it renders as 0 bytes (control token with `special=false`) and immediately triggers the generation loop break. The model produces the tool call JSON but the output is truncated with no frame boundary visible to the SDK.

## Fix
- Detect Harmony/GPT-OSS architecture at initialization and resolve the `<|call|>` token ID
- In the generation loop, intercept `<|call|>` before the generic EOG break when `isHarmonyModel_` and `params_.use_jinja` are true
- Render `<|call|>` as visible text using `common_token_to_piece(lctx_, tokenId, true)` so the SDK can parse frame boundaries
- Stop generation cleanly — Harmony is turn-based, one tool call per pass, SDK handles tool execution and re-prompts
- Applied to both `TextLlmContext.cpp` and `MtmdLlmContext.cpp`
- Added multi-turn example (`harmonyMultiTurnTools.js`) demonstrating sequential tool execution across turns
- Confirmed parallel tool calling is not supported — model emits exactly one <|call|> per generation regardless of prompt

author: tmarshall
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Adds an external channel guard to `handleMemberJoinedChannel` so the bot never posts a greeting in Slack Connect (externally shared) channels. When added to such a channel, the bot:

1. Calls `conversations.info` to check `IsExtShared` / `IsPendingExtShared`
2. If external: logs "Leaving external channel", calls `conversations.leave`, and returns immediately
3. If the API call fails: logs a warning and continues with the normal greeting (fail-open)

This prevents the bot from operating in channels shared with external organizations. Downstream agent prompt guards serve as a second layer of defense.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- Introduced a `slackAPI` interface to make the handler testable without real Slack API calls. The `*slack.Client` satisfies it implicitly.
- The `FetchThreadContext` signature in `thread.go` was updated to accept the interface instead of `*slack.Client` (no behavior change).
- Uses `enrichCallTimeout` (5s) for both the `conversations.info` and `conversations.leave` calls, consistent with existing timeout patterns.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
The Slack bot now automatically leaves externally shared (Slack Connect) channels when added, preventing operation in channels shared with external organizations.
```

Notely had a minimal, unstyled Bootstrap UI with no theming, poor mobile support, and inconsistent component patterns. This adds a complete design system and updates all views.

## New CSS Architecture

Three new stylesheets replace the near-empty `site.css`:

- **`theme.css`** — CSS custom property tokens (colors, spacing scale, shadows, typography, transitions) with full `[data-theme="dark"]` override block. `@import` for Inter font placed first for optimal loading.
- **`components.css`** — Reusable component styles: sticky navbar, gradient buttons, note/feature/auth/form cards, search bar, badges, hero section, empty state, footer. Hamburger icon uses `mask-image` so its color adapts to the active theme.
- **`responsive.css`** — Mobile-first CSS Grid layouts (notes: 1→2→3→4 cols, features: 1→2→3 cols), fluid containers, responsive auth page, touch targets via `(hover: none), (pointer: coarse)`, focus-visible keyboard styles, print rules.

## Dark Mode (`theme-toggle.js`)

New JS module reads/writes `localStorage` (`notely-theme`), respects `prefers-color-scheme` as default, and updates toggle button icons. A small inline `<script>` in `_Layout.cshtml` applies the saved theme before first paint to prevent FOUC — intentionally separate from the toggle module.

| `_Layout.cshtml` | Sticky navbar with brand icon, mobile hamburger + collapse, dual theme toggles (mobile/desktop), footer |

## What does this PR do?

This PR fixes `setup-hermes.sh` to avoid failing in non-interactive environments.

The script currently used `read -p` directly for interactive questions, which can hit EOF and abort under CI/container/non-interactive execution (`set -e`), even when the user requested a headless install flow. This patch adds a small helper to detect non-interactive stdin and safely skip prompts, preserving interactive behavior while preventing EOF crashes.

## Summary
- `/api/notifications/send` was returning 500 in prod because the `user_notification_preferences` table in Cloud SQL still had the old schema (`notification_type_id` FK) while the code was querying for `template_name`. The Dec 2025 schema refactor never made it to the prod database.
- The SQL file is now fully idempotent (indexes use `IF NOT EXISTS`); the existing `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` + `CREATE TABLE` already handles the schema swap. **The fix has already been applied to prod by re-running this file.**
- The route handlers were logging only `error.message`, which Drizzle reduces to the unhelpful `"Failed query: …"` prefix and hides the actual postgres error code/detail. Added a pino error serializer that walks the cause chain and pulls postgres fields (`code`, `detail`, `hint`, `table`, `column`, `constraint`, etc.), and switched the catch blocks to log the full error object so the serializer engages.

## SQL migration files
- `apps/notifications/sql/user_notification_preferences.sql` — added `IF NOT EXISTS` to all four index definitions. No column changes.

- [ ] Deploy `crm-notifications` and confirm new revision is healthy

author: alex-budanov
body:
## Why

A production outage of similar-bugs and Suggest Fix on \`serg-corp-3\` (visible as eternal "Generating suggestion..." spinners and 404s) traced to a deploy-config drift:

- [bugspotter-intelligence#27](../../../bugspotter-intelligence/pull/27) migrated \`bug_embeddings.embedding\` to \`vector(1024)\` (for \`BAAI/bge-m3\`).
- This compose file still hardcoded \`EMBEDDING_MODEL: all-MiniLM-L6-v2\`. \`environment:\` wins over \`env_file:\`, so the prod \`.env\` had no effect — the container ran MiniLM (384-dim) writing into a \`vector(1024)\` column.
- Result: silent insert failures (no error in default \`LOG_LEVEL=warn\`), 61 bug records with NULL \`embedding\` accumulated over 13 days. \`enrich\` kept working (no embeddings needed) and made the AI features *look* alive, hiding the breakage.

Compounding factors discovered in the same incident:
- \`INTELLIGENCE_TIMEOUT_MS\` (worker → intelligence) and \`OLLAMA_TIMEOUT\` (intelligence → Ollama) were both 120s — inverted/equal, so the worker frequently gave up while intelligence was still mid-generation.
- Intelligence container's 2 GiB memory limit OOM-killed BGE-M3 (~2.3 GB on disk + activations) on first load.
- Ollama at 2 CPUs (of 4 host cores) capped CPU inference at <8 tok/s, pushing 300-token mitigation requests past the worker timeout.

## What changed

\`docker-compose.yml\`
- **Embedding env**: \`EMBEDDING_PROVIDER\` / \`EMBEDDING_MODEL\` now use \`\${VAR:-default}\` so \`.env\` is read; default switches to \`BAAI/bge-m3\` to match the schema.
- **Similarity thresholds**: default 0.75 → 0.68 / 0.90 → 0.85 (bge-m3-optimal per the embedding-benchmark research).
- **Timeouts**: \`INTELLIGENCE_TIMEOUT_MS\` 120000 → 240000; \`OLLAMA_TIMEOUT\` 120 → 240. Documented the must-be-greater-or-equal relationship inline.
- **Resources**: Ollama \`cpus 2 → 3\`; intelligence \`memory 2G → 4G\` (\`reservations\` 512M → 1G).
- **Healthcheck**: intelligence \`start_period 30s → 120s\` to cover BGE-M3 lazy-load.

\`.env.example\`
- Mirror the new defaults and document the schema/model coupling and timeout ordering.

## What is NOT in this PR

- **Bake BGE-M3 into the image** — Dockerfile change in \`bugspotter-intelligence\`, separate PR.
- **Polling termination on the UI side** — \`SuggestFixButton\` keeps spinning forever on backend hiccups, separate PR in this repo.
- **Switch to \`llama3.1:3b\` for faster mitigation** — env-only change, can be made later via \`INTELLIGENCE_OLLAMA_MODEL\` without another PR.
- **Dynamic \`target_dim\` in migrations** — proper engineering fix in \`bugspotter-intelligence\` so model/schema can't drift again. Separate issue.
- **Backfill the 61 NULL-embedding bugs** — separate operational task.

## Test plan

- [x] \`docker compose --profile intelligence config\` — values resolve to \`BAAI/bge-m3\`, 240000 ms, 240 s, 0.68, 0.85.
- [x] Manually applied equivalent edits on prod, confirmed end-to-end pipeline works for newly-created bugs (analyze → 1024-dim embedding → enrich + similar + mitigation).
- [ ] Re-deploy on prod after merge, verify VM \`docker-compose.yml\` no longer needs hand-edits.

### Motivation
- Make the humanoid rig produce more natural idle/grip/shoot poses by exposing explicit grip and idle parameters instead of a single `gripRatio` magic value.
- Compute right-hand socket offsets and hand basis more directly to improve wrist placement and finger posing when gripping the cue.
- Add a lightweight seated player character rig to the `PoolRoyale` scene so a player figure follows the cue/aim and animates while shooting.

### Description
- Replace `CFG.gripRatio` and related single-handed constants with a richer set of configuration keys in `BilardoShqipGame.tsx` such as `idleRightHandX/Y/Z`, `idleCueGripFromBack`, `shootCueGripFromBack`, `idleCueDir`, `rightHandRollIdle`, `rightHandRollShoot`, and `rightHandCueSocketLocal` to control grip and idle geometry.
- Add `cueSocketOffsetWorld` helper and update `updateHumanPose` / `driveHuman` to compute `idleWristTarget` / `liveWristTarget`, refined `gripSide`/`gripUp` vectors, roll blending, and stronger finger posing to improve the right-hand grip and overall aiming posture.
- Improve idle cue rendering by computing an `idleCue` via `cuePoseFromGrip` and switching cue visuals depending on `state` (`idle` vs active) so the cue aligns with the new idle grip parameters.
- Integrate a seated human template in `PoolRoyale.jsx` by calling `ensureSeatedHumanTemplate` and `createPlayerCharacterRig`, spawn a single rig, and add `updatePlayerCharacters` logic to position/rotate the rig, place grip/bridge proxies, and blend a simple `poseT` on shooting.

body:
This pull request improves thread safety and the handling of concurrent cache calculations in the `BalanceTopImpl` class, and adds comprehensive unit tests to verify the new behavior. The main focus is on ensuring that only one cache calculation runs at a time, and that concurrent requests for a calculation share the same future.

**Thread safety and concurrency improvements:**

* Added a `cacheLockMonitor` object and synchronized blocks to ensure that only one cache calculation can run at a time, and that concurrent calls to `calculateBalanceTopMapAsync` return the same `CompletableFuture` if a calculation is already in progress. (`Essentials/src/main/java/com/earth2me/essentials/BalanceTopImpl.java`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-24d4e66666e0790d1f6c4bb0e220cefc97765553a74204d5d3bd605dcac15810R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-24d4e66666e0790d1f6c4bb0e220cefc97765553a74204d5d3bd605dcac15810L28-R30) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-24d4e66666e0790d1f6c4bb0e220cefc97765553a74204d5d3bd605dcac15810L65-R89) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-24d4e66666e0790d1f6c4bb0e220cefc97765553a74204d5d3bd605dcac15810R108-R112)

**Testing enhancements:**

* Introduced a new test class `BalanceTopImplTest` with tests to verify that concurrent calls to `calculateBalanceTopMapAsync` reuse the same future and that only one asynchronous task is scheduled at a time. body:
## Summary

The MCP SDK lets a tool advertise a `description` string as the second positional argument to `server.tool(...)`. Per the MCP spec the field is optional, but Anthropic's API rejects requests carrying tools whose description is null/missing with:

```
tools.<n>.custom.description: Input should be a valid string
```

This breaks any chat where this server is enabled on an Anthropic-backed client (Claude Desktop, Claude via LiteLLM, anything routing to Anthropic). The bug surfaces immediately on first prompt — the tool list is included in every request.

Adding non-empty descriptions also helps LLMs route to the correct tool without having to infer behavior from the JSON-schema input alone.

## Changes

- `create-image`: descriptive string covering text-to-image, base64 default, file_output mode, 1MB cap fallback.
- `edit-image`: descriptive string covering image arg formats (path / base64), mask semantics, output modes.

Two-line addition; no behavior change.

## Test plan

- \`yarn build\` clean.
- Verified on a Claude (Anthropic) chat: previously triggered \`tools.<n>.custom.description: Input should be a valid string\`; now succeeds.
- \`tools/list\` returns a non-null \`description\` for both tools.

author: sanjacob99
body:
## Summary

Three coordinated upgrades to the agent-facing session tools, fully wired end-to-end:

- **`sessions_yield`** is now real async-resume orchestration. Agent calls it after spawning sub-agents; the turn ends, and the runtime auto-dispatches a synthetic user turn back to the parent when all sub-agents reach a terminal state (or a 10-min safety timeout fires). Aggregated text carries each sub-agent's status / duration / output (1500-char per-sub cap, 8000-char total). A `sam.sub_agent_resume` custom transcript entry marks the resume so the UI can render it distinctively.
- **`sessions_list`** gains `label` (substring of `displayName`, case-insensitive), `agent` (caller-scoped — rejects cross-agent values until that wiring lands), and `preview: true` (boolean toggle that includes first-user-message preview + messageCount per session, capped at 50 sessions to bound transcript I/O).
- **`sessions_history`** switches plain-text output to JSON with `before: <entryId>` cursor pagination (newest-first), per-entry truncation (500 chars / 200 chars for tool results), and a 12k-char total response budget that sets `truncated: true` + `nextCursor` when cut short.

Supporting plumbing:
- `SubAgentRegistry` rewritten from a boolean flag to a stateful `YieldState` map (timer + idempotent resolve callback). New methods: `setYieldPending(opts, resolve) → SetYieldResult`, `cancelYield`, `cancelAllYields`. `onComplete` / `onError` / `kill` all drive `maybeResolveYield`.
- `RunCoordinator` wires `resolveYield` through `SessionToolContext`, with a `handleYieldResume` private method that persists the marker entry then dispatches the synthetic user turn. Both persistence and dispatch wrap independent try/catch — a deleted parent or transcript-write failure can't crash the registry resolve. `destroy()` calls `cancelAllYields()` to clear timers on shutdown. `finalizeRunError` notifies the registry's `onError` for `sub:` keys (so a child crash resolves the parent's yield without waiting out the safety timeout).
- New custom transcript entry types in `shared/session-diagnostics.ts` (`SUB_AGENT_RESUME_CUSTOM_TYPE`, `SubAgentResumeData`, `SubAgentResumeResult`).

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-29-session-tools-yield-list-history-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-29-session-tools-yield-list-history.md`.

13 commits (6 feature + 7 review-driven follow-ups). 66 directly-relevant tests added/updated; pre-existing failures elsewhere in the project are unrelated to this branch.

## Test plan

**Unit tests** (already passing — the PR ships these):

- [ ] Run the registry suite in isolation: `npx vitest run server/agents/sub-agent-registry.test.ts`. Expect 15 passing — covers spawn / onComplete / onError / kill / get / allComplete record lifecycle, plus the yield surface (no-active-subs, already-pending, all-complete resolve, all-complete-via-error resolve, timeout resolve, idempotent double-fire, cancelYield, cancelAllYields).
- [ ] Run the tools suite: `npx vitest run server/sessions/session-tools.test.ts`. Expect 26 passing — covers default `sessions_list`, the new label/agent/preview filters, default `sessions_history`, the new pagination/cursor/budget cases, and all six `sessions_yield` text branches.
- [ ] Run the coordinator suite: `npx vitest run server/agents/run-coordinator.test.ts`. Expect 25 passing (no regressions).
- [ ] Server typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.server.json`. Pre-existing errors at unmodified lines are out of scope; verify no NEW errors at lines this branch touched.

**Manual verification** (recommended before merging into a deployment):

- [ ] Build a graph with a Storage node, an Agent node, and Tools node where the **sessions** group is enabled. Start the dev server.
- [ ] **`sessions_list`**:
  - Call with `{}` — expect default JSON shape (sessionKey, sessionId, chatType, updatedAt, totalTokens, displayName).
  - Call with `{ label: "<substr>" }` — expect filtering by `displayName`; case-insensitive.
  - Call with `{ agent: "<other-agent-id>" }` — expect text starting with `Cross-agent listing is not yet supported`.
  - Call with `{ preview: true }` — expect each result to include `preview` (≤120 chars) and `messageCount`. With >50 matching sessions, expect at most 50 results.
- [ ] **`sessions_history`**:
  - Call with `{ sessionKey }` against a session with >20 entries — expect newest-first ordering, 20 entries, `nextCursor` set, `truncated: false`.
  - Call again with `{ sessionKey, before: <previous nextCursor> }` — expect the next page of older entries.
  - Call with `{ sessionKey, before: 'nope' }` — expect `Cursor not found: nope` text.
  - Call with `{ sessionKey, includeToolResults: false }` — expect message-only entries; `totalEntries` excludes tool results.
  - Call against a session whose page would exceed 12k chars — expect `truncated: true` and a valid `nextCursor`.
- [ ] **`sessions_yield`** (requires the agent to be configured with `subAgentSpawning: true` and to have called `sessions_spawn` first):
  - Call `sessions_yield` with no spawned subs — expect `No sub-agents pending; yield is a no-op.`
  - Spawn one or more sub-agents via `sessions_spawn`, then call `sessions_yield` — expect `Yielded; will resume when N sub-agent(s) complete (timeout = 600s).` and the parent's turn to end.
  - Wait for sub-agents to finish — expect a new turn to appear in the parent transcript with the aggregated results text. The transcript should contain a `sam.sub_agent_resume` custom entry immediately preceding the resume user message.
  - Spawn a sub-agent that errors out (e.g., bad tool call) — expect the parent to still resume, with that sub-agent's `status: 'error'` and `error: <message>` in the aggregated text.
  - Call `sessions_yield` while a yield is already pending — expect `Yield already pending; ignoring.`
  - Set `timeoutMs` very small (e.g., 5000) and spawn a long-running sub — expect the parent to resume after ~5s with `reason: 'timeout'` and the still-running sub-agent shown with `status: 'running'`.

**UI follow-up (out of scope here):** the `sam.sub_agent_resume` custom entry is persisted but no UI consumer renders the "Sub-agent results" pill yet. That's a frontend task for a separate PR.
