Assigned work order: Implement Ice Dragon Core Interaction and Audio Feedback

Implement the core interaction loop for the Ice Dragon in the `studio-dragon-crew` repository. Create a single-screen web interface with a primary trigger action (e.g., click to exhale). Develop visual state transitions (locked, active, exhaled) with polished motion and a deliberate visual hierarchy. Integrate procedural audio using the Web Audio API for input, transition, and success states, ensuring graceful mute fallback. Ensure the code is responsive, accessible, and free of external dependencies, resulting in a shippable prototype that demonstrates the complete core loop.

Locked goal:
# The Dragon Crew Build

## Hook
Build a focused, shippable web experience for The Dragon Crew from the available ideation context. The result should be understandable within seconds and compelling enough to replay or share.

## Experience Goal
Prioritize one clear interaction, immediate feedback, and a complete audiovisual payoff. Avoid broad feature lists; choose the strongest concrete idea from the context and make it feel finished.

## Core Interaction Loop
The visitor should see the state, perform one primary action, receive visible and audible feedback, and reach a satisfying end state or loop reset without instructions getting in the way.

## Scope and Constraints
Keep the project to one screen, one primary mechanic, responsive layout, no external paid services, and no fragile setup. Preserve accessibility basics and make the default path work without configuration.

## Visual Direction
Use a deliberate visual system with strong hierarchy, readable type, purposeful color, and polished motion. The page should look intentional rather than like a raw prototype.

## Music and Sound Design
Include meaningful procedural or bundled audio where the browser allows it. Audio should reinforce the main interaction and state changes, with graceful mute or silent fallback behavior.

## Interaction Audio
Tie input, transitions, success, failure, and reset states to distinct sonic feedback. Keep sounds short, controlled, and synchronized with visible changes.

## Ship Bar
The delivered project must run from a clean checkout, have no obvious console errors, include the complete core loop, and feel coherent on desktop and mobile.

author: ptaranat
body: ## What Buyers clicking "Cancel" on their Manage membership page now see a modal first: pause for 1 month, pause for 3 months, or cancel anyway. Pausing defers the next charge by N billing cycles. The buyer's last paid period resolves as usual, access lapses at its end (same as cancelling), and `RecurringChargeWorker` picks back up on its next tick after the pause expires. Few cases are blocked from pausing: installment plans, free trials, test subs, anything already pending cancellation, and fixed-length memberships on final cycle. Tier upgrades and downgrades are also blocked while paused, since they'd otherwise fire an immediate prorated charge mid-pause (which is kinda rude). Plan changes already queued before the pause apply on the resume charge automatically, since `RecurringChargeWorker` already handles that path. ## Why [Recharge](https://getrecharge.com/blog/reduce-your-cancellations-by-10-with-pause-subscriptions/), a subscriptions SaaS for Shopify, shared findings showing merchants who added a pause-as-deflection saw an average 9.6% save rate on attempted cancellations. Netflix also does this. Gumroad offers cancel and restart with no middle ground for a buyer just wanting to pause for a month so they can make better use of the sub. Rather than creating a new pause state, we're reframing it as a deferred charge date. ### Notes on scope - Buyer surface is cancel-flow modal only. Proactive pause from management page can come later if the save-rate metric pays off. - No seller-facing config. We just make it storewide to keep it simple. Per-product opt-out is easy to add if creators on Gumroad ask for it. - Durations are 1 and 3 cycles. This also avoids the "pause forever as a free cancel" loophole without having to worry about defending against abuse. - Anchor date drift: pausing shifts the day-of-month anchor by the pause length permanently. This same drift already happens after card-decline retries so the documented "we charge on the original day" is best-effort. Worth hardening later. ## Out of Scope - Manual resume endpoint (auto-resume fine for now) - Per-product seller opt-out - Pause analytics dashboard - Multiple consecutive pauses - Cancel-during-pause path - Pausing gifted memberships ## Before / After ### Pause 1 Month https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b7d73ba-6905-4499-abd8-99093e3f9519 ### Pause 3 Months https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74dc24c5-2a54-42a5-a0c2-d6a101667eb2 ### Cancel Anyway https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2759caa-e21c-4e89-9e0d-a92765351b57 ### Light Mode + mobile https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a492005-3ceb-4853-b10a-619b9e911a42 ## QA Steps 1. Sign in as a buyer who owns an active monthly membership 2. Open `/subscriptions//manage`. Confirm page renders with "Cancel membership" button at the bottom and no paused banner. 3. Click `Cancel membership`. The "Need a break?" modal should open with two primary CTAs ("Pause for 1 month", "Pause for 3 months") and a danger "Cancel anyway" in the footer. 4. Click `Pause for 1 month`. Modal closes, page refreshes props and shows an info banner: "Your membership is paused until . It will resume automatically on the next charge." The `Cancel membership` button is hidden. 5. In Rails console, verify backend state: ```ruby sub = Subscription.find_by_external_id("") sub.paused? # => true sub.can_be_paused_by_buyer? # => false (already paused) ``` 6. Run `RecurringChargeWorker.new.perform(sub.id)` while paused. There will be no charge so worker returns early. 7. Set `sub.update_column(:paused_until, 1.day.ago)` and re-run the worker. It should proceed with normal charge attempt. 8. Re-pause, then attempt tier change: `sub.update_current_plan!(new_variants: [], new_price: nil)`. This raises `Subscription::UpdateFailed: "Resume your membership to change tier or plan."` 9. Try paths the modal should not open on (installment plans, free trials, test subs). body:
## Summary

Adds first-pass pinning support across Halley for windows, collapsed nodes, and cluster core nodes.

Pinned items are treated as important field entities: they can still be moved deliberately by the user, but automatic bumping and overlap resolution will not displace them. Pinned items are also always included in Bearings so they remain easy to find anywhere in the field.

## Changes

- Add pin toggling for the focused item with the default `mod+p` binding.
- Render pinned windows and collapsed nodes with a configurable pin badge.
- Add pin badge configuration under `field.pins`, including:
  - badge corner
  - glyph colour
  - background colour
  - size scale
- Transfer pinned state from absorbed windows into clusters/core nodes.
- Keep compositor-side pin registries synchronized across cluster create, absorb, collapse, expand, and dissolve flows.
- Refactor cluster transition paths through Halley wrappers so core state and workspace pin state stay consistent.
- Preserve maximized window shadows.
- Update config defaults, generated templates, bootstrap merging, split-config examples, and changelog entries.
- Update gathered config behavior via `rune-cfg` 0.4.6 so unaliased gathered sections deep-merge correctly.
- Protect fullscreen/game surfaces from collapsing into nodes while their fullscreen session is alive.
- Make `close-focused` respect focused cores and monitor-local targeting.
- Preserve maximize state through fullscreen transitions.
- Move pure overlap contact physics into `halley-core`.
- Make overlap-policy windows stack on click without hover focus changing z-order.

## Testing

Verified with:

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo test -p halley-wl close_focused`
- `cargo test -p halley-wl`

Added or updated regression coverage for:

- pin toggling
- pinned bump/displacement protection
- Bearings inclusion for pinned items
- movement behavior after unpinning
- pinned state transfer into clusters and core nodes
- gathered config deep-merge behavior
- fullscreen/game surfaces resisting collapse
- close-focused core and monitor isolation behavior

body:
## Summary

- Doc-only audit at `docs/audits/zstd-batch-compatibility.md` covering whether zstd can serve as a batch-compatible compression alternative for `--write-batch` / `--read-batch` (task #1685).
- Recommendation: Conditional Yes for self-round-trip only. Zstd's independent per-frame framing avoids zlib's `see_deflate_token()` dictionary-sync requirement, but the upstream batch header (`batch.c:59-76` bit 8) does not record the codec name, so a zstd batch is indistinguishable from zlib on the wire and would be mis-decoded by stock upstream rsync. The existing magic-byte auto-detect at `crates/batch/src/replay.rs:985-988` already anticipates this.
- Cites: oc-rsync `replay.rs`, `batch.rs`, `flags.rs`, `zstd.rs`, CLI help text, and upstream `batch.c` / `compat.c` / `token.c`.

Adds a live preview of badge styling changes directly in the editor canvas, updating in real-time as settings are changed in the sidebar.

## Changes Made

- **`assets/css/admin-editor.css`**: Updated to use CSS custom properties with `unset` fallback so the editor canvas reflects live setting changes.
- **`src/settings/use-settings.ts`** (new): Shared `useSettings()` hook that centralises all 13 `useEntityProp('root', 'site', ...)` calls and returns a typed `Settings` object with values and setters.
- **`src/settings-preview/index.tsx`** (new): `ClearancePreviewStyles` component in its own top-level module. Uses `useSettings()` (read-only) and owns the `useEffect` with CSS var injection, iframe load listener, and `MutationObserver`. Registered as the `wc-clearance-preview-styles` plugin.
- **`src/page-editor-sidebar/index.tsx`**: `ClearanceSectionSidebar` now calls `useSettings()` instead of 13 individual `useEntityProp` calls, and imports `ClearancePreviewStyles` from `src/settings-preview`. Both plugins are registered at the bottom, each wrapped with the shared `withSiteRecord` guard:
  - `wc-clearance-sidebar` — renders the `PluginSidebar` with all badge controls, reads/writes settings via `useSettings()`, contains no preview side effects.
  - `wc-clearance-preview-styles` — reads badge settings via `useSettings()`, builds CSS custom property declarations, and injects a `<style id="wc-clearance-preview-vars">` element into the editor canvas head. Handles iframe reload and replacement via a `MutationObserver` independently of the sidebar lifecycle. Returns `null` (no UI).

- **`src/settings-preview/test/index.test.tsx`** (new): Tests that `ClearancePreviewStyles` renders nothing and that the preview effect correctly injects CSS vars (`label`, `bg-color`, `text-color`) into the style element.
- All 53 unit tests pass.
- JS and CSS linters pass.

author: thomasjiangcy
body:
## What was changed

Adds the Node-level Port Access entrypoint for HTTP and Upgrade requests. The data-plane gateway now intercepts Port Access hosts before Hono, validates the existing Port Access session cookie, reconstructs adapted raw HTTP request heads from Node `rawHeaders`, and opens `ports.tcp.*` streams through the PR2 transport.

The entrypoint preserves forwarded header casing/order/repeated values, strips the Port Access session cookie, rewrites target-facing `Host` and `Origin`, appends `X-Forwarded-*`, preserves Upgrade handshake headers, forwards Node `upgrade` head bytes, propagates client close/abort/error to the TCP stream, and re-encodes dechunked Node HTTP request bodies when the client used `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`.

## How to review

Review `apps/data-plane-gateway/src/publishing/port-access-node-entrypoint.ts` first. The request and upgrade intercept/delegate wiring is in `apps/data-plane-gateway/src/server.ts` and `apps/data-plane-gateway/src/runtime/index.ts`.

The main PR3 coverage is in `apps/data-plane-gateway/integration/port-access-http-node-entry.integration.test.ts` and the rewritten `apps/data-plane-gateway/integration/port-access-websocket.integration.test.ts`.

## What the implication was

Client-facing Port Access HTTP and WebSocket Upgrade traffic can now use the raw TCP transport while existing non-Port-Access routes continue through Hono. This PR keeps the older semantic Port Access route code in place for migration compatibility; PR4 removes or quarantines that path.

## Checks and tests performed

- `pnpm validate:changed`
- `pnpm --filter @mistle/data-plane-gateway typecheck`
- Targeted integration attempt: `pnpm --filter @mistle/data-plane-gateway exec vitest run -c vitest.integration.config.ts integration/port-access-http-node-entry.integration.test.ts integration/port-access-websocket.integration.test.ts`

The targeted integration attempt was blocked by a fixture-level `data-plane-api` deadline update 500 during bootstrap attach. I reproduced the same local failure with the existing `integration/port-access-http.integration.test.ts`, so this is not isolated to the PR3 diff. The read-only review agent reviewed this context and greenlit the PR3 implementation after blocker fixes.

## Summary

Two CI fixes for MyJobHunter, both pre-existing failures on `main`:

1. **`backend-tests` job** — installs `platform_shared` so pytest can collect (`ModuleNotFoundError` blocked it).
2. **`integration` smoke test** — switches register+login email from `*.invalid` (rejected by `email-validator>=2` per RFC 6761 globally_deliverable check) to `*.example.com` (RFC 2606 reserved + accepted).

## Why

MJH backend imports `platform_shared.{db,core.security}`, but the CI workflow installed only `requirements.txt`. The smoke test email `*@myjobhunter-test.invalid` started 422-ing once email-validator was bumped past 2.0.

MJH backend-tests has been red on `main` since the regressions; this unblocks every MJH PR (incl. #112, #114).

- Replace inline `update()` in `updateSpectrum()` with a `QTimer`-driven repaint loop in `SpectrumWidget`, decoupling display refresh rate from FFT buffer fill timing
- Add `m_hasNewSpectrum` flag so the timer only repaints when new FFT data has arrived, avoiding redundant renders
- Add `setDisplayFps()` slot so the Setup FPS slider keeps the display timer in sync alongside `FFTEngine::setOutputFps()`
- Raise `FFTEngine` safety cap to 60 fps (was matched to display rate, causing irregular frame spacing)
- Add `dbmToYf()` for sub-pixel Y coordinates in the CPU-path trace polyline so `QPainter` antialiasing has fractional values to work with

## Root cause

The display was being repainted directly from `updateSpectrum()` on every FFT frame. `FFTEngine` rate-limits emission to 30 fps (33 ms minimum interval), but the IQ buffer fills every ~22 ms. Since 33 ms is not a multiple of 22 ms, frames were only emitted every ~44 ms (~23 fps) with uneven spacing - producing visibly choppy spectrum updates despite the 30 fps setting.

## Test plan

- [ ] Connect to an OpenHPSDR radio and verify the spectrum trace updates at a consistent, smooth rate
- [ ] Adjust the FPS slider in Setup ? Display and confirm the display timer interval changes accordingly
- [ ] Verify peak hold and waterfall continue to function correctly
- [ ] Build on Windows (MinGW), macOS, and Linux - no new dependencies introduced

## Summary

Two changes to make the event landing page convert harder:

1. **Registration form now lives in the hero** ~ visitors don't have to scroll to sign up. Since the event is free, friction = lost signups.
2. **Featured Skool community section** ~ leans into the "200+ members in less than a week" momentum to drive community signups (the recurring revenue path).

## What changed

### Hero ~ now a two-column landing pattern

- Left column: existing pitch (image, badge, "This is where you start", walk-aways, meta chips), tuned for the narrower column
- Right column: **the registration form**, sticky on desktop so it follows you as you scroll the pitch
- Form card header: `RESERVE YOUR SPOT · FREE · 30 SEC` (kills any friction perception before they read the form)
- "Reserve My Free Spot" button removed from hero (the form replaces it); "See agenda" + community link demoted to small text links
- `id="register"` moved to the hero section so anchor links land on the form

### New `#community` section

Between hero and audience pillars. Three-column layout:

| | |
|---|---|
| **🔥 GOING FAST** badge | **JOIN OUR COMMUNITY** label |
| Massive **200+** in italic peach Cormorant | Headline: "The room is *already filling up.*" |
| **MEMBERS** + *in less than a week* | Body about Skool 0 → 200+ in 7 days |
| | 5 stacked emoji avatars + "+195" counter |
| | **Join the community →** CTA (peach, links to Skool) |

### Hero secondary action

Replaced "Join our community" text link with: \`🔥 200+ IN < 1 WEEK\` peach badge + "See our Skool" link, anchored to \`#community\`. Lands the proof in the first viewport.

### Bottom of page

- Old REGISTER section (full duplicate form) replaced with a slim "Still here?" final CTA that scrolls back up to the hero form
- No duplicate RegisterForm rendering; cleaner Suspense boundary

## Test plan

- [ ] Open \`/events/claude-for-business\` ~ form is visible alongside the hero pitch (no scroll needed)
- [ ] On desktop, scroll the hero ~ form stays sticky in view
- [ ] Click \`See our Skool\` chip ~ scrolls to the community section
- [ ] Community section shows the 200+ stat, avatars, and "Join the community" CTA
- [ ] CTA links open https://www.skool.com/future-proof-with-ai-4339 in new tab
- [ ] Mobile: hero stacks (pitch on top, form below)
- [ ] Bottom "Still here?" anchor scrolls back to hero form

body:
## Summary

- **Closes #3003**: Increase default request timeout in `run-all-tests.sh` from 60s to 120s to prevent HTTP 000 timeout errors on multi-round AI tool call tests.

### Problem

`run-all-tests.sh` set a default timeout of 60s and passed it to all sub-scripts via `--timeout`. This overrode the individual test scripts' own defaults of 120s for AI-heavy test suites:

| Test Script | Script Default | Override from Runner |
|-------------|---------------|---------------------|
| `use-case-2-task-execution.sh` | 120s | 60s ❌ |
| `mcp-tools-test.sh` | 120s | 60s ❌ |
| `multimodal-test.sh` | 120s | 60s ❌ |

Tests involving multi-round tool calls (File listing task ~60s, Tool result format ~60s) regularly exceeded the 60s boundary, causing HTTP 000 errors.

### Solution

Align `run-all-tests.sh` default timeout (60s → 120s) with the AI-heavy test scripts' own defaults.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `tests/integration/run-all-tests.sh` | Default `TIMEOUT` 60 → 120; update header comment |

### Test Results

- Existing tests that pass in <60s remain unaffected
- Multi-round tool call tests now have sufficient headroom
- No behavioral change to individual test script defaults

### Description
Implements the changes requested by @glenn-jocher in the issue linked above:
- Added `eval-only` support for dynamic OKS sigmas via dataset YAML (`kpt_oks_sigmas`).

## 🛠️ PR Summary

<sub>Made with ❤️ by [Ultralytics Actions](https://www.ultralytics.com/actions)</sub>

### 🌟 Summary
Adds optional `kpt_oks_sigmas` support for pose evaluation via dataset YAML, enabling custom OKS sigma values with validation and test coverage. 🎯

### 📊 Key Changes
- Added support in `PoseValidator.init_metrics()` to read optional `kpt_oks_sigmas` from dataset YAML for pose evaluation.
- Added validation to ensure the provided `kpt_oks_sigmas` length exactly matches the keypoint count defined by `kpt_shape`, raising a clear `ValueError` when mismatched.
- Preserved existing default behavior by continuing to use built-in OKS sigmas for standard `[17, 3]` pose datasets and uniform fallback values for other keypoint layouts when custom sigmas are not provided.
- Added a new test file `tests/test_pose_custom_oks.py` covering both valid custom sigma loading and invalid length handling. ✅
- Updated documentation in `docs/en/guides/model-yaml-config.md` to describe the new optional dataset YAML parameter and its expected format. 📘

### 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- Gives pose users more flexibility to evaluate custom keypoint datasets with dataset-specific OKS sigma settings.
- Improves robustness by validating configuration errors early instead of silently using incorrect settings.
- Enhances usability through documentation and tests, making the new behavior easier to adopt and maintain.
- Benefits pose workflows in the Ultralytics package without changing default behavior for existing datasets. 🚀


---

## Maintainer update

Deleted: `tests/test_pose_custom_oks.py` (bundled test removed per repo preference, behavior verified empirically) and the docs note in `guides/model-yaml-config.md` (wrong page — `kpt_oks_sigmas` is a dataset YAML key, not a model YAML key), relocated to `datasets/pose/index.md` beside the optional `flip_idx` key. The validation was compacted to a single `self.data.get()` branch reusing the existing `OKS_SIGMA` fallback and the `kpt_iou` consumer — no new helper added.

Verified empirically with `yolo11n-pose.pt` on `coco8-pose`: custom `kpt_oks_sigmas: [0.1] * 17` changes pose mAP50-95 (0.3094 → 0.465, confirming the sigmas flow into `kpt_iou`), omitting the key reproduces the default COCO-sigma metrics exactly, and wrong length (10 of 17) or non-positive values raise a clear `ValueError` at `init_metrics`.

body:
### Overview
This PR modernizes the bypass to support **Hermes 0.11.0** and addresses recent Anthropic server-side validation changes (April 2026) that were causing "Third-party app" 400 errors and plan-limit bypass failures.

### Key Changes

#### 1. Hermes 0.11.0 Architecture Support
- **Transport Layer Patching:** Hermes 0.11.0 refactored its Anthropic adapter to use an `AnthropicTransport` class. This PR adds a hook into `AnthropicTransport.normalize_response` to handle response unwrapping, ensuring compatibility with the new architecture while remaining backwards-compatible with older versions.

#### 2. Advanced Validator Bypass
- **Tool Namespacing:** Implements the `mcp__hermes__<ToolName>` wrapping required by the latest Anthropic validators.
- **Account Linking:** Automatically reads `accountUuid` from `~/.claude.json` and injects it as `user_id` in the request metadata. This ensures the request perfectly matches the account identity of the official Claude Code CLI.
- **Telemetry Sanitization:** Strips Python-specific "Stainless" headers and spoofs the official JS-based CLI fingerprint (Node/v22 runtime headers).

#### 3. UX & Logic Improvements
- **Robust Tool Unwrapping:** The response unhook now handles cases where Hermes has already partially stripped prefixes, and it correctly restores tool names to lowercase (e.g., `Mcp__hermes__Terminal` -> `terminal`). This eliminates the "Auto-repaired tool name" noise in the Hermes logs.
- **Environment Detection:** Improved `install.sh` to correctly detect `site-packages` in global, virtualenv, or `--user` installations.

### Impact
- Fixes "Extra inputs are not permitted" 400 errors.
- Fixes "Unknown tool" errors caused by namespacing.
- Restores the ability to use Claude Pro/Max limits instead of "Extra Usage" credits.

body:
Fixes #198

## What

Hyperlinks inside PDFs are tappable again, and tapping the area around the bottom page indicator no longer gets swallowed by its full-width wrapper.

## Why

Two regressions from the Apr 9-10 PDF navigation update:

- The `Pdf` component's `onPressLink` defaulted to a no-op, so tapping a link did nothing. Wired it up to the existing `safeOpenURL` helper.
- The `PageIndicator` is positioned absolutely across the full bottom of the screen. Its outer wrapper was intercepting touches in the empty space beside the chip, blocking page swipes and link taps that landed near the bottom of the page. Setting `pointerEvents="box-none"` lets touches fall through everywhere except on the chip itself.

Also set `enableAnnotationRendering` explicitly. The library default is already `true`, but the flag is explicit because the link-rendering layer is the surface this fix depends on.

author: bruno02468
body:
This PR contains two new features and fixes METIS builds on Windows.

The two new features are:
  - `mystran --version` now prints information about the MYSTRAN build: compiler flags, build type, timestamp, embedded libraries, etcetera.
  - `mystran --licenses` now prints MYSTRAN's license, followed by the licenses of every library embedded into the binary.

Since all that information depends on the build environment, it cannot be determined until CMake runs. Therefore, `CMakeLists.txt` now contains code to keep track of all libraries are being statically linked into MYSTRAN (plus LAPACK, which is built from source and linked as object code -- still embedded into the binary).

The motivation for `--licenses` is compliance with open-source licenses, which require distribution of copyright notices in both source and binary form. We were covered for source form, since licenses would be present on the submodules and, in the case of system-provided libraries, we added them to an `extra_licenses` directory. But for binary form, we had to embed them and `--licenses` works.

As for `--version`, well, since I was already working on generating build information for runtime display, I decided to make something that'd help me. More than once I wasted time because some Fortran flag was being silently overridden, or because I lost track of what build type I was running. So `--version` takes care of that!

Oh, and METIS for Windows was breaking because of some weird stuff with GKlib's build script. I fixed include directories, linked against the embedded implementation of `<regex.h>`, and forced C99, and it works fine now. Yet another `_patches` directory, so... yay. Maybe we should contribute these fixes upstream one day.

author: malteos
body:
## Summary

Make `dump_api_data` the canonical, reproducible OLDP data-publishing path for [`oldp-toolkit`](https://github.com/openlegaldata/oldp-toolkit) (which produces the HuggingFace `openlegaldata/court-decisions-germany` dataset) and other downstream consumers.

The dump now guarantees:

- **Always-accepted filter** — records with `review_status != "accepted"` never appear in any output. Previously this was incidental (via `ReviewStatusFilterMixin` reading `request.user`; the dump uses no request); it's now enforced directly in the command.
- **Reproducible ordering** — pk-ascending iteration so the same prod state yields byte-identical dumps.
- **Self-describing manifest** — a sibling `manifest.json` records `snapshot_date`, `oldp_version`, applied filters, and per-file row counts so consumers can pin against a specific snapshot.
- **Stream-gzipped output** — `*.jsonl.gz` written directly (the toolkit already auto-detects `.gz`).
- **Citation-matching-friendly fields** — `LawSerializer` now denormalizes `book.code` as `book_code`, so a `(book_code, slug) → law_id` index can be built from `laws.jsonl.gz` alone.

Documentation for the dump command was scattered between `docs/production.md` and `docs/api/api-overview.md`; both now point to a new consolidated [`docs/data-dumps.md`](docs/data-dumps.md).

## Compatibility

`oldp-toolkit` only consumes `cases.jsonl[.gz]`, auto-detects `.gz`, ignores extra files and unknown fields, and ignores `manifest.json` — so all changes here are additive from the toolkit's perspective and require no coordinated release.

## Test plan

- [x] `make lint` passes
- [x] `manage.py test oldp.apps.homepage.tests.test_commands` — 5 tests pass (filter, gzip, manifest, pk-ordering, book_code)
- [x] `manage.py test oldp.apps.laws oldp.apps.courts oldp.apps.cases.tests` — 419 tests pass
- [x] `manage.py test oldp.api` — 43 tests pass
- [x] Verify end-to-end against a prod-like dataset before publishing the next HuggingFace snapshot
- [x] Confirm `oldp-toolkit`'s `convert_dump_to_hf` produces a parquet with the same column schema as the existing `court-decisions-germany` dataset when pointed at the new `cases.jsonl.gz`

## Out of scope (follow-up PRs)

- Adding a `references` viewset/serializer so reference data can ship as part of the dump
- Coordinated `oldp-toolkit` changes to consume the additional dump files (`laws.jsonl.gz`, `courts.jsonl.gz`, `law_books.jsonl.gz`)
- Renaming the published HF dataset to `oldp-snapshot-YYYY-MM-DD` and publishing siblings (`laws-germany`, etc.)

author: copilot
body:
Previously, the grid probe generated columns using global bounding-box X positions (`minX..maxX`) and skipped points outside the inset polygon. This caused row 1 to start far inside the board for non-rectangular shapes instead of at the actual SVG boundary edge.

## Changes

### New helper: `_polyRowXSpan(poly, targetY)`
Scanline intersection against the inset polygon at a given Y — returns `{ xLeft, xRight }` or `null` if the row is entirely outside the polygon.

### Per-row column generation in `runOutlineSurfaceGridProbe`
- For each row, computes `xLeft`/`xRight` from the inset polygon via `_polyRowXSpan`
- Generates exactly `colCount` columns evenly spaced from `xLeft → xRight`:
  ```
  rowDx = (xRight - xLeft) / (colCount - 1)
  colX  = xLeft + col * rowDx
  ```
- Rows with no polygon intersection (outside Y range) are skipped cleanly with a log message
- The point-in-polygon check is retained as a floating-point edge-case guard only

### Row transition
Moves to the next row's `xLeft` (from polygon span) rather than always to `gridCfg.minX`.

### Logging
- Per-row debug line: `ROW span: xLeft=..., xRight=..., cols=N, dx=...`
- Grid summary annotated with `(per-row X span from polygon boundary)` when in detected outline mode
- SKIP log updated to `(edge case)` since points are generated inside the boundary by construction

### Tests
Added 11 unit tests for `_polyRowXSpan` covering axis-aligned rectangle, above/below null returns, octagon (circular shape), and inset polygon span.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Create a new PR (previous PR #270 already merged) to change Outline Surface Grid Probe so that each row’s X probe points are generated from the SVG outline boundary span.
> 
> Repo: Badgerk1/live-edge-3d-probe
> Base branch: main
> 
> User requirement (Option 1)
> - For each row (at grid Y), compute the inset outline polygon intersection span for that row: xLeft to xRight.
> - Instead of using global grid X columns (minX..maxX) and skipping outside points, generate exactly N column positions (configured grid columns) evenly spaced from xLeft..xRight for that row.
> - Probe points should therefore start at/near xLeft (SVG boundary) each row and end at/near xRight.
> 
> Traversal requirement
> - Keep non-serpentine behavior: every row probes left-to-right (no reversing).
> 
> Logging
> - Update log text to reflect new per-row span sampling.
> - Add a per-row debug line like: "ROW span: xLeft=..., xRight=..., cols=N, dx=...".
> 
> Acceptance criteria
> - In logs, row 1 begins with a probe point near xLeft rather than jumping to first in-bounds global column.
> - No “SKIP outside boundary” should be needed for most points because points are generated inside boundary by construction (though still handle edge cases where computed span is invalid).
> - Works for rectangular and round outlines.
> 
> Notes
> - Previous PR #270 already merged; open a new PR with this boundary-based per-row column generation change.

## Summary

Closes the docs/schema mismatch reported in feedback id `0b37f7a1`.

The CLI's `AuthSection` only knew about the legacy `redirect_uris` field and was annotated `serde(deny_unknown_fields)`, so the documented accounts-mode auth shape failed preflight with:

> `INVALID_PROJECT_CONFIG: unknown field access_policy, expected redirect_uris`

The API has accepted the new shape for a while — `tarball.py::_parse_auth_config` reads `[auth] access_policy` + `allowed_domains` straight from the TOML in the deploy tarball, and `routes/deploys.py` syncs them to `app.access_policy` and `AppAllowedDomain` rows. Only the CLI was rejecting valid configs at preflight time.

- Add `access_policy: Option<String>` and `allowed_domains: Option<Vec<String>>` to `AuthSection`. `redirect_uris` stays for backward compatibility with apps that haven't migrated.
- Validate in `validate_app_config`:
  - `access_policy` must be one of `{"invite", "domain", "open"}`.

- Both error paths emit `INVALID_PROJECT_CONFIG` with a clear remediation suggestion.

author: daishiman
body:
## Summary

Cloudflare Workers Edge Runtime 互換の Google Sheets API 認証を新設。Service Account JSON + Web Crypto API による RS256 JWT 署名で access token を取得し、UT-09 / UT-21 など下流 wave に `getSheetsAccessToken({ env })` 公開 API を提供する。

- 実装: `packages/integrations/google/src/sheets/{auth,auth.test,auth.contract.test,index}.ts` 新規
- 公開: `packages/integrations/google/src/index.ts` に `sheets` namespace export 追加
- 仕様書: `docs/30-workflows/completed-tasks/ut-03-sheets-api-auth-setup/` (phase-01〜13 全揃)
- スキル反映: aiworkflow-requirements の references 4件 + indexes 4件 + lessons-learned 新設

関連: closes #52

## 実装ガイド (Phase-12 implementation-guide.md より)

### Part 1: 中学生レベルの説明

#### このタスクで何をしているの?

UBM 兵庫支部会のメンバー情報は Google Form に書き込まれて Google スプレッドシートに集まります。これを私たちのアプリ（Cloudflare で動いている）が読みに行くために、**「このアプリは正規のお客さんですよ」と Google に証明する仕組み** を作るのがこのタスクです。

#### 鍵束のたとえ

- **Service Account（サービスアカウント）** = アプリ専用の鍵束
- **JSON キー** = その鍵束に入っている合鍵そのもの
- **JWT 署名** = 「この合鍵は本物だよ」と Google に提出する一筆
- **Access Token** = 受付で「OK」と言われた後にもらえる入館証（1 時間で期限切れ）
- **TTL 1 時間キャッシュ** = 入館証は毎回もらいに行くと受付が混むので、もらった入館証を 1 時間メモして使い回す

#### なぜ Service Account を選んだの?

人間が毎回ログインするのは大変だし、夜中に Cloudflare が自動で同期したいときに「人間 寝てるから無理」になります。Service Account ならアプリ自身が自分で鍵を出して入れます。

#### なぜ秘密にするの?

合鍵を落とすと誰でも私たちのスプレッドシートを読めてしまうので、**秘密の場所（Cloudflare Secrets と 1Password）にしか置きません**。GitHub にも `.env` にも実物は置かない。AI（Claude Code）にも見せない。

### Part 2: 技術者レベルの説明

#### アーキテクチャ

```
apps/api (Cloudflare Workers, Edge Runtime)
  └─ packages/integrations/google/src/sheets/auth.ts
       ├─ parseServiceAccountJson(env)        : Zod schema validation + JSON parse
       ├─ signJwt(claim, privateKey)          : Web Crypto API RS256 sign
       ├─ exchangeJwtForAccessToken(jwt)      : POST oauth2.googleapis.com/token
       └─ getSheetsAccessToken(env): closure cache (TTL 1h, refresh 5min before)
```

#### 採択方式: Service Account JSON key + Web Crypto JWT

| 項目 | 採用 | 不採用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 認証方式 | Service Account JSON key | OAuth 2.0 (user consent flow) |
| JWT 署名 | Web Crypto API (RS256) | google-auth-library（Node API 依存で Workers 非互換） |
| キャッシュ | in-memory closure (TTL 1h, refresh 5min before) | KV / D1 永続化（YAGNI） |
| Secret | `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` (Cloudflare Secrets, 1Password ref) | `.env` 平文 |

#### Edge Runtime 互換ポイント

- `crypto.subtle.importKey('pkcs8', ...)` で PKCS#8 PEM の改行 (`\n` → 実改行) を正規化
- `crypto.subtle.sign('RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5', ...)` で RS256 署名
- `fetch` のみ使用（`https`/`node:crypto` 不使用）

#### 公開 API（契約）

```ts
export type SheetsAuthEnv = {
  GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: string;
  SHEETS_SCOPES?: string;
};
export function getSheetsAccessToken(env: SheetsAuthEnv): Promise<{ accessToken: string; expiresAt: number }>;
```

下流（UT-09 / UT-21）はこの shape のみを依存対象とする。変更時は major bump。

#### 異常系（Phase 6 抜粋）

- F-1 JSON parse 失敗 → fail-fast、redact
- F-5 Sheets 未共有 → 403 PERMISSION_DENIED、Phase 5 ステップ 3 へ
- F-6/F-7 429/5xx → exponential backoff（1s/2s/4s）

#### Secret 配置

```
1Password → .env (op:// 参照のみ) → bash scripts/with-env.sh で実行時注入
1Password → bash scripts/cf.sh secret put → Cloudflare Secrets (dev/staging/production)
```

## 品質検証

- ✅ `pnpm install --force`
- ✅ `pnpm typecheck` (5 packages 全て PASS)
- ✅ `pnpm lint` (5 packages 全て PASS)

## Test plan

- [x] Phase-11 で NON_VISUAL evidence 縮約 (`main.md` / `manual-smoke-log.md` / `link-checklist.md` の 3 点)。実 Sheets API 疎通は UT-26 へ委譲
- [x] `auth.test.ts` (292 行) で parse / sign claim / token exchange 4xx・5xx / TTL キャッシュ / 5分リード refresh / in-flight Promise 共有 / scope 別モジュールキャッシュ / redact を網羅
- [x] `auth.contract.test.ts` で `SheetsAuthEnv` / `SheetsAccessToken` の型契約を凍結 (UT-09 / UT-21 の依存契約)
- [ ] 後続 wave (UT-09 / UT-21) で `getSheetsAccessToken` を consumer として呼び出し、実 Sheets API 疎通を確認

## 既知の課題（本 PR スコープ外）

- pre-push の `coverage-guard` が 80% 閾値で失敗 (主に main 側既存の `packages/shared` 34% / `packages/integrations` 0% の baseline 問題)。本 PR の `sheets/auth.ts` は 70.85% で F-6/F-7 リトライ経路が未カバー — 別タスクで一括対応予定

author: lespinald
body:
## Auth Flow – Description of Code Changes

- The implemented changes establish a complete authentication flow for the web application, enabling secure access control and session management.

- The login and registration interfaces were connected to the backend authentication service, allowing users to create accounts and sign in. Upon successful authentication, the application stores an access token (via cookies or storage), which is used to authorize subsequent requests.

- A route protection mechanism was introduced using Next.js middleware, ensuring that any attempt to access protected routes (e.g., /app/*) redirects unauthenticated users to the login page. This guarantees that only authenticated users can access the main application.

- Additionally, a token refresh mechanism was implemented: when an API request returns a 401 Unauthorized, the client automatically attempts to refresh the session by calling the refresh endpoint and retries the original request once. This maintains user sessions seamlessly without requiring repeated logins.

- Finally, a logout action was added to clear authentication data and redirect the user back to the login screen, effectively ending the session.

### Motivation
- Provide a public documentation site and capture product/architecture decisions for the Flux MVP. 
- Ship an initial Node/TypeScript backend scaffold with in-memory domain modules to accelerate Sprint 1 development. 
- Enable simple CI/CD for docs and backend by adding GitHub Pages and Railway deploy workflows. 

### Description
- Adds a static docs site at `docs-site/index.html` and multiple documentation files under `docs/` (PRD, ADR, technical architecture, sprint backlogs, next steps). 
- Introduces `flux-backend` scaffold including `src/` modules (`auth`, `companies`, `users`, `employees`, `attendance`, `audit`), common utilities (`token`, `password`, `validation`, `id`, `http`, `audit`), middleware, `server.ts`, types shims, `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`, `Dockerfile`, `.env.example`, `.dockerignore`, and a README with deploy notes. 
- Adds simple in-memory stores and REST endpoints for auth (register/login/refresh/logout), employees CRUD, attendance clock-in/clock-out and summary, audit events, and companies/users admin endpoints. 
- Adds automated common tests script `flux-backend/scripts/common-tests.mjs` and package scripts (`build`, `dev`, `check`, `test:common`). 
- Adds CI workflows: `/.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` to publish `docs-site` to GitHub Pages and `/.github/workflows/deploy-railway.yml` to deploy the backend to Railway (uses secrets `RAILWAY_TOKEN`, `RAILWAY_PROJECT_ID`, `RAILWAY_SERVICE_ID`), and `railway.toml` for Railway configuration.

author: richard-ramos
body:
## Summary

This updates pubsub peer sending so pending transport writes are tracked by the peer queue.

Before this change, `sendMsg` started `conn.writeLp(msg)` but did not keep the returned future. This meant pubsub could think a peer had no pending send even when the transport was still writing. As a result, more messages could keep being sent to the same peer and build up inside the transport buffers.

This is especially problematic for QUIC, where bandwidth can look fine while message latency grows because messages spend more time waiting in hidden queues.

With this change:

- `sendMsg` returns a future that represents the actual write lifecycle.
- high-priority sends store that future in the peer queue when the write is still pending.
- `sendEncoded`, `broadcast`, and `publish` still get fire-and-forget behavior and do not wait for the transport write to finish.
- medium/low priority peer queue processing can now see pending high-priority sends and wait before sending more messages to that peer.

With this, pubsub will be aware of slow peer sends without adding backpressure to publishers or receive handlers.

## Affected Areas

- [x] Gossipsub  
  Pubsub peer send queue behavior is updated so pending sends are tracked correctly.
- [ ] Transports
- [ ] Peer Management / Discovery
- [x] Protocol Logic  
  Internal message scheduling between high, medium, and low priority pubsub messages is affected.
- [ ] Build / Tooling
- [ ] Other

## Impact on Library Users

No API changes.

`publish`, `broadcast`, and normal pubsub send paths remain fire-and-forget. This PR should not make application publishing wait for network writes.

The behavior change is internal: pubsub now tracks pending per-peer sends and avoids sending lower-priority messages to a peer while a high-priority send is still pending.

Expected impact:

- reduced hidden transport buffering for slow peers
- better queue visibility through existing pubsub peer queue metrics
- no migration required for downstream users

## Risk Assessment

Risk is moderate because this changes internal pubsub send scheduling.

Main behavior risk:

- medium and low priority messages may be delayed more consistently behind pending high-priority sends for the same peer.

This is intended, but it can affect timing-sensitive tests or workloads.

### KEEP THIS INTO ACCOUNT WHILE REVIEWING CODE:
Backpressure risk:
- this PR should not add caller backpressure.
- `sendEncoded`, `broadcast`, and `publish` still return without waiting for transport writes.
- receive handlers should not block on pubsub writes.

Network behavior risk:
- slow peers may see more delayed or dropped medium/low priority messages when their queues fill.
- this is preferable to silently accumulating latency inside transport buffers.

author: psoholt
body:
## Summary

After the master/main branch consolidation, CI on \`master\` started failing on two unrelated issues. This PR fixes both.

### 1. gitleaks-action license error

\`gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2\` requires a paid license for organization accounts. \`Energee-AS\` is an org, so the action errors out before scanning. Removed the gitleaks job from \`.github/workflows/test.yml\`.

Rationale: upstream \`garrytan/gbrain\` (a personal account) still runs the action free, so secret-scanning still happens at the upstream layer; and GitHub's built-in push protection covers our local pushes. Buying a license or self-hosting the OSS gitleaks CLI was rejected as overkill for an internal fork.

### 2. \`PGLiteEngine: search since filter > searchKeyword respects since\` failing

The test added in PR #3 (\`feat/since-filter\`, \`828ac39\`) had two real bugs:

- **Hard-exclude collision.** Slugs starting with \`test/\` are filtered by \`searchKeyword\`'s default hard-exclude prefixes (\`DEFAULT_HARD_EXCLUDES\` in \`src/core/search/source-boost.ts\`, v0.22 source-aware ranking). Both test pages used \`test/old-page\` / \`test/new-page\`, so they never made it past retrieval. Switched to \`concepts/*\` slugs.
- **Missing chunk fixtures.** The v0.20 Cathedral II refactor moved \`searchKeyword\` to chunk-grain — it ranks \`content_chunks.search_vector\`, not \`pages.search_vector\`. \`putPage\` alone does not populate \`content_chunks\`. Existing search tests in this file all call \`upsertChunks\` after \`putPage\`; the new since test forgot to. Added explicit \`upsertChunks\` calls.
- **Bonus hardening.** The original cutoff was \`new Date()\` taken between two 10ms-spaced \`putPage\` calls. JS wall clock vs Postgres \`NOW()\` is a cross-clock comparison and fragile under microsecond truncation on slow runners. Replaced with a DB-derived cutoff (\`oldPage.created_at + 1ms\`) plus a tiny sleep to guarantee the new page's transaction-time is strictly greater.

## Test plan

- [x] \`bun test test/pglite-engine.test.ts -t "search since filter"\` passes locally on PGLite
- [ ] CI green on \`fix/ci-gitleaks-and-since-test\` (the real verification)

author: propensive
body:
Stacked on top of #927.

Bitumen previously raised `TarError.NameTooLong` when a path or link target exceeded the 100-byte USTAR header limit, so it could not produce archives of realistic deep directory trees. With this change it instead emits a POSIX.1-2001 PAX `'x'` extended-header entry immediately before any USTAR entry whose `path` or `linkpath` exceeds the limit, carrying the full value as a record in the form `<length> <key>=<value>\n`.

### What changed

- New `bitumen.Pax.scala` formats PAX records (including the recursive decimal-length-prefix calculation) and concatenates record bytes.
- New `TarEntry.Pax(records: Data)` case with type flag `'x'`, fixed name `PaxHeaders/0`, and data = the records bytes (chunked to 512-byte blocks). The other entry-derived fields (path, mode, user, group, mtime) are inherited as constant defaults.
- `Tar.serialize` (no longer `using Tactic[TarError]`) injects a synthetic `TarEntry.Pax(...)` before any entry that needs one. The driver is `Tar.paxRecordsFor`, which today produces records for `path` (entry name > 100 bytes) and `linkpath` (link target > 100 bytes).
- `TarEntry.header` no longer raises. The writer silently truncates oversize fields in the regular USTAR header (PAX carries the full value, so readers prefer the PAX value). Truncation is now also applied to `uname` and `gname` (32-byte fields) where the old code could overrun via `System.arraycopy`.
- `Tar is Streamable by Data` no longer requires a `Tactic[TarError]`. `TarError` itself stays defined for the forthcoming reader, but is no longer raised by the writer.

```scala
import charEncoders.ascii
import bitumen.*

val deepPath = ("a"*150).tt.decode[Relative on Posix]

val entry = TarEntry.File(
  path  = deepPath,
  mode  = UnixMode(),
  user  = UnixUser(0),
  group = UnixGroup(0),
  mtime = 0.bits.u32,
  data  = LazyList()
)

// previously: raised TarError(Reason.NameTooLong(_, 150, 100))
// now: emits a PAX 'x' header carrying `path=aaa...` ahead of the
// regular header, which itself stores the truncated 100-byte name.
val bytes = Tar(LazyList(entry)).serialize
```

### Tests

The suite grows from 10 to 21 tests. The two new sub-suites cover:

- Long-path file produces 5 blocks (PAX header + PAX data + regular header + 2 trailing zero blocks); PAX header has type flag `'x'` and name `PaxHeaders/0`; PAX record begins with the decimal length `160 path=` and ends with `\n`; regular header has type flag `'0'` and its 100-byte name field is fully populated by the truncated path.
- Long-target symlink produces 5 blocks; PAX record begins `164 linkpath=`; regular header has type flag `'2'` and its 100-byte link-target field is the truncated value.

### Out of scope

- Reader-side parsing of PAX records.
- Long `uname` / `gname` via PAX (currently silently truncated to 32 bytes; PAX `uname` / `gname` records would be a small follow-up using the same `paxRecordsFor` mechanism).
- Sub-second `mtime`, large `size` (>8 GB), and other PAX keywords. The plumbing is in place for these as one-line additions to `Tar.paxRecordsFor`.

author: ddrthall
body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds diagnostic infrastructure to the Kubernetes log pipeline E2E tests (`TestK8sCCAOff`, `TestK8sSuite`) so that failures produce actionable information instead of a generic "Ubuntu service not found" timeout.

Changes:
- **`WaitForJobPodRunning`** shared utility in `test/e2e-framework/testing/utils/k8s/k8s.go`: polls until a Job's Pod leaves Pending phase, returning immediately with a descriptive error on image pull failures (`ImagePullBackOff`, `ErrImagePull`), scheduling failures, or crash loops.
- **`DescribeJob`** shared utility: collects Job status, Pod phase/conditions, container states, Pod events, and container logs into a diagnostic string.
- **Enhanced assertion messages**: when "ubuntu" is not found in fakeintake service names, the message now includes the list of services that *were* found, fakeintake `RouteStats` (payload counts per endpoint), and full Job/Pod diagnostics.
- **`AfterTest` hooks** on both suites: dump fakeintake route stats on failure (following the NPM test pattern).
- **Error guards** added to the CCA-off test's `EventuallyWithT` callback (matching the CCA-on test pattern).

### Motivation

These tests have been failing in CI (tracked in AGNTLOG-619) with no useful diagnostic output. The failure message is always "Ubuntu service not found" regardless of whether the issue is an image pull failure, a scheduling problem, the agent not collecting logs, or a fakeintake transport issue. This makes triage impossible without reproducing the failure locally.

### Example: diagnostic output from a real CI failure

Before this PR, the test would time out after 30 seconds with only `"Ubuntu service not found"`. With this PR, the failure output from [pipeline 113482429](https://gitlab.ddbuild.io/DataDog/datadog-agent/-/pipelines/113482429) shows:

```
Error:      Annotations job pod failed to start
Messages:   job annotations-job pod annotations-job-qcmdm container annotations-job:
            ErrImagePull - failed to pull and unpack image "docker.io/library/ubuntu:latest":
            429 Too Many Requests

            --- Job default/annotations-job diagnostics ---
            Job status: active=1 succeeded=0 failed=0
            Pod annotations-job-qcmdm: phase=Pending reason= message=
              condition: type=Ready reason=ContainersNotReady
                         message=containers with unready status: [annotations-job]
              condition: type=ContainersReady reason=ContainersNotReady
                         message=containers with unready status: [annotations-job]
              container annotations-job: waiting: reason=ErrImagePull
                message=failed to pull and unpack image "docker.io/library/ubuntu:latest":
                429 Too Many Requests
              events:
                Scheduled Normal: Successfully assigned default/annotations-job-qcmdm to ...
                Pulling Normal: Pulling image "ubuntu"
                Failed Warning: Failed to pull image "ubuntu": 429 Too Many Requests
                Failed Warning: Error: ErrImagePull
                BackOff Normal: Back-off pulling image "ubuntu"
                Failed Warning: Error: ImagePullBackOff
```

The root cause (Docker Hub rate-limiting) is immediately identifiable without any local reproduction.

### Describe how you validated your changes

- `go vet` passes on all modified packages
- `golangci-lint` passes with zero issues
- Test files compile cleanly
- No behavioral change to existing test logic — all additions are diagnostic-only
- Verified diagnostic output in CI pipeline 113482429: `WaitForJobPodRunning` detected `ErrImagePull` immediately (no 30s timeout) and `DescribeJob` produced compact, scoped diagnostics showing only the relevant job pod

author: abacigil
body:
## Summary

Adds \`GET /api/v1/me\` — a universal endpoint that returns the authenticated \`UserPrincipal\` from the request context. Single source of truth for "who am I" surfaces (sidebar avatar, account menu, audit metadata for client-side actions) regardless of which auth backend is registered.

## Why

Today the enterprise dashboard's UserMenu reads identity from \`useSession()\` (NextAuth-only). In the cloud-enterprise tenant image, an admin who arrives via the cloud-SSO handoff has no NextAuth session — so the sidebar footer renders empty even though the API has the principal in hand. The previous attempt added a cloud-specific overlay route (\`/api/cloud-auth/me\`) plus a middleware bypass to make it reachable, which was a workaround layered on top of the \`/api/*\` proxy assumption.

The proper fix is to expose the principal as a normal API endpoint: every auth backend's middleware writes the principal into the request context, this handler reads it back. Same code path for NoAuth, OIDC, and the cloud-SSO chain.

## What changes

- \`services/api/internal/handler/me.go\` (new): tiny handler that reads from \`auth.FromContext\` and writes JSON. 401 when context holds no principal — defensive for chains where the route somehow gets mounted ahead of the auth middleware.
- \`services/api/internal/handler/me_test.go\` (new): 4 unit tests covering OIDC-shaped principal pass-through, NoAuth anonymous principal, missing-context 401, and the pathological \`WithUser(ctx, nil)\` branch.
- \`services/api/internal/server/server.go\`: mount \`GET /api/v1/me\` with \`viewer\` role (any authenticated user can ask).
- \`CHANGELOG.md\`: entry under \`### Added\`.

## Coordinated PRs

- decisionbox-io/decisionbox-enterprise fix/user-menu-via-api-me — switches \`UserMenu.tsx\` to fetch \`/api/v1/me\`.
- decisionbox-io/decisionbox-cloud-enterprise-tenant fix/cloud-sso-user-menu-cleanup — drops the now-redundant cloud-specific overlay routes; adds a middleware intercept that handles cloud-SSO sign-out via \`/api/auth/logout\`.

## Test plan

- [x] \`go test ./services/api/internal/handler/ -run TestMe\` — passes.
- [x] \`golangci-lint run ./services/api/internal/handler/...\` — clean.
- [x] \`go build ./services/api/...\` — clean.
- [ ] CI on this PR.
- [ ] After all 3 merge + image rebuild + tenant roll-forward — sidebar shows the user identity for both auth flows on tenant-ostest3.

author: rmcd-mscb
body:
## Summary

The aggregation driver enumerates every year in a source's files. For
monolithic single-file sources (mwbm_climgrid: 1895–2020 in one NC),
the fetch period is provenance-only and can't subset bytes, so without
an agg-time clip you get ~125 per-year files including the publisher's
1895–1899 spinup and everything outside the NHM run window. Add an
optional `--period` to `agg mwbm-climgrid` and an aligned `AGG_PERIODS`
array in the SLURM script, threading the value into the driver as a
`(year, file)` filter.

- New parameter: `aggregate_source(..., period: str | None = None)`.
  After `enumerate_years`, filter to `start_year <= y <= end_year`.
  Empty intersection raises a clear error including the source's
  actual covered range.
- `aggregate_mwbm_climgrid` and the `agg mwbm-climgrid` CLI both
  accept `period`. `_run_tier_agg` forwards it only when set, so
  other aggregators are unaffected.
- `agg_all.slurm` grows `AGG_PERIODS` parallel to `AGG_TASKS`;
  mwbm-climgrid (task 10) defaults to `1979/2020`. The script passes
  `--period` only for tasks with a non-empty entry.
- `docs/sources/mwbm_climgrid.md` updated with the new flag.

## Test plan

- [x] `pixi run -e dev fmt-check`
- [x] `pixi run -e dev lint`
- [x] `pixi run -e dev test` — 517 passed (was 515; two new tests
      cover the clip path and the exclude-everything error)
- [ ] On HPC: `sbatch --array=10 agg_all.slurm`; expect per-year files
      `mwbm_climgrid_1979_agg.nc`–`mwbm_climgrid_2020_agg.nc` only,
      and a log line `mwbm_climgrid: --period 1979/2020 clipped 125 → 42 years`.

author: alekspetrov
body:
## Summary

Automated PR created by Pilot for task GH-2415.

Closes #2415

## Changes

GitHub Issue #2415: fix(executor): send X-OpenCode-Directory header in attached mode

## Problem
When Pilot talks to an attached OpenCode server over HTTP, it creates sessions in the server process cwd instead of the target project path.

## Root Cause
OpenCode attached mode resolves the project directory from the `x-opencode-directory` header or `directory` query parameter, not from the legacy JSON `path` field in the `POST /session` body.

Verified against upstream OpenCode source:
- `packages/sdk/js/src/v2/client.ts`
- `packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/middleware.ts`

## Impact
Pilot can execute tasks against the wrong repository even though `ExecuteOptions.ProjectPath` is set correctly.

## Proposed Fix
Send `X-OpenCode-Directory: <urlencoded project path>` on both:
- `POST /session`
- `POST /session/:id/message`

Add regression coverage to assert the header is present on both requests.

Implemented high-impact backend performance optimizations:
1. **Zero-DB Cache Hit**: In `ShopPublicQueryService.getShopBySlug`, removed redundant database queries previously executed on Redis cache hits. This reduces DB queries from 2-3 to 0 for cached requests.
2. **Query Parallelization**: Parallelized independent Prisma queries for hotspot IDs and label keys in `ShopPublicQueryService` and `ProductService.getById`, reducing latency on cache misses.
3. **Cache Consistency**: Added eager cache invalidation in `ShopImageMapService` methods (`activateMap`, `saveLayout`) to ensure shop profiles and product lists are refreshed when hotspot configurations change.
4. **Verification**: Added `test/bolt-anti-pattern.spec.ts` to explicitly verify that hotspot queries are skipped on cache hits and parallelized on cache misses.
5. **BOLT Journal**: Recorded critical learnings regarding the 'Zero-DB Cache Hit Anti-Pattern' and sequential Prisma query bottlenecks.

### Motivation
- Allow long-range historical backfills (e.g., daily data back to 2015) by making the Yahoo Chart backfill interval configurable instead of hard-coding minute-based stepping. 
- Prevent unnecessary truncation of history by applying Yahoo intraday lookback clamping only to minute-based intervals.
- Ensure fetched timestamps align with the ingestion cadence so stored observations remain consistent with `interval_minutes`.

- Added support for a configurable `backfill_interval` read from `scrape.extra` and used as the Yahoo Chart `interval` parameter via `backfill_interval` and `_interval_to_timedelta` in `ingestion/adapters/tradingview.py`.

body:
## Summary
Track A4a of [docs/activemodel-privates-100-plan.md](../blob/main/docs/activemodel-privates-100-plan.md). Mirrors `ActiveModel::Validations::NumericalityValidator` (`numericality.rb`) coercion pipeline:

- `INTEGER_REGEX` (`/^[+-]?\d+(?![\s\S])/` — true `\z`-equivalent, rejects `"1\n"`) + `HEXADECIMAL_REGEX` constants — `numericality.rb:18-20`.
- `parseFloat(num, precision, scale)` — `numericality.rb:86-88`. `round(num, scale)` then `toPrecision`.
- `round(num, scale)` — delegates to activesupport `RoundingHelper` (half-away-from-zero, single source of truth in the repo).
- `isIsNumber(rawValue, precision, scale)` — `numericality.rb:94-100`. Honors `only_numeric`; restricts to `string|number` (Rails `Kernel.Float` raises `TypeError` on Date/boolean/objects); rejects blank, leading-whitespace hex, and `0b…`/`0o…` literals.
- `isIsInteger(rawValue)` — `numericality.rb:102-104`.
- `isIsHexadecimalLiteral(rawValue)` — `numericality.rb:106-108`. Anchored, no leading whitespace.
- `optionAsNumber(record, optionValue, precision, scale)` — `numericality.rb:67-69`. **Closes the `resolveValue` consumption gap** flagged for Numericality in PR #971. Anchored hex returns `undefined` (Rails skip semantic); `0b/0o` and trim-only-hex throw the consistent `Resolved numericality option must be numeric: …` error.

Privates attached to `NumericalityValidator.prototype` (not class fields) so they survive `EachValidator`'s super-time `checkValidity()` call — same bootstrapping pattern as PRs #994 / #1002 / #1009. `@internal` JSDoc tags satisfy `blazetrails/rails-private-jsdoc`. Names follow `extract-ts-api` conventions: `is_number?` → `isIsNumber`, etc. (the doubled `is` prefix is fixed in a follow-up PR — see Outstanding section below).

## Out of scope (Track A4b)
`filtered_options`, `allow_only_integer?`, `prepare_value_for_validation`, `record_attribute_changed_in_place?` — the dispatch-side helpers. Saved for the next PR.

## Impact
- `pnpm api:compare --privates --package activemodel`: `numericality.rb` 5/15 → **11/15 (73%)** (+6). Overall 471/607 → **477/607 (78.6%)**.
- `pnpm api:compare --package activemodel`: stays **433/433 (100%)**.
- `pnpm test:compare --package activemodel`: stays 959/963.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test:compare --package activemodel` — 959/963 (0)

## Outstanding Copilot feedback (max review cycles hit — flagged for human reviewer)

After **9 Copilot review rounds**, one comment remains unaddressed and is left to the human reviewer to adjudicate:

- **Round 9** — Asks for an explicit test asserting `isIsNumber` rejects `true` / `Date` / arbitrary objects (the new typeof-narrowing branch). Reasonable; would lock in the Rails-faithful no-coercion behavior. Skipped here only because the cycle ceiling was hit; recommend folding into the immediate follow-up PR (the api:compare conventions fix that renames `isIs*` → `is*`).

## Copilot review history (9 rounds, max ceiling)

Resolved across the prior rounds:
- **Round 1** (5 comments): thread `precision`/`scale` through `resolveNumeric`; banker's rounding (later corrected); strict `isIsNumber` blank/hex guards; `optionAsNumber` hex rejection; regression tests.
- **Round 2** (3): rescue raw `TypeError` on `Number()`; accurate `toPrecision` wording; `isIsNumber` try/catch matching Rails `rescue`.
- **Round 3** (3): `INTEGER_REGEX` strict end-of-string `(?![\s\S])`; restrict `isIsNumber` to string/number; `optionAsNumber` typeof guard.
- **Round 4** (1): `round()` realigned to half-away-from-zero matching the in-repo `rubyRound` (Ruby `Float#round` default is NOT banker's — new in-repo evidence).
- **Round 5** (2): reject JS binary/octal literal strings (`0b…` / `0o…`) plus regression tests.
- **Round 6** (2): hex compare options return `undefined` (Rails `parse_as_number` falls through), not throw; test updated to assert skip.
- **Round 7** (1): only `\A`-anchored hex skips silently; trim-only hex (`"  0x10"`) raises (matches Rails `Kernel.Float`).
- **Round 8** (2): reuse activesupport `RoundingHelper`; drop dead `try/catch`.
- **Round 9** (1): test for the new `string|number` narrowing in `isIsNumber` — deferred per max-cycle ceiling.

author: dylanmassaro
body:
## Summary
Two related fixes around `joinGame`'s auto-route path:

1. **Auto-route slot cap** — was hard-coded to `team-1..team-8` (24 max players). Now scales with `playerCap`: `maxSlots = max(8, ceil(playerCap/TEAM_CAP) + 5)`.
2. **M-05 team-size cap correctness** — moved `memberCount: increment(1)` and the `roleAssignments` write *inside* the transaction so the cap check actually holds under concurrent joins.

## Why

The 8-slot cap blocked any session over 24 players from using auto-route. That's the latent P0 #2 from the bug report.

The bigger find: while testing the cap fix, the M-05 team-size cap turned out to be **silently broken under concurrent joins on the same team**:

- Inside the txn: `if (memberCount >= TEAM_CAP) throw "team is full"` ✓
- Outside the txn (post-commit): `teamRef.update({ memberCount: increment(1) })`

So under load, N concurrent joiners all read `memberCount=0` at txn-read time, all pass the `< 3` check, all commit their player + roster docs, then all run the post-txn increment — landing the team at `memberCount=N` despite the cap. I observed it directly: a stress test of 70 concurrent auto-route joins put 57 players on `team-1` (memberCount 30+) before the system started erroring.

The matching comment claimed atomic-increment was used "for performance" — but the performance argument was about contention on `gameRef.totalPlayers` (one global doc, valid argument), not `teamRef.memberCount` (≤3 contending writers per team — well within transaction-friendly territory). Looks like a copy-paste from the totalPlayers path.

This patch:
- Moves the team-level `memberCount + roleAssignments` writes back inside the txn
- Keeps the `totalPlayers` increment outside (correct primitive there)
- Raises the auto-route slot cap to scale with `playerCap`

## Test plan
- [x] Backend mocha suite: 52 passing / 16 pending unchanged
- [x] Realistic FE flow (24 `createTeam` + 46 `joinGame` with explicit `teamId`, what `LandingPage` actually does): 70 players land in 24 teams, **0 overflow**, 0 failures, ~19s
- [ ] Manual: practice-run smoke with 25+ teams forming via the join UI

## Known limitation

Auto-route under 70-concurrent (no `teamId`/`teamNumber`, everyone racing the same `team-1`) still saturates because every player picks the same first slot. That's a fundamental property of the auto-route path — not a regression of this patch. Random slot allocation in the auto-router (`team-${rand}` instead of `team-${lowest-unused}`) would fan out the contention if a future flow exercises concurrent auto-route at scale; the realistic FE flow doesn't, so I left it out of this PR.

body:
## Summary

The \`WidgetAction\` types landed back in the framework scaffolding (\`WidgetAction\` record + \`WidgetActionTrigger\` + \`WidgetActionKind\` enums) but no runtime was dispatching them. This wires up the click-handler side: widget renderers call \`dispatch(action, rowData)\`, the framework substitutes \`\${row.x}\` / \`\${aliasName}\` placeholders, then forwards to the matching kind-specific handler.

Self-contained: no backend coordination needed.

## Surface

### Types

- \`WidgetActionDispatchContext\` — dispatch-time context (row data, resolved aliases, \`setView\` from the active dashboard view, resolved+substituted params).
- \`WidgetActionHandler\` — function signature per kind.
- \`WidgetActionHandlerRegistry\` — \`Record<WidgetActionKind, Handler>\`.

### Pure helpers

- \`composeWidgetActionHandlers(...registries)\` — last-wins composition (mirrors \`composeRegistries\` for renderers).
- \`expandActionPlaceholders(value, ctx)\` — substitutes \`\${row.x}\` + \`\${aliasName}\`. Unknown placeholders left verbatim.
- \`expandActionParams\` / \`expandActionTargetAndParams\` — bulk variants.

### Framework defaults

| Kind | Handler |
| --- | --- |
| \`Navigate\` | \`window.location.assign(target)\` + query string from params |
| \`OpenDashboardView\` | \`setView(target)\` via the surrounding view provider (no-op outside multi-view) |
| \`OpenDashboard\` | \`window.location.assign(\`/dashboards/\${name}\`)\` with query-string params |
| \`ExportData\` | emits \`granit:dashboard:export\` \`CustomEvent\` |
| \`OpenDetail\` | emits \`granit:dashboard:open-detail\` \`CustomEvent\` |

Apps replace per-kind handlers via \`composeWidgetActionHandlers\` — typical case is wiring \`Navigate\` to React Router (\`useNavigate()\`) and \`ExportData\` / \`OpenDetail\` to app-specific dialog hooks.

### Provider + hook

- \`<WidgetActionProvider handlers>\` — provides the registry. Falls back to framework defaults when not mounted (dispatcher works out of the box, with the trade-off of full-page \`Navigate\`).
- \`useWidgetActionDispatcher()\` — returns \`dispatch(action, data?)\`. Resolves placeholders against the dispatch context (row data + aliases from \`<DashboardAliasProvider>\`), routes to the registered handler, threads the view setter from \`<DashboardViewProvider>\`.
- \`useStableWidgetActionDispatcher()\` — same with a \`useMemo\` wrapper for memoisation boundaries.

## What's intentionally out of scope

- **Wiring widget renderers** (KpiTile / table rows / chart series / map markers) to dispatch their actions — that's per-renderer work landing alongside each widget kind's interaction polish.
- **Action chains / pre-action hooks** — apps compose middleware on top of the registry by wrapping handlers themselves.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm exec vitest run packages/@granit/react-dashboards\` — 16 files / 134 tests pass (17 new: placeholder substitution rules including row vs alias namespaces and unknown-placeholder leave-verbatim, dispatcher forwarding with substituted target/params/row, registry composition override semantics, ExportData/OpenDetail custom-event dispatch).
- [x] \`pnpm lint\` clean.
- [x] \`pnpm tsc\` clean across all 87 \`@granit/*\` packages.

## Summary

Adds an `includedActions` option to `PinGitHubActionsToSha` that, when supplied, restricts pinning to only the actions matching one of the patterns in the list. Pattern forms supported:

| Pattern | Matches |
|---|---|
| `owner/repo` | Exact `owner/repo`, with or without a subpath in the `uses:` |
| `owner/*` | Any repo in an org |
| `owner/repo/subpath` | Exact match including subpath |

When the allow list is non-empty, an explicit allow always wins — `pinOfficialActions` is bypassed for matched entries — so e.g. `actions/checkout` can be pinned via the allow list without globally flipping the official-actions flag. An omitted or empty list preserves today's default behavior.

- The base of this PR is the [pin-actions-to-sha](https://github.com/openrewrite/rewrite-github-actions/tree/pin-actions-to-sha) branch — intended to be folded into #169 before merging to `main`.

body:
## Summary

Consolidate read-time display-name fallback chains in the FactBase rendering layer. Three new helpers in `apps/web/src/components/factbase/entity-detail-shared.ts` replace ~22 duplicated `?? ?? ??` chains across 13 files.

This is **QUA-771 (Tier 6 of QUA-154)** — fixing the *read-time* duplication. Fixing the *underlying* missing-data problem at write-time is tracked in QUA-848 (validator) and follow-ups.

## What changed

| Helper | Replaces | Sites |
|---|---|---|
| `getRecordDisplayName(item)` | `field(item, "name") ?? titleCase(item.key)` | 9 |
| `getPersonRecordName(item, personEntity?)` | `personEntity?.name ?? item.displayName ?? field(item, "display_name") ?? titleCase(item.key)` | 3 |
| `getPropertyLabel(prop, propertyId)` | `prop?.name ?? titleCase(propertyId)` | 10 |

Files touched: `entity-detail-shared.ts` (+helpers, +import), `entity-collection-records.tsx`, `entity-person-cards.tsx`, `entity-fact-display.tsx`, `FBAutoFacts.tsx`, `FBCompareTable.tsx`, `FBCompareChart.tsx`, `FBEntityFacts.tsx`, `FBEntitySidebar.tsx`, `directory/FactsSection.tsx`, `organizations/[slug]/page.tsx`, `organizations/[slug]/main-content-sections.tsx`, `organizations/[slug]/_data/charts.ts`, `entity-detail-shared.test.ts` (new, 23 tests).

## Why

Per QUA-771: read-time fallback chains compensate for missing/null data at the read site rather than enforcing it at write-time. Symptoms are:

1. **Duplication** — same chain repeated across many components, hard to keep in sync
2. **Hidden bugs** — raw `sid_` IDs leaking when name resolution fails (cf. QUA-156, `validate-rendered-sid`)
3. **Unclear canonicality** — new contributors don't know which field is "the" name

Consolidating into helpers gives us:
- One place to refine the derivation logic
- One place to insert future write-time enforcement (e.g., once QUA-848 validator is blocking, the `titleCase(key)` branch in `getRecordDisplayName` becomes dead code that we can remove)
- Tests that lock in the contract

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run` — 1773 tests pass (incl. 23 new for the helpers)
- `pnpm build` — clean compile
- `pnpm crux w validate gate --fix` — 64/64 checks pass (3 pre-existing advisory warnings unrelated)
- Local Playwright render-audit (port 3014, my build) on 20 affected pages — all 20 pass
  - `/organizations/anthropic`, `/people/dario-amodei`, `/ai-models/claude-opus-4-5`, `/wiki/E815` (Anthropic), all directory indexes, OG-link checks, the QUA-418 dead-link checks — every one green

## Out of scope (sub-tickets)

- **QUA-847** — `entity?.title || pageData?.title || slug` fallback in `app/wiki/[id]/`. Wiki-page title resolver, separate from FactBase rendering.
- **QUA-848** — Validator for FactBase records missing `name`. The helper still falls back to `titleCase(key)` when records lack `name`; validator is Phase A of removing that branch.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm vitest run` — 1773 tests pass (incl. 23 new for the three helpers)
- [x] `pnpm build` — clean compile in 10.6s
- [x] `pnpm crux w validate gate --fix` — 64/64 checks pass (3 advisory warnings, all pre-existing)
- [x] `cd apps/web && PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3014 npx playwright test e2e/render-audit.spec.ts` — 20/20 affected pages pass on local build (incl. `/organizations/anthropic`, `/people/dario-amodei`, `/ai-models/claude-opus-4-5`, `/wiki/E815`)
- [x] Local smoke check on `/factbase/entity/anthropic` — funding rounds, products, model releases render with consolidated helpers; no JS errors; pre-existing `sid_` leak (also present on prod) tracked separately under QUA-848 follow-up
- [ ] CI green on this PR

Closes QUA-771.

author: copilot
body:
No single command existed to bring up the full Apex-Omega-v6 stack — Rust wheel build, Python deps, dashboard, and arbitrage bot all had to be wired together manually.

## What's added

### `start.sh` — full system boot in one command
```bash
./start.sh            # shadow mode by default (LIVE_EXECUTION=false)
./start.sh --dry-run  # forces LIVE_EXECUTION=false + APEX_SEND_TX=0
./start.sh --dashboard-only | --bot-only | --no-build
```

Execution order:
1. Load `python/apex_omega_core/.env` — shell vars win; `.env` keys validated against `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` to block injection
2. `pip install -r requirements.txt`
3. Build + install Rust/PyO3 wheel via `maturin==1.7.8` (pinned to match prod workflow)
4. Python module self-check (core + Rust extension)
5. Launch Flask dashboard on `127.0.0.1:5000` (override via `DASHBOARD_BIND`)
6. Launch arbitrage bot — `Ctrl+C` sends SIGTERM to all tracked processes

### `stop.sh` — graceful shutdown
Reads `.apex_pids` (written by `start.sh`) and sends SIGTERM to each tracked process.

## Security hardening
- `LIVE_EXECUTION` defaults to `false`; must be explicitly armed in `.env`
- Dashboard binds to `127.0.0.1` by default, not `0.0.0.0`
- `.env` key-name validation prevents shell injection via crafted config files
- `maturin` pinned (`==1.7.8`) — no floating install from PyPI
- Cleanup trap is idempotent (no double-fire on `EXIT` after signal)
- Process startup uses a retry loop (up to 10 s) rather than a fixed `sleep 2`
- Bot script existence verified before launch

author: rnagulapalle
body:
## What

Fixes #26794

When an MCP server is backed by an OpenAPI spec (`spec_path`), the `extra_headers` configuration is silently ignored. Only managed (SSE/HTTP transport) MCP servers correctly forward `extra_headers` from caller requests to the upstream API.

## Why

`extra_headers` is a list of header names (e.g. `["X-TOKEN"]`) that should be forwarded from the client request to the upstream API. For managed MCP servers, this works correctly via `_prepare_mcp_server_headers`. But for OpenAPI-backed servers, the dispatch path bypasses header forwarding entirely — there's no mechanism to carry per-request headers from the caller to the generated tool function.

## How

Added a new `ContextVar[Optional[Dict[str, str]]]` called `_request_extra_headers` in `openapi_to_mcp_generator.py` (same pattern as the existing `_request_auth_header`):

1. **`openapi_to_mcp_generator.py`** — added `_request_extra_headers` ContextVar; the generated tool function merges it into `effective_headers` before making the upstream request
2. **`server.py`** — in the local/OpenAPI tool dispatch branch, builds the extra headers dict from `raw_headers` using the server's configured `extra_headers` list, and sets the ContextVar before calling the tool handler
3. **`mcp_server_manager.py`** — in `_call_openapi_tool_handler`, sets the ContextVar with forwarded headers and removes the warning about headers being unsupported for OpenAPI servers

Uses the same header normalization pattern as `_call_regular_mcp_tool` and `_prepare_mcp_server_headers` for consistency.

## Changes

- `openapi_to_mcp_generator.py` — new ContextVar + merge in tool function
- `server.py` — build and set extra headers in local tool dispatch
- `mcp_server_manager.py` — forward headers in OpenAPI tool handler, remove unsupported warning

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

author: bin-ario
body:
## Summary

Adds a `health-checks` input that takes one JSON object per line so callers can poll multiple endpoints on the same container before it's torn down.

## Motivation

The action's `always()` step does `docker rm -f`. That means a calling workflow can't add a follow-up `curl` step for a second endpoint — by the time control returns to the workflow, the container is gone. Today the only way to poll multiple endpoints is to call the action twice (rebuilding + rerunning the container) or to give up and skip the second check.

Concrete case: `getgather`'s `container.yml` polls both `/health` and `/extended-health`. After migrating to `container-health-check@v1`, the inline `/extended-health` step would race the cleanup and fail.

## Design

```yaml
- uses: remotebrowser/shared-github-actions/container-health-check@v1
  with:
    image-name: getgather
    health-checks: |
      {"url": "http://localhost:23456/health"}
      {"url": "http://localhost:23456/extended-health", "match": "ready"}
    health-timeout-seconds: 180
```

- One JSON object per line: `{"url": "...", "match": "..."}`. `match` defaults to `"OK"`.
- Blank lines ignored. Malformed JSON fails fast with `jq`'s parse error.
- Checks run sequentially against the same container, each gets the full `health-timeout-seconds` budget.
- Wins over `health-url`/`health-match` when both are set.
- `health-url` becomes optional; the action validates that one of the two is set.

## Compatibility

- `health-url` callers: unchanged behavior.
- `health-url` is now `required: false` in the action manifest. Anyone who relied on schema-level enforcement will get a runtime error instead — same outcome, different layer.

## Release

Once merged, tag `v1.5.0` and move the floating `v1` tag.
